News.title: UK sees hottest day of the year as 38.1C recorded in Kew Gardens
News.content:
The UK has experienced its hottest day of the year and fifth hottest day on record, as a heatwave that gripped much of the country peaked at 38.1C on Thursday, the Met Office said.

Kew Gardens in west London recorded England's top temperature, provisionally surpassing the 38C recorded in Lingwood, Norfolk on 26 June.

The latest spell of extreme heat marks the UK's fifth heatwave this year, with the Met Office warning this summer is on course to be the UK's hottest since records began.

An amber heat health alert, warning of significant detrimental impacts to health and social care services is in place across the whole of England until 21:00 BST on Friday.

News.title: Five key takeaways from results day 2026
News.content:
Results for A-levels, T-levels, BTecs and other vocational qualifications are out.

And this year, they've come at a time when all eyes are on what teenagers decide to do next.

Universities are keen to get them through the door. As they grapple with their finances, they know that every filled seat in a lecture hall comes with tuition fee funding.

The new prime minister, meanwhile, wants to carve out clear routes into technical jobs that can rival the well-established path of A-levels and a university degree.

For teenagers, considerations about the immediate and long-term cost of university, as well as the availability of other options, are all in the mix.

Here are the standout things you need to know.

News.title: Son pays tribute to dad, 102, who died after allegedly being assaulted in pub
News.content:
The son of a 102-year-old great-grandfather who died after allegedly being assaulted at a south Wales pub says he was a "pub character".

Phillip Ormerod, from Cwmbran, Torfaen, was taken to hospital in a critical condition following the incident at the Crow's Nest pub in the town on 1 August.

Gwent Police confirmed on Thursday that he had since died.

A 56-year-old man from Llanelli, Carmarthenshire, was arrested on suspicion of inflicting grievous bodily harm, and remains under investigation.

Ormerod's son, Robert Ormerod, said his dad had been diagnosed with dementia and was a widower who lived alone.

News.title: The key signs you may have damaged your eyes by looking at the eclipse
News.content:
Eye experts are warning people to be on the alert for any signs their vision has been damaged by looking at the sun during Wednesday's eclipse.

The symptoms can include blurred vision, a central blind or dark spot and increased sensitivity to light.

After the previous total eclipse of the sun that was visible in the UK in 1999, around 70 people were left with damaged sight.

Many of them had spent less than a minute looking at the spectacle, without realising they were harming their eyes.

The danger comes because staring at an eclipse without protection can damage the retina, which sits at the back of the eye, and particularly those cells responsible for sharp central vision.

The sun is incredibly bright, even when partially obscured by the moon.

Normally if we stare at it, we wince and quickly look away.

But when it is darker, during an eclipse, that instinct may not kick in, even while our eyes are being damaged.

The bright light and ultraviolet radiation given off by the sun can lead to a condition known as "solar retinopathy".

And because the retina has no pain receptors, it's hard for people to notice the damage as it happens, so symptoms may only appear several hours later.

Leading up to the eclipse itself, experts were warning only genuine specially-designed solar eclipse glasses should be used, and that ordinary sunglasses or other devices were not enough to prevent potential damage.

News.title: Honeytrap thieves jailed for killing men they had drugged
News.content:
A couple who drugged men seeking sexual services in order to steal from them have been jailed for killing two men and poisoning others.

Adina Mihai and Madalin Dumitru admitted the manslaughter of Gary Mouat, 37, from Oxfordshire, and Malcolm King, 80, from Gloucestershire, in 2025 and 2024 respectively.

The pair also each admitted two further counts of administering poison to surviving victims on the first day of their trial in June.

Mihai, 31, and Dumitru, 30, were both sentenced to 17 years in prison at Oxford Crown Court.

Mihai, who posed as a sex worker, and her partner Dumitru, arranged to meet men paying for services she had advertised online at their homes.

The court heard four had their alcoholic drinks spiked with the powerful sedative gamma-butyrolactone (GBL) so the pair could steal from them.

Two men died as a result, while two others - who cannot be named due to reporting restrictions - survived.

News.title: Voting under way in Clacton by-election
News.content:
Voting is under way in the Clacton by-election as a record number of candidates vie to become its next MP.

Fifty-one polling stations in the Essex resort, which includes the towns of Jaywick, Frinton and Walton-on-the-Naze, opened at 07:00 BST and will shut at 22:00.

An electorate of 79,785 registered voters have the chance to vote for one of 34 candidates - the most ever to stand in a British election.

Voters will need to show a form of acceptable ID - such as a driving licence or passport - to be able to cast their ballot.

They will receive the longest ballot paper in British electoral history at 90cm - about 3ft long - to choose their candidate and cast their vote.

There are 12 political parties and 20 independents standing.

The constituency also has rural villages including St Osyth, Weeley and Great Bentley.

Polling stations will remain open to anyone registered to vote until 22:00, with the count taking place overnight.

News.title: Bonnie Tyler's classic hit spiked in streams during solar eclipse
News.content:
Born Gaynor Hopkins in a council house in Neath, Tyler grew up with a love for music before she was discovered by talent scout Roger Bell in a Swansea club.

Tyler released her first single, Lost in France in 1977, but it was the release of Total Eclipse of the Heart five years later which changed her life.

The ballad spent two weeks at UK number one and four weeks in the US.

The iconic love song's music video surpassed 1.2 billion views on YouTube and has had over a billion streams on Spotify.

Spotify previously said it had paid out more than $1.4 million for streams of Tyler's catalogue in 2025.

The music platform said Total Eclipse of the Heart was one of a few "celestial" songs that saw a streaming spike in the UK on 12 August.

According to Spotify, the biggest increases in UK streams during the eclipse were:

Evolfo, Moon Eclipsed the Sun (+12,817%)

Chris Staples, Dark Side of the Moon (+2,805%)

Pink Floyd, Eclipse (+594%)

Delta Goodrem, Eclipse (+104%)

Bonnie Tyler, Total Eclipse of the Heart (+94%)

Bill Withers, Ain't No Sunshine (+17%)

Ahead of the solar eclipse, Tyler's McVitie's Jaffa Cakes TV advert also resurfaced - it was originally broadcast in 2023 when there was a partial lunar eclipse.

The nostalgic advert came after research revealed almost half (49%) of Brits did not understand how eclipses occurred.

In the video, Tyler uses a Jaffa Cake as a prop to describe the different types of eclipse.

She said: "There are three types of eclipse. You've got the lunar eclipse, the solar eclipse, and then there's the total eclipse of the heart.

"When the earth is situated between the moon and the sun it creates a shadow, and when it looks like someone has just taken a bite out of the moon. That's a partial lunar eclipse."

The grammy-nominated star had a string of other hits, including Holding out for a Hero and also represented the UK at the Eurovision Song Contest in 2013.

She was named in the Queen's last Birthday Honours list in 2022 and was awarded an MBE for her services to music by Prince William the following year.

Tyler died "unexpectedly" on 8 July, aged 75, at a Portugal hospital, "as a result of the illness that she was being treated for", her family said in a statement released on the star's official website, external.

At the time, tributes poured in from a host of friends and stars including Catherine Zeta-Jones, Bryan Adams and Rod Stewart.

Tyler's funeral service will take place on 17 August at 12:00 BST at St Mary's Church in Swansea.

It has since been confirmed that her coffin will be brought to her Mumbles home on 15 August at 15:30 BST.

People are invited to "pay their respects" by lining Newton Road at 15:15 BST.

News.title: 'I worked really hard and it paid off': Elation, nerves and proud parents as students get results
News.content:
"I've worked really hard, I've tried and that's all I can doâ¦ and it's paid off", Emily, a student in Hartlepool said as she received her A-level results, admitting she "felt a bit sick" before finding out her grades.

She was just one of hundreds of thousands of young people to receive their A-level, Btec and T-level results across England, Wales and Northern Ireland on Thursday after weeks of waiting.

This year saw a record number of 18-year-olds accepted into university, with more than ever getting into their firm choice - although there are more of them in the population than in previous years.

Nervous, elated and tired students flocked to schools across the UK on Thursday to find out their grades, with many telling the BBC how they did and their hopes for the future.

Emily, who attended English Martyrs School and Sixth Form College, said she felt "sick" waking up on Thursday morning, but was happy with with her A*, A and B.

She said she's now looking forward to starting a degree apprenticeship to become a solicitor, a route she picked for the experience "now it's harder to get a job".

News.title: Dad to stand trial accused of murdering daughter Minnie Merriman
News.content:
The father of a nine-year-old girl who died after being found seriously injured at an industrial estate in Arbroath is to stand trial accused of her murder.

Prosecutors allege Christopher Rice, from Wakefield, West Yorkshire, killed Minnie Merriman, who died in Dundee's Ninewells Hospital on 3 August.

The 35-year-old, who was remanded in custody, made no plea during a second appearance in private via videolink at Forfar Sheriff Court. He was fully committed for trial.

Minnie's family previously paid tribute to their "beloved, absolutely incredible, beautiful and brave Minnie Moo".

Emergency services were called to the Elliot Industrial Estate in Arbroath shortly after midnight on 3 August following reports that a child had been found injured.

Minnie was taken to Ninewells Hospital alongside four other people, but later died as a result of her injuries.

Police Scotland said they were not looking for anyone else in connection with Minnie's death and the other members of the family - who were camping in the area - are being supported by specialist officers.

News.title: Bishop appears in court over child rape charges
News.content:
A 70-year-old bishop has appeared in court for the first time accused of two counts of rape against a female under the age of 16.

David Oakley, the Bishop of Northampton, was charged in June following an investigation by Staffordshire Police.

He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court via videolink from his lawyer's office.

Oakley was not asked to enter a plea during the hearing as Chief Magistrate Paul Goldspring sent the case to the Old Bailey.

Oakley was released on bail, with conditions not to contact the alleged victim, or her family, ahead of a plea hearing on 10 September.

The incidents allegedly took place in Staffordshire between February 2000 and February 2001, when Oakley was in his mid-40s working as a Catholic priest.

Oakley was born in Stourbridge, West Midlands, and ordained as a priest in 1980 before becoming Bishop of Northampton in 2020.

Oakley retains the title of Bishop but has withdrawn from public ministry.

The Catholic Diocese of Northampton - which covers Northamptonshire, Bedfordshire and Buckinghamshire â said in a previous statement that it recognised the case was "very distressing for all concerned".

News.title: Human bones found in south-east London garden
News.content:
Human bones found in the garden of a bungalow in south-east London are being examined by the Met Police.

Officers were called to Aperfield Road in Biggin Hill at about 15:30 BST last Friday, the force said.

The bones were sent for specialist examination which confirmed they were human. They are now undergoing further tests to establish their age and identity, police added.

The area around the home was cordoned off for six days, according to The Sun, external, with one resident telling the newspaper the property was being renovated.

"The builders discovered something on Friday and of course they completely had to stop work," they added.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson added: "The crime scene is now closed and an investigation remains ongoing to establish the full circumstances."

News.title: Harvey Nichols bought by owner of Sports Direct
News.content:
Luxury department store Harvey Nichols has been bought by the owner of Sports Direct, which warned a "significant restructuring" was needed to ensure the 200-year-old business remains sustainable.

Mike Ashley's Frasers Group will take control of the Harvey Nichols stores, including its flagship in Knightsbridge, as well as the international franchise.

The department store was immortalised in BBC sitcom Absolutely Fabulous, but had faced challenges in recent years. The firm had appointed administrators in June.

Michael Murray, Frasers' chief executive and Ashley's son-in-law, called the store a "British institution with significant potential" but added "clear meaningful change is needed".

"The turnaround will require tough choices and we are prepared to make those decisions, even if that means a smaller business in the near term, to create a stronger and more sustainable Harvey Nichols for the long-term," he said.

Harvey Nichols carries more than 800 premium and luxury brands and has over 1,000 employees. Its other stores are located in Manchester, Birmingham, Bristol, Leeds and Edinburgh.

Frasers Group will also acquire the online business, and shops will continue to operate under their existing licensing.

Earlier this week, Harvey Nichols warned in its latest accounts that it would need to "cease trading" within a year if it failed to secure new investment.

It had faced "sustained trading and operational challenges" recently and Frasers Group said it will need to conduct a review of the store's portfolio, structure and cost base.

A recent auction for the store saw Frasers battle retail rival Next to take control of the firm.

Harvey Nichols was bought in 1991 by Hong Kong-based businessman Sir Dickson Poon but he put the group up for sale earlier this year.

News.title: Ski Sunday host Chemmy Alcott suffers collapsed lung after jumping into lake
News.content:
Ski Sunday presenter Chemmy Alcott says she suffered a collapsed lung after jumping into a lake while on holiday in France.

The 44-year-old former GB Olympic skier posted a clip on Instagram, external that showed her jumping off a five metre platform into Lake Annecy, in the French Alps, before landing badly and ending up in hospital.

"Most people badly time a front flip off a five-metre platform and get winded," she said in the clip.

"I apparently don't do things by halves. Collapsed lung, chest drain and a very expensive lesson in rotation."

Alcott explained that she initially went back to jump again after her difficult landing, out of "embarassment" and "just so I wasn't making a big deal out of it".

But she soon realised she "couldn't breathe properly and should probably go and get it checked out".

She later shared images of herself in hospital with tubes and wires sticking out of her body.

In the caption to the main clip - titled "this didn't end well" - she wrote: "Well... that escalated quickly. Turns out five metres is quite a long way to discover you've got the rotation wrong.

"One badly timed front flip. One very hard landing. One collapsed lung. One chest drain. And a few more hospital overnights than were on the holiday itinerary...

"I absolutely loved Annecyâ¦ but I'm not entirely sure it loved me back."

A collapsed lung - medically known as a pneumothorax - occurs when air becomes trapped in the space between the lung and the chest wall, according the NHS.

News.title: Met chief accepts mistakes made over Simon Levy but defends investigation into murders
News.content:
The head of the Metropolitan Police Sir Mark Rowley has defended the force's investigation into double murderer Simon Levy.

Levy was on bail and being monitored by police when he murdered Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo in March 2025 and Sheryl Wilkins five months later, as well as violently raping a third woman.

Sir Mark acknowledged mistakes over the force's handling of Levy, but said suggestions it had not tried to build a case over his first murder were "just not true", following criticism including from Labour MP Jess Phillips.

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that detectives had done "serious" work but "didn't have enough evidence" for a charge.

The Met did not seek a charging decision from the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) over Valencia-Trujillo's murder until after Wilkins had been killed.

The police and CPS has apologised over a series of decisions that left the convicted sex offender free to attack the women.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is currently examining how Levy, 40, was managed over the four-year period from his first conviction in September 2021 for sexual assault up to his final arrest in September 2025.

At the Old Bailey on Wednesday, he was given a whole life prison sentence, meaning he will never be released.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Sir Mark - who on Wednesday called the case a "whole system failing" - said he had already apologised for what the Met had got wrong.

It emerged after Levy's conviction that the Met did not class Valencia-Trujillo's death in March 2025 as a murder, or pass the case to specialist homicide detectives, until after he had killed again.

Sir Mark said "the public debate needs to be better informed" because "the facts on that are much more complex than people want to acknowledge".

He said that while Valencia-Trujillo's death was "clearly very suspicious and concerning", a pathologist was unable to determine a cause of death and the force "didn't have enough evidence to get to a charge".

Sir Mark added it was only after the murder of Wilkins that the Met had the "combined evidence" to move forward.

"So the inference that the Met didn't try on that case is just not true, the Met tried," he said.

However, the Met did not ask the CPS for advice about Valencia-Trujillo's death, let alone a charging decision, until after the murder of Wilkins, the BBC has previously reported.

The fact there was no formal cause of death would not have prevented the case being taken on by specialist homicide detectives, who are skilled at building murder cases even when there is not a formal cause of death.

Levy's semen was on Valencia-Trujillo and his blood was at the murder scene. CCTV that showed Levy in the area, walking in the same direction as Valencia-Trujillo shortly after she passed a camera, was not viewed by the local team despite being gathered.

Other possible relevant CCTV was never gathered, and had been deleted by the time the specialist murder team took over months later.

In that case, the local team investigating the death did not engage with the Met's specialist murder teams apart from the day her body was discovered in March 2025.

A specialist homicide team attended the crime scene that day and recommended the case stay with local officers pending further enquiries, but there was no further contact until after Wilkins was murdered in August.

News.title: Heatwaves drive A&E attendances up to record high
News.content:
England's A&Es are experiencing their busiest period ever, with the record-breaking heat cited as a key factor.

More than 2.4 million patients attended emergency departments each month for May, June and July â the three highest monthly totals recorded in history.

NHS bosses say the pressure has been as bad as it is in winter months. The extreme heat has caused people to fall ill with dehydration and heatstroke, and has increased the risk of complications for those with heart, kidney and respiratory problems.

It comes as unions warn staff are being forced to work in inhumane conditions because of the heat, with reports of some collapsing and others having seizures.

The problems have been further complicated by equipment, including scanners and IT systems, breaking down.

Alongside A&Es, ambulance services have been reporting significant pressures.

The June heatwave pushed demand on the London Ambulance Service beyond levels seen during the peak of the Covid-19 pandemic.

NHS medical director Prof Frankie Swords praised the "outstanding professionalism" of staff and said the situation was making delivering care challenging.

She advised: "With temperatures peaking today, please take sensible precautions to stay safe - keep hydrated, avoid the sun during the hottest part of the day, especially if you are clinically vulnerable, and check in on older or vulnerable friends, relatives and neighbours."

News.title: Boy suffered fatal brain injury in seaside drowning
News.content:
A seven-year-old boy suffered a fatal brain injury after he got into difficulty off the Essex coast, a coroner has said.

Musa Ahmed died six days after the incident in West Mersea, in which his 15-year-old cousin, Sameeha Rahman, and her mother, Shelina, 41, also died.

They were all enjoying a day out to the island, near Colchester, from east London when the tragedy unfolded on 22 July.

Their provisional causes of death were all given as drowning at an inquest opening in Chelmsford, while Musa also died from a hypoxic ischaemic brain injury.

"Clearly it is so tragic to come across the death of any individual," said Lincoln Brookes, the senior coroner for Essex.

"But when three occur at the same time and all from the same family, one cannot understand the tragic nature of such an incident."

Three others were taken to hospital by ambulance after the incident and are said to be recovering.

Multiple houses are on fire and people have been evacuated from their homes following an “extensive” fire in Stourbridge, West Midlands Fire Service said.

The blaze, which left two casualties affected by the heat and smoke, is impacting six properties, the service added.

Care home residents have also been evacuated alongside others as a result of the fire, Wollaston & Stourbridge Town councillor Andrew Southall said.

Around 60 firefighters attended the scene near Stourbridge golf course after being alerted to the blaze at around 1.30pm, with the fire service saying that more resources were added throughout the afternoon.

open image in gallery Around 60 firefighters are tackling an extensive grass fire near Stourbridge golf course ( ITV )

West Midlands Fire Service reported "extreme levels of demand" after homes were threatened by the major blazes.

The grass fire follows scorching temperatures across the region and other parts of the UK.

Drone video shared by the service showed a thermal map of flames threatening nearby homes as heavy smoke drifted over the town.

open image in gallery A heat map of flames in the Stourbridge area ( PA )

Stourbridge town hall has now opened as a rescue centre for displaced residents.

In a statement on its incidents page, West Midlands Fire Service said: “Around 60 firefighters are tackling an extensive grass fire near Stourbridge golf course, in the Racecourse Lane area.

“We were first alerted to it just before 1.30pm on Thursday.

“Flames are spreading across roads in places. Please avoid the area.

open image in gallery Drone video shared by the service showed a thermal map of flames threatening nearby homes as heavy smoke drifted over the town ( WMFS )

“If smoke is affecting your home or workplace, keep doors and windows closed as a precaution.”

The fire service added that flames were spreading “across roads in places”, with people urged to stay indoors.

The M6 northbound near Birmingham has been closed between junction 5 and 6 as a result of smoke from nearby wildfires, with delays of up to two hours.

Junction 5 is the Castle Bromwich Interchange and junction 6 is Gravelly Hill, also known as Spaghetti Junction.

“Thick smoke is blowing across the carriageway; closures have been implemented for safety reasons,” National Highways West Midlands said.

open image in gallery People have been urged to avoid the area ( BBC )

“Southbound carriageway remains open at this time, however reduced speeds are in place.”

In an update, the highways agency said: “The fire keeps igniting. Fire commander at the scene not happy for M6 to reopened until fire fully extinguished.

“Delays building, 120 mins and 5 miles of congestion.”

Meanwhile, Warwickshire Fire and Rescue Service said they are responding to a “large fire” in Salford Priors, Stratford-on-Avon. It urged residents in the area to close all doors and windows.

Police, fire crews and ambulances are at the scene of the wildfire which has been declared a major incident.

Warwickshire Fire and Rescue Service were called at 2.30pm on Thursday to reports of a large plume of smoke on Tothall Lane, Salford Priors in Stratford-on-Avon.

The fire service said: “On arrival crews discovered a wildfire which was spreading to nearby out-buildings.

“There are currently 10 appliances in attendance. This incident has been declared a major incident.

“We would like to express that there is a large emergency presence in the area and we continue to advise residents nearby to close all doors and windows.

“Please stay away from the area. Our control room is receiving a large number of calls, so please contact us only in a genuine emergency.

“It’s imperative that residents take all steps to reduce any fire risk. Please read advice on our social media channels about fire and water safety.

“West Midlands Ambulance Service and Warwickshire Police are also on scene.”

More to follow...

The military is reportedly preparing to send a new aircraft carrier to the Middle East to replace the issue-plagued USS Abraham Lincoln, which has carried out a lengthy and high-stakes deployment as part of the Iran war.

The USS George Washington will take the Lincoln’s place, U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal. The switch is reportedly part of a previously planned rotation.

The Navy has said it is not publicly discussing plans for the carriers because of operational security concerns.

The swap comes after sailors and their families have alleged issues on the Lincoln including food shortages, months at sea without interruption and deteriorating mental health.

The George Washington and an accompanying carrier strike group were in the Strait of Malacca in Southeast Asia on Thursday, USNI News reports.

open image in gallery The military is reportedly preparing to send a new aircraft carrier to the Middle East to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln, after the ship faced complaints of food shortages and a brewing mental health crisis onboard during its lengthy deployment in the Iran war ( Reuters )

The Lincoln set sail in November and has gone a record-setting 200 days without making a port call, according to Sen. Richard Blumenthal. Aircraft carrier crews typically visit ports roughly once every one or two months.

“There have been widespread reports of shortages of basic supplies, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns, and disruptions in the mail system, which have caused many care packages in route to the ship to be lost in transit for months,” Blumenthal wrote in a letter on Wednesday to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao.

Multiple sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln have attempted to go overboard, their families told MilitaryTimes.

Secretary Hegseth said Thursday conditions on the ship had been “completely misrepresented.”

"We make sure every ship, every crew, every captain has everything we can provide them at every single moment,” he told reporters during a trip to Panama. “Some deployments are longer than others, and I have more respect and gratitude for those sailors than anybody. What they do in those high seas in those austere conditions with less port calls - it's incredible.”

Family members reportedly confronted Secretary Cao earlier this month at a contentious meeting in San Diego about conditions on the carrier.

The military said Wednesday it had “not identified an increase in reported suicidal ideation or suicide attempts aboard the ship.”

open image in gallery The aircraft carrier swap is reportedly part of a previously planned rotation ( Reuters )

“Navy leadership is listening to our families, supporting our service members, and ensuring the Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group has the resources needed to safely and successfully accomplish its mission,” a Navy official told USNI News on Wednesday.

Rep. Marlin Stutzman of Indiana has said he will seek a report from the Pentagon about conditions on the ship and what is being done to address them.

“At the end of the day, we know that those who are serving have to have comfort knowing that they’re getting properly taken care of,” he told CNN.

In addition to the USS Abraham Lincoln, the USS George H.W. Bush is deployed in the region as part of the Iran conflict.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the US, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

Rory McIlroy made a run of costly late bogeys as he slipped to a four-over par opening round at the FedEx St Jude Championship in Memphis.

The Northern Irishman had been aiming to rebuild some momentum heading into the PGA Tour Play-offs, following a run of disappointing results after his successful defence of his Masters title in April – which included tied for 40th at The Open at Royal Birkdale.

McIlroy, currently 12th in the FedExCup standings, was in a marquee pairing at TPC Southwind alongside world number one Scottie Scheffler on his return to the event he skipped last year.

open image in gallery Rory McIlroy found the water at the 18th (George Walker IV/AP) ( AP )

A bogey on the par-five third was soon recovered with a birdie at the par-three fourth, before another dropped shot at the eighth saw him head into the turn at one-over.

McIlroy sank a 15-foot birdie putt on the 11th, but a wayward tee shot off the 16th out to the right saw him make another bogey. His second at the 17th then bounced away past the green towards the stands, meaning a drop before eventually taking five.

There proved little relief on the 18th as McIlroy sent his tee shot into the water and then came up short in his approach, meaning a double bogey and a round of 74.

open image in gallery Scottie Scheffler made a solid start on his return to action in Memphis (George Walker IV/AP) ( AP )

Scheffler, returning to action for the first time since finishing runner-up at the 3M Open, finished at two under, his only bogey coming on the 15th.

“I felt like I hit a lot of quality shots with my irons,” he said. “I did a good job of being patient and not trying to force it too much.

“I feel like I was right on the edge of having a good day, so I felt like patience-wise, I did a pretty good job.”

American duo Michael Thorbjornsen and Jordan Spieth set the early clubhouse lead at five under. England’s Tommy Fleetwood was a shot back after his 66, which included an eagle at the third.

Scotland’s Robert MacIntyre, though, had an opening round to forget, finishing at 12 over with four double bogeys.

American cancer patients are facing longer surgery wait times today than over the past few decades - with dangerous consequences.

Wait times have increased from weeks to over a month for six types of common cancer, a new study of more than 2.7 million patients found.

Those cancers include breast, colon, lung, pancreatic, gastric and esophageal cancer, medical researchers said this week. The patients had stage 1 to 3 cancers - the only stages considered eligible for surgery at diagnosis.

“What was striking was the consistency,” Tim Donahue, the senior author on the study and a surgical oncologist at the University of California, Los Angeles, told STAT. “Across every cancer we studied, patients are waiting longer today than they were a decade ago.”

open image in gallery Cancer patients in the US are facing longer wait times for life-saving surgeries. That’s dangerous, according to experts ( Getty )

For people with breast cancer, wait times increase from 34 days to 45 days, gastric cancer waits rose from 35 to 49 days and those with colon cancer waited for between 20 to 31 days.

Where patients were treated and other factors dictated whether or not they were impacted by longer wait times. For example, the biggest waits were seen at large academic health centers, but Black Americans, people who were uninsured or on Medicare and patients who sought out treatment in America’s West were disproportionately affected.

The study’s authors also suggest there are multiple reasons for these delays.

Staffing challenges and limited resources within the facilities are one. So is an increasing number of referrals from urgent care facilities and the increasing complexity of modern cancer care, including robotic surgeries.

Notably, the study included surgeries conducted during the Covid-19 pandemic - using records from the National Cancer Database from 2012-2023 - when some cancer surgeries were pushed back.

But the researchers said they also saw the “noticeable increase” in waiting times post-Covid.

open image in gallery While there was a delay in cancer surgeries during the Covid-19 pandemic, the researchers said there was also a ‘noticeable increase’ after the pandemic ( AFP/Getty )

These findings are concerning because longer wait times can raise the risk of disease spread and premature death, according to experts.

Every month delayed in cancer treatment can raise the risk of death by around 10 percent, a past study from U.K. and Canada researchers showed. For every 30-day delay from the time of diagnosis, the risk of death increased by 4.6 percent, another study from The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center determined.

“Many things are completely out of the medical team’s control when caring for patients with head and neck cancer, but time to surgery is something we can immediately modify,” head and neck cancer surgeon Dr. Stephen Kang said in a statement alongside the study’s findings.

An estimated 626,140 people in the United States will die from cancer in 2026, according to the American Cancer Society. There will be over 2.1 million new cases.

A Massachusetts police officer who lost half his family in a devastating Airbnb fire is no longer able to work and remains haunted by his late wife’s cries for help as she and the couple’s 1-year-old daughter struggled in vain to escape the flames, according to a federal lawsuit reviewed by The Independent.

John Hubbard IV, 40, “will never be able to recover from hearing his wife through a trapped door while their lives ended in flames and smoke,” the former patrolman’s complaint states. The couple’s 3-year-old son survived the October 13, 2024 inferno, but, the filing contends, “his own young personality and love for life will be forever changed.”

It claims the homeowners – who were later arrested and accused of manslaughter – falsely advertised the Upstate New York rental as being equipped with smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. However, they never installed the devices in order “to save a buck,” the complaint contends, blaming the tragedy on the pair’s “inattentiveness, hastiness, deceptiveness and willingness to prioritize short-cuts over the safety of the occupants of the premises.”

Hubbard’s lawsuit names Airbnb and others as defendants.

The fateful choice by Airbnb hosts Dennis and Meredith Darcy “catastrophically broke the Hubbard Family,” according to the complaint.

Hubbard, who served as a police officer for more than 15 years, was subsequently forced to retire so he could focus on his “new responsibilities as a single parent,” the complaint says.

Attorney Eric Green, who is representing Hubbard, told The Independent that Hubbard and his son “continue to undergo therapy” in an attempt to deal with what happened.

“It’s something that doesn’t go away,” he said.

open image in gallery John Hubbard (right) is suing Airbnb after losing half his family in a house fire while they were in New York ( Nantucket Police )

Co-counsel Shawn Green said he finds it especially troubling that the Hubbards “did their research, but the listing was misrepresented and false.”

“It said it had smoke detectors, when it did not,” he said, arguing the home was “not compliant with local laws and was in a completely unsafe condition.”

The Independent has reached out to Airbnb for comment. The company says it “strongly urges” hosts to install smoke detectors in their home, and provides them free of charge to eligible homeowners.

Hubbard and his wife Shannon, along with their kids Jack and Maggie, were spending the weekend at an Airbnb in the quaint Dutchess County town of Salt Point to enjoy the fall foliage and visit relatives, according to the complaint, which was filed August 12 in Manhattan federal court.

The pair were relaxing on the patio of the 4-bed, 2.5-bath home when John, a patrolman in Nantucket before joining the Dennis Police Department, and Shannon, a pre-school teacher for kids with special needs, smelled smoke.

Hubbard quickly dialed 911 as Shannon ran inside. The New York State Police, the East Clinton Fire Department and the Dutchess County Fire Investigation Division responded, discovering Shannon and the children on the second floor of the home, according to an official news release issued several months later.

The four family members were taken to area hospitals, where Shannon and Maggie were pronounced dead.

Investigators determined that the fatal blaze had originated in the chimney flue and had not been intentionally set. At the same time, a State Police probe found that the property lacked required permits and “was not properly equipped with functional smoke detectors.” The Dutchess County DA’s office went even further, saying the Darcys “deliberately ignored the significant and unjustifiable risk of death” by not installing the detectors.

open image in gallery The fire-damaged home in Salt Point, New York, where Shannon and Maggie Hubbard died in a blaze on October 13, 2024 ( Google Maps )

An attorney for the Darcys said at the time they were “devastated” over what had happened, but that they had “a stark difference of opinion” with the district attorney over the manslaughter charges.

Yet, according to the complaint, the two chose to “line their pockets without any regard for the safety of the Hubbard family.” In addition to the home lacking any smoke detectors, the residence had not been inspected, did not have a valid rental permit, and contained a wood-burning stove that was not code compliant.

Hubbard, who saved Jack from the deadly blaze “while saying his last words to his wife and daughter,” will never be the same, the complaint maintains. He used to love fishing and taking his family to the beach, it says. Jack, for his part, suffered severe burns, smoke inhalation, and will endure “life-long trauma” because of the disaster, according to the complaint.

“Before this horrific event, [Jack] was a very happy child, who was easy going, and extremely close to his mother,” it explains. “He loved being an older brother and liked sharing his toys and incorporating his younger sister… into his play. [Jack] loved the beach, playing in the water and fishing with his dad, was extremely social in school with his friends and loved learning about dinosaurs and space.”

Since the fire, however, Jack “has not been the same child.”

“He constantly asks for his mother and sister, stares at photos of his mother and sister and has a tough time leaving his father’s side,” the complaint states.

Shannon Hubbard, a teacher who worked with special-needs children, “loved being married to John,” the complaint goes on.

open image in gallery Airbnb hosts Dennis and Meredith Darcy face manslaughter charges after a fatal house fire that killed two ( Dutchess County DA )

“She loved to read and was a member of book clubs, loved outdoor activities, loved going to the beach with her children and dogs and loved living on Cape Cod,” it says. “More than anything, Shannon loved being a mother to [Maggie] and [Jack] and would choose her children first and always.”

Maggie, the complaint continues, “had her complete life stolen, but in her brief time on this earth was very confident, spunky and had an assertive personality.”

It says she “loved playing with her brother… and was daddy’s girl.”

“At the time of her death she was learning to walk and would gravitate towards anything her brother… showed interest in,” the complaint states. [Maggie] was named after her paternal grandma Margaret and her maternal grandma June.”

Airbnb removed the Darcys’ listing after the incident, according to the complaint. The filing names Airbnb, Meredith and Dennis Darcy, several contractors, and a home inspector as co-defendants. The Darcys’ criminal case remains pending.

“This devastating tragedy could have been prevented,” Dutchess County DA Anthony Parisi told WRGB-TV News. “The deaths of Shannon Hubbard and her young daughter in this senseless fire serve as a tragic reminder of the critical role smoke detectors play in safeguarding lives.”

Hubbard is now demanding a money judgment to be determined by a jury, including compensatory damages for pain, suffering, emotional distress, and loss of enjoyment of life; economic and pecuniary damages for medical expenses, out of pocket expenses, loss of earnings, and funeral expenses; and punitive and/or exemplary damages for the “wanton, willful, fraudulent, [and] reckless acts” of the Darcys; as well as pre-judgment interest, post-judgement interest, attorneys’ fees and court costs.

Wildfires driven by powerful winds swept through homes and trees near northern Greek resorts on Thursday, forcing locals and vacationers to escape villages in the Halkidiki region across both land and sea at the peak of the holiday season.

Wearing protective face masks and holding their pets, residents and visitors boarded dinghies and small boats in coastal Siviri as flames consumed nearby forests and thick gray smoke filled the clear skies. Inland, fires severely damaged holiday rental apartments and balconies facing toward the open sea.

According to an official statement from the coast guard, over 300 individuals were evacuated by vessel from Siviri, located on a scenic peninsula of forests, olive trees and beaches south of Greece's second city, Thessaloniki. The maritime effort utilized patrol craft, firefighting boats, and local fishing vessels during the rescue operation.

More than 140 firefighters were deployed to battle flames raging on both sides of the main road from Siviri to the town of Kassandreia ( Reuters/Alexandros Litsardakis )

More than 140 firefighters were deployed to battle flames raging on both sides of the main road from Siviri to the town of Kassandreia. Nine aircraft and seven helicopters were also deployed, the fire brigade said in a statement posted on X. One firefighter was injured and traffic has been stopped.

"Our effort is focused on extinguishing the fire and the safe transport of people," fire brigade spokesman Giannis Artopios told Protothema news portal.

Across Europe, successive heatwaves this summer have intensified drought, strained water supplies and left vegetation tinder-dry, fueling an unusually active wildfire season in France, Spain and Greece that has scorched near-unprecedented amounts of land.

Roughly 1,200 people were evacuated from a campsite as a result of two wildfires near a beach in northern France, local officials announced on Wednesday.

The prefecture for the administrative department of Pas-de-Calais, situated in the country's north and bordering the Strait of Dover, reported that one wildfire was under control. However, conditions were "unfavourable" for the second blaze, as difficult access allowed the fire to spread unimpeded toward the south.

French environment minister Monique Barbut said earlier on Wednesday that the heatwaves could result in as much as €15 billion ($17 billion) in direct and indirect costs.

France and the wider continent, the world’s fastest-warming region, saw vegetation flourish after a relatively wet winter before drying out during the rolling heatwaves.

News.title: ‘More pain’ to come after economic slowdown
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The economy grew at a slower pace in the second quarter of the year, official figures show, under pressure from the Iran war.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc between April and June, down from 0.6pc in the first three months of the year, according to the Office for National Statistics.

The figures underline the challenge that the conflict poses for Andy Burnham, who has pledged to deliver “growth in every postcode”.

The Prime Minister has already been warned that the economy will slow further next year if Donald Trump continues his war in the Middle East.

Treasury officials have predicted UK growth of just 0.3pc in 2027 if the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked for the rest of this year.

That is far lower than the 1.6pc predicted by the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) in March, based on assumptions made before the start of the war. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Iran war threatens to cripple growth, Treasury warns Burnham | Officials predict economic expansion of just 0.3pc in 2027 if Strait of Hormuz stays blocked

2) Britain facing £54bn bill for North Sea shutdown | Costs soar amid shortage of specialised ships needed to clear up abandoned oil rigs

3) Ban on zero-hours contracts to cost companies up to £3bn | Businesses face huge bill to offer workers guaranteed hours under Employment Rights Act

4) Nvidia’s AI push has echoes of Enron, says Big Short investor | Michael Burry claims chip giant is engaging in ‘circular’ financing

5) Shadow bank founder battles to stave off bankruptcy threat | Paresh Raja launches legal claim to prevent administrators from chasing him for repayment

What happened overnight

Asian shares were mostly higher, powered by gains for AI-related stocks including computer chips as regional markets tracked a rally on Wall Street.

Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 advanced 1.6pc to 68,601.21. In South Korea, the Kospi jumped 4pc, climbing to 6,844.65, as shares in Samsung Electronics surged 5.4pcc. Computer chipmaker SK Hynix jumped 7.1pc.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng rose 0.3pc to 3,967.28, while the Shanghai Composite index added 0.5pc to 3,967.65.

In Australia, the S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.4pc to 9,155.80.

Data from the US on Wednesday showed consumer prices had risen in line with analysts’ expectations in July.

Wall Street stocks were boosted on Wednesday by gains made by tech companies CoreWeave and Super Micro Computer, both of which closed up by more than 19pc.

The Nasdaq Composite ended the session up 0.5pc, with the S&P 500 up nearly 0.3pc. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the session marginally down.

Oil prices were little changed as investors weighed the deadlock in talks between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, was broadly flat at nearly $89 a barrel.

News.title: H5N1 sparks a very Australian epidemic
News.content:
H5N1 bird flu has reached Australia’s shores and is threatening to infect some of the country’s most unique wildlife.

Australasia is the last continent to be hit by the highly infectious avian influenza H5N1, a new strain of which has been circulating worldwide since 2020.

Since recording its first case in June, more than 200 wild seabirds in Australia have been infected, with fears that the highly infectious flu could quickly ‘jump’ to other species.

While H5N1 has infected animals from foxes to sea lions in other parts of the world in recent years, the epidemic now threatens some of Australia’s most iconic wildlife – many of which are found nowhere else on earth.

An Australian government assessment of more than 2,000 native species warned that nearly one in five faces a high risk from the deadly H5N1 bird flu, with hundreds of unique birds and mammals vulnerable to severe population reductions or even extinction.

Those animals include iconic species like the Tasmanian devils, quolls, and dingoes.

Other aquatic mammals, including the platypus, which is only found in Australia, are at risk of infection through contact with bird droppings in shared wetlands and coastal environments.

News.title: Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end
News.content:
Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

News.title: Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG
News.content:
His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

News.title: Advice, cookbooks and emergency pot noodles: Your best gifts for university students
News.content:
When it comes to sending a child or grandchild off to university, it can be tempting to fill their room with every conceivable gadget.

So to help, we asked the Telegraph Recommended Community for their best gift recommendations and their suggestions ranged from desk lamps to cookery books and supermarket gift cards.

Here are the essentials worth buying.

Kitchen basics

From cupboard essentials to electrical appliances and cookbooks, most readers say they’d gift kitchen equipment.

Thinking back to his university days, reader TJ, 43, from London, says “the main essentials are around kitchen items and good long lasting food”.

“It’s nice to have some bits to cook for others as well and to make friends quickly,” he adds.

Susan, 54, from the West Midlands, agrees, recommending “basic cooking equipment” as a key staple and “distinctive cutlery, plates and cups that are easily identified”, which are particularly useful for shared accommodation.

“A box of store cupboard ingredients such as olive oil, soy, stock cubes and spices to use when cooking,” is also well-received, she says.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check
News.content:
Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

Team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

Sports.title: Arsenal rocked by £20m Ezri Konsa problem after new transfer talks with Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Arsenal rocked by £20m Ezri Konsa problem after new transfer talks with Aston Villa

Arsenal remain strongly interested in Aston Villa and England central defender Ezri Konsa, who has two years left to run on his existing deal at Villa Park

View 2 Images Arsenal's are not currently prepared to match Aston Villa's £60m valuation for Ezri Konsa

Arsenal have been back in touch with Aston Villa over a potential deal for Ezri Konsa but the UEFA Super Cup finalists' £60million valuation is proving problematic.

‌



The 28-year-old remains the Premier League champions' top defensive target heading into the final stretch of the summer transfer window with head coach Mikel Arteta actively pushing to strengthen his backline.

‌



For now, there remains a notable gap - worth in the region of £20m - between what the Gunners would be willing to pay and the kind of money that would see Villa seriously consider a sale.

‌



Arsenal are understood to have made a verbal approach for Konsa earlier in the window, around the time of their interest in Morgan Rogers, which ultimately amounted to nothing.

But the Gunners never truly threw in the towel as the versatile centre-back, who can also operate as a right-back, ticks multiple boxes Arteta.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He is rapid approaching his peak and is vastly experienced having just competed in his second major tournament for England. He is also a threat in both boxes and crucially, is homegrown.

Konsa, who is also close friends with Bukayo Saka, hails from Newham in east London and is thought to be open to joining Arsenal, even though he was a boyhood Tottenham Hotspur supporter.

Still, a transfer, at this stage, remains difficult as Unai Emery is counting on the player for the upcoming season.

‌



Villa have also offered Konsa a new contract, his existing deal expires in 2028, and that proposal remains on the table.

Mirror Football understands Arsenal would be prepared to better the wages currently on offer in the Midlands, which may prove attractive for Konsa

Villa are not thought to be under any immediate financial pressure to cash-in following the exits of Rogers (£117m to Chelsea ) and Youri Tielemans (£35m to Manchester United) and there's a desire to strengthen, not weaken, Emery's squad following the 2-1 defeat to PSG in Salzburg.

‌



View 2 Images Arsenal are in the hunt for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa (Image: (Photo by Sarah Stier - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images))

For now, Arsenal view 16-year-old Marli Salmon is viewed as adequate cover and competition for Cristhian Mosquera at right centre-back but there is still scope to bolster their defensive options without William Saliba sidelined due to a back issue.

An injury to Ben White or Mosquera, would also drastically change the picture with Jurrien Timber still recovering from a minor groin procedure.

‌



Ideally, the Gunners want to sign a profile that can play at both centre-back and right-back, which is why Konsa fits the bill.

Other options, including Tottenham's Cristian Romero (now set to join Atletico Madrid) and Atletico's Marc Pubill have been explored but to no avail. Arsenal will be forced to consider other alternatives if Villa continue to dig their heels into the ground.

Konsa has been handed an extended break by Emery alongside England team-mate Ollie Watkins and goalkeeper Emi Martinez following their involvement in the World Cup. He has insisted that all three players required four weeks of rest, which is why he ruled them out of the Super Cup.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford and Man Utd have 'questions to answer' despite Michael Carrick praise
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford and Man Utd have 'questions to answer' despite Michael Carrick praise

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United for pre-season training this week after his loan spell with Barcelona came to an end

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is back with Manchester United (Image: (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United legend John O'Shea says it'll be a straightforward conversation between Michael Carrick and Marcus Rashford ahead of his return to the first-team setup. The England forward is set to return to the fold for Carrick, despite spending the last 18 months plying his trade elsewhere.

‌



Barcelona turned down the chance to Rashford permanently after his loan stint at the Nou Camp, and he reported back for pre-season training with the Reds earlier this week. There was still uncertainty about his future at Old Trafford leading up to the pre-season clash with Leeds United, but O'Shea is convinced his former colleague is man to get the best out of the England international.

‌



Speaking to ITV before Man United's pre-season fixture against Leeds United, O'Shea said: "Yeah, listen, it's straightforward. I think it'll be an honest conversation, straight up.

‌



Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear READ MORE :

Michael Carrick tells Man Utd owners exactly what he needs in rest of transfer window READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Do you want to stay? If you do, great, let's see what you've got again, and then start afresh. And listen, you know the fans, there'll be question marks thinking, what are we doing, type of thing.

"But if he goes and struts his stuff at Old Trafford straight away, a lot will be forgiven, I think. [There's] Still some questions to answer as well."

‌



Fellow pundit Michael Brown concurred, and said: "See, all those players we mentioned, we always have to come back down to Marcus Rashford.

"The reason it does, John, is because, as you know, he's got everything, hasn't he? He can change games. He's electric, he's got the pace. If you can get the best out of him, then it'd be a great sign.

"I think Michael Carrick is a great person to go and do that. He's going to have to work, he's going to have to earn it to get into the team, but imagine if he was firing this season."

‌



View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is back in the Manchester United fold

Rashford travelled with the United squad for their pre-season clash against Leeds United in Dublin at Croke Park, yet was absent from the matchday squad having just returned to training this week.

It proved to be a solid outing for Carrick's side, who broke the deadlock in the first half through Joshua Zirkzee in the 16th minute following some superb work from Bryan Mbeumo down the left flank.

‌



Leeds hit back to level things up when Brenden Aaronson equalised just before the half-hour mark. Neither side could find the decisive breakthrough in the second half, with the match ultimately heading to a penalty shootout in front of a sold-out Croke Park.

Bruno Fernandes squandered his spot-kick for United, yet they still prevailed 5-4 as Harry Wilson and James Justin both failed to convert for Leeds.

Carrick was asked about Rashford's future and said: "He's our player, he came back Sunday night, he arrived with Kobbie [Mainoo], and Lisandro [Martinez] came the day after, and he's part of the group like anybody else. He came in, he's trained really well.

Article continues below

"I've known him a long time, like I've known some of the others a long time, so I don't treat him any different to anybody else, but it's been good to have him around the group again this week. So I'm really positive with that."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick confirms Man Utd's Marcus Rashford plan as transfer reality becomes clear

Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United following loan spells with Aston Villa and Barcelona as Michael Carrick prepares to reintegrate him into the squad

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is back in the Manchester United picture

Michael Carrick insists Marcus Rashford still has plenty to offer Manchester United this season with it now looking increasingly likely he will stay at Old Trafford.

‌



The England international hasn't played for his boyhood club since December 2024, when he was frozen out by former manager Ruben Amorim. Since then, he has had loan spells with Aston Villa and then spent last season with Barcelona.

‌



It was expected that he would secure a permanent move to the Camp Nou, but their decision to sign Anthony Gordon meant they opted against triggering his £26million clause.

‌



He now returns to United, where he could make his return, ironically, against Amorim's AC Milan this weekend. The Manchester Evening News report both sides believe it is most likely he will remain at his parent club and Carrick is confident he will be a positive presence in his squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"He's a very good player, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in a direction and maybe a different direction," he said.

‌



"I think there are ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting."

Had Amorim stayed in charge, it is inconceivable that the burnt bridges would have been able to be mended, but Carrick has a history with Rashford and has helped to smooth the process.

And while Carrick stopped short of definitively confirming he will stay at United, he described him as 'our player' and said he is being treated the same as anyone else within his squad.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford has not played for Manchester United since December 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

"He's our player, he came back Sunday night, he arrived with Kobbie [Mainoo], and Lisandro [Martinez] came the day after, and he's part of the group like anybody else. He came in, he's trained really well.

"I've known him a long time, like I've known some of the others a long time, so I don't treat him any different to anybody else, but it's been good to have him around the group again this week. So I'm really positive with that."

‌



Carrick added that he was confident the returning Rashford would bring something new to his options and help balance the squad for the upcoming Premier League campaign.

He added: "We're really calm, we just treat it like anybody else coming into the group and there's obviously this slight twist that he knows the club as well as anybody and that's a real positive.

‌



"He's been here all his career, all his life before the last 18 months or so, to understand what it means. That side of things is natural, that's a given. I know he's got history, but I've got history with a number of the players as well, so that doesn't make that a unique situation at all and treat him as exactly like any other player.

"Bringing him into the group and carrying on as normal brings the good things that we haven't got, and we want to get that balance with every individual player, and Marcus has come back and he's in good form, and it's been good to have him around this week."

Sports.title: Man Utd handed Lewis Hall transfer update as Newcastle close in on full-back agreement
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed Lewis Hall transfer update as Newcastle close in on full-back agreement

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick wants the club to sign a new left-back before the summer transfer window closes and Newcastle's Lewis Hall is top of their wish list

View 2 Images Lewis Hall remains a Newcastle player for now (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Manchester United's pursuit of Lewis Hall could be given renewed hope after Newcastle made a breakthrough in the transfer market. Hall is United's No.1 target as they chase a left-back this summer and a development on Tyneside may have caught their eye.

‌



United manager Michael Carrick is keen to add some competition for Luke Shaw ahead of the start of the 2026/27 season. Academy graduate Harry Amass has been told he is free to leave, Diego Leon hasn't kicked on as hoped, Diego Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui are more comfortable at right-back and Patrick Dorgu is better further forward on the left.

‌



United have been monitoring Hall for some time and believe he is the perfect long-term successor to Shaw, who is entering his 13th season at the club. A previous approach was firmly rejected by Newcastle, who are determined not to sell Hall after waving goodbye to Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



The 21-year-old still has three years left on his contract following a £28million move from Chelsea two years ago, putting the Magpies in a strong negotiating position. It is believed they value the defender at £60m.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Despite Newcastle's reluctance to do business, United may be encouraged by a report from The Athletic, which says they have made significant progress in talks with Benfica for full-back Amar Dedic.

Bosnia and Herzegovina international Dedic is expected to cost Newcastle around €35m (£30m) and will become the first signing of the Matthias Jaissle era. The 23-year-old is primarily a right-back, but is also capable of playing at left-back with Tino Livramento closing in on a return to full fitness.

Newcastle have been desperate for defensive reinforcements and to bolster a squad depleted by the departures of Kieran Trippier, Emil Krafth and Matt Targett this summer.

‌



Newcastle have banked over £250m from the sales of Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes and their hierarchy are under pressure to ensure Eddie Howe's successor has a competitive squad come the start of the campaign. As such, they have so far been unwilling to discuss an exit for Hall.

View 2 Images Amar Dedic is expected to leave Benfica for Newcastle (Image: Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images)

What could change that stance is Hall himself. The Sun reported this week that Hall is keen to leave for the Red Devils. If he were to agitate for a move, like Alexander Isak famously did last summer to leave for Liverpool, it could leave Newcastle with little choice.

‌



United have signed Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa and Andrey Santos from Chelsea to strengthen their midfield, while Karl Darlow has arrived on a free transfer to become the back-up goalkeeper. But a left-back and another central midfielder are considered must haves by Carrick.

If Hall proves unattainable then United will pursue other targets. Club Brugge's £30m-rated Joaquin Seys another option, along with Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander, who would cost around £14m.

Sports.title: The £250m Premier League triple transfer that could cause chaos this weekend
Sports.content:
The £250m Premier League triple transfer that could cause chaos this weekend

Manchester City could be at the centre of £250m worth of transfer dealings before the weeks is out which could see a club-record bid lodged for Chelsea's Enzo Maresca

View 3 Images Rodri could choose to call time on his Man City career this summer (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Manchester City could be involved in three deals this weekend should the blocks fall into place - which could end with them lodging a club-record bid for Enzo Fernandez.

‌



Those at the Etihad are embarking on a new era following the departure of Pep Guardiola and the Enzo Maresca tenure could begin with some wholesale changes to the club's midfield.

‌



Since winning the World Cup, Rodri has been linked with a return to Spain and Barcelona look to have leapt ahead of Real Madrid in the queue, despite their long-term interest. The Catalans have already seen one bid rejected by the Premier League side.

‌



City could ultimately be forced into a corner regarding Rodri, who was a talisman of the Guardiola era and one of the men who drove their winning mentality. He's entered the final year of his deal and returning home is ultimately on his agenda.

Chelsea set Man City strict deadline to complete £120m Enzo Fernandez transfer READ MORE :

Elliot Anderson backs himself to replace Rodri as he doubles down on Man Utd snub READ MORE :

The Manchester outfit are seeking £70m before they consider letting Rodri leave and if Barcelona hit that figure then a move back to La Liga could be on the cards.

The club-record signing of Elliot Anderson, who joined from Nottingham Forest for £116m, is part of planning for life after Rodri with the England star blossoming since leaving Newcastle. Anderson would serve, from a technical point of view, as a similar player to the Spaniard, operating at the base of midfield.

‌



One man from the Guardiola era who was not seen his City career take off has been Tijjani Reijnders. He headed to Manchester from AC Milan off the back of being named the best midfielder in Italy, but the Dutchman found it difficult to nail down regular minutes at the Etihad.

View 3 Images Enzo Fernandez has been linked with a move away from Chelsea this summer (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

He was signed for £46.5m but a move to Saudi Arabia is now on the cards with Al Qadsiah willing to pay £60m. That profit would give City scope to go out and add more quality in the midfield, which would ultimately be needed if Rodri and Reijnders did both depart Manchester. Bernardo Silva also left this summer upon the expiry of his contract.

‌



That comes 12 months after Kevin De Bruyne was allowed to seek a new challenge, heading to Napoli, all of which leaves City undergoing a major revamp of their midfield. Rodri and Bernardo were the last remaining figures of the team that dominated England in the early 2020s.

The club remain in talks with Lille for Morocco midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who enjoyed a stellar World Cup, but Maresca's appointment has led to inevitable links with Fernandez at Chelsea.

View 3 Images Tijjani Reijnders' spell in Manchester could be over inside a year

‌



The Argentina star made noises about leaving Stamford Bridge last season, expressing his desire to live in Madrid, which eventually saw him suspended by the club. New Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso is determine to keep hold of his midfielder, who alongside Moises Caicedo forms one of the more impressive partnerships in the country.

Chelsea want to avoid a scenario whereby Fernandez's future is still being discussed whilst their beginning their Premier League campaign, and as a result have given City until 5pm on Friday to table an offer.

They want £120m for Fernandez, which would exceed the fee City spend on Anderson. The need for midfielders, and the bank balance, may have shifted over the next 48 hours depending on who leaves the blue side of Manchester.

Article continues below

It could all lead to a transfer merry-go-round that sees £250m changing hands if price tags are met with Fernandez becoming one of the most expensive domestic deals ever.
