Sports.title: Chelsea still await bid for Enzo Fernandez despite looming deadline - as his suitors Man City agree to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi Arabia: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Chelsea still await bid for Enzo Fernandez despite looming deadline - as his suitors Man City agree to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi Arabia: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea wait on Enzo bid

Chelsea have still to receive any bids for Enzo Fernandez - 23 hours ahead of their self-imposed deadline.

Manchester City are interested but have been told to submit a written £120m offer by 5pm on Friday.

Chelsea are among the clubs to have checked on Monaco's Lamine Camara.

The principality club rejected an offer from Crystal Palace for 22-year-old Camara earlier this week.

Chelsea are yet to receive a bid from Enzo Fernandez after setting a deadline of 5pm on Friday

Tijjani BYE-nders

Tijjani Reijnders has agreed to join Al Qadsiah from Manchester City.

The Saudi Pro League club coached by former Celtic and Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers agreed a £52million fee with City.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed, Nottingham Forest had made a proposal earlier this month for the 28-year-old Netherlands international and Galatasaray had made an approach in recent days.

Spence set for Italian job

Djed Spence will travel to Italy ahead of his Inter Milan medical tomorrow.

Tottenham have agreed to sell the England international for £26million and his former club Middlesbrough hold a percentage sell-on of the profit.

Spurs paid £20m to buy Spence from Boro in 2022

City reject fresh Rodri bid

Manchester City and Barcelona continue to discuss a fee for midfielder Rodri.

City have dismissed Barca’s latest offer of around £55m as they hold out for closer to £68m for the Spain captain.

Meanwhile, City forward Jeremy Doku has signed a new contract at the Etihad that will keep him at the club until 2031, with an option for a further year.

The Belgium international said : ‘This club means so much to me – I have developed as both a player and a person. I feel settled here, and I know I am improving every day because of the work the staff here do.

‘It’s hard to explain just how much this Club does to help players. I don’t take it for granted and it makes me better.

‘With Enzo here now I am really excited about the new season. His style of football is the kind we love, so that’s exciting for the players.

‘The City fans are also a huge reason I have signed this new contract. I feel their love and support, and it means the world to me. I want to focus of bringing them the success they deserve.’

Barcelona have had a fresh £55million bid for Rodri rejected by Manchester City

Galatasaray move for Martinelli

Galatasaray have made their move for Arsenal winger Gabriel Martinelli with a £38million offer.

However, the Brazilian is not inclined to leave for Turkey.

The 25-year-old is one of the players Arsenal are prepared to listen to offers for with a valuation around £50m.

Roma have also shown interest and it is understood Martinelli will only consider options from the strongest leagues.

Arsenal are re-evaluating options to strengthen their left hand side, they are also continuing discussions with Aston Villa for centre back Ezri Konsa with their latest proposal understood to be around £40m for the centre back.

Al Qadsiah make offer for Reijnders

Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah have made an offer of around £52million for Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders.

Nottingham Forest remain in the frame for the Netherlands international but he is weighing up whether to accept the offer to link up with coach Brendan Rodgers.

Al Qadsiah have been looking to make room for Reijnders arrival.

They are in the process of selling Jeffrey Afriyie to Genk with other departures planned.

It became clear during the pre-season tour of Asia that the 28-year-old was the most likely midfielder to move on before the transfer window closes.

City hold an interest in Enzo Fernandez but Chelsea have imposed a deadline of 5pm on Friday to present a suitable offer for the Argentina international.

It’s understood that City are operating a one-in, one-out system with transfers this month and the exit of Reijnders would free up a space in the engine room.

JACK GAUGHAN

Tijjani Reijnders missed City open training after Al Qadsiah have made an offer for him

Besiktas in the frame for £18m Willock

Besiktas remain in the frame for Newcastle United midfielder Joe Willock.

The 26-year-old has one year left on contract and is valued around £18m. Premier League sides have also shown interest while Besiktas had an offer rejected early this month.

Race for Nwaneri heats up

Interest is building in Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri who is considering his options and whether to depart this window.

A number of clubs, including RB Leipzig and other Premier League sides, have been looking to take the 19-year-old on loan or potentially a permanent basis after his disappointing spell with Marseille last season.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta praised the England U21 international after his return to pre-season training, saying: ‘Ethan has been really good, probably what happened on the field on his loan in Marseille wasn’t what was expected, and there was a lot of noise and change around the club.

‘But he looks different, a lot more mature, it’s incredible what six months and a different experience abroad can do to you - to be abroad on your own, to go through tough times and to witness that is a part of football you have to be good enough to cope with. I’m very happy with what Ethan has done in pre-season.’

Nwaneri joined Arsenal's academy aged eight and made his Premier League debut against Brentford in September 2022, becoming the youngest player to appear in the English top flight, at 15 years and 181 days old.

He has made 34 appearances for Arsenal and though only made nine appearances at Marseille, still managed to score two goals.

Pape Sarr a target for Al Ahli

Tottenham midfielder Pape Matar Sarr is emerging as a target for Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League.

The 23-year-old will be allowed to leave if suitable offers arrive and has been the subject of interest from Brentford and Aston Villa as well as other European sides.

Spurs beat off strong competition to sign Sarr from Metz in 2021 and, while he has shown glimpses of what he is capable of, the Senegal international has been inconsistent overall, as have the majority of the squad in recent seasons.

The arrival of Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali mean his starting opportunities will be limited and he is open to exploring a move away.

Spurs are looking to wrap up the sales of Cristian Romero to Atletico and Djed Spence to Inter today.

They remain keen on Manchester City’s Savinho and Cody Gakpo of Liverpool. City’s Omar Marmoush is also on their list.

Villa expected to reject Arsenal offer for Konsa

Aston Villa were expected to turn down Arsenal’s initial proposal of £40million for Ezri Konsa, who is thought to be open to the move.

Villa are also looking to close deals for midfielder Joao Palhinha and left-back Matteo Ruggeri.

TOM COLLOMOSSE

Ezri Konsa is said to be open to a move to the Premier League champions Arsenal

United youngster Williams joins Peterborough

Manchester United winger Ethan Williams has joined Peterborough United for a ‘sizeable’ undisclosed fee.

The 20-year-old, who was part of United’s pre-season tour of Finland, Norway and Sweden, has signed a long-term deal.

Williams had spent time on loan at League Two Cheltenham Town and Scottish Premiership outfit Falkirk.

He said: ‘I have enjoyed my time at [Manchester] United and it's always tough to leave a place like that, but there comes a time in your career where you have to make tough decisions to develop yourself and Peterborough is renowned for helping younger players.’

United’s deal also includes add-ons, a 50percent sell-on clause, a buy-back option and matching rights.

Tigers making moves in the market

Leeds United forward Joe Gelhardt has completed his medical at Hull City ahead of his £4.5million move.

He has agreed a four year contract with option for a further year. Wrexham and Rangers had also made efforts to sign the 24-year-old.

Meanwhile, Hull have formalised their interest in Everton midfielder Tim Iroegbunam with an offer understood to be in excess of £15million.

The 23-year-old has a year left on contract.

If it ain't So?

Brazilian side Palmeiras have signed Fabio So from Burnley.

The 18-year-old made 15 appearances in the U18 Premier League for Burnley, as well as a couple of appearances for the U21s. He left on a free transfer and has signed a contract until the end of January. The contract includes the possibility of an automatic renewal.

Portuguese midfielder So joined Burnley after being at Newcastle's academy.

Amorim's Milan exodus

AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim has decided Fikayo Tomori and Christopher Nkunku do not figure in his plans this season.

The former Chelsea players are available for sale along with midfielder Youssouf Fofana.

David Odogu, Pervis Estupinan, Santiago Gimenez and Philip Terracciano are also expected to leave.

Fikayo Tomori is one of eight AC Milan players who have been put up for sale by Ruben Amorim

Ge-Evan-noa

Brighton striker Evan Ferguson is a target for Genoa.

The Republic of Ireland international was on loan in Serie A at Roma last season, where he scored five goals in 22 appearances, and rivals Genoa would like him to return.

The 21-year-old has been hindered by niggling injuries and damaged his ankle in March but he is also attracting Premier League interest.

Reds youngsters on the move

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is closing on a loan to Cardiff City.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff and they have been working hard to bring him back.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and attracted a number of enquiries.

League One Sheffield Wednesday, notably, made concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Liverpool midfielder James McConnell is a loan target for Championship side Preston North End.

A number of other Championship teams have enquired for the 21-year-old plus League One Leicester City.

Meanwhile, Arsenal are closing in agreement for 16-year-old striker Vincent Joseph who had decided to leave Liverpool last month.

Liverpool offered the teenager a scholarship but he declined and talks are ongoing over compensation.

The last teenager to leave Liverpool for another Premier League club was Isaac Moran. He left for Newcastle United earlier this year and a subsequent tribunal resulted in a seven-figure fee being payable to Liverpool with the settlement having the potential to reach £5m.

TUESDAY: Roy Keane's son-in-law linked with move to Portugal

MONDAY: West Ham interested in free agent Jamie Vardy

SUNDAY: Everton and Crystal Palace in advanced talks over McNeil-Johnson swap

SATURDAY: West Ham and Tottenham agree £5m fee for Manor Solomon

FRIDAY: Rodri tells Real Madrid he wishes to join Barcelona

THURSDAY: Man City target new goalkeeper after James Trafford sale

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez is the face of the ugly game and Enzo Maresca should run a mile from him. Replacing Pep Guardiola at Man City is already the hardest job in football without once again indulging Argentine's graceless, brainless behaviour
Sports.content:
It is not a surprise that Manchester City appear to be pursuing Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez, a player who has come to symbolise much that is ugly about the beautiful game.

City's new manager, Enzo Maresca, has got form for indulging and rewarding the graceless and base antics of the Argentina midfielder that goes back to his time in charge at Stamford Bridge.

Two years ago, Maresca was forced to defend his decision to select Fernandez as Chelsea captain in their opening game of the 2024-25 season, against City, just a month after Fernandez posted a video of him and other Argentina players mocking the racial heritage of the France team.

Chelsea team-mate Wesley Fofana branded the video, uploaded by Fernandez after Argentina's victory over Colombia in that summer's Copa America final, as 'uninhibited racism'. Fernandez apologised. And in the absence of Reece James, Maresca made him skipper.

What Fernandez did was brainless as well as offensive. This is a player, don't forget, who was suspended by his own club at the end of last season after he flirted publicly with Real Madrid. This is a player who helped to get Liam Rosenior the sack at Chelsea when his performances dipped noticeably.

This is a man who is up there with the worst in the league in his attempts to pressure referees with his antics. This is a player who was sent off in the World Cup final and whose thuggish, unpunished behaviour in the semi-final against England prompted widespread disgust.

It is not a surprise that Manchester City appear to be pursuing Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez, who in the last couple of years has come to symbolise much that is ugly about the beautiful game

City's new manager Enzo Maresca has got form for indulging the graceless and base antics of the Argentina midfielder that goes back to his time in charge at Stamford Bridge

In those circumstances, and given Chelsea set an asking price of £120million, it was predictable that Madrid did not want to go anywhere near him. It was less predictable that they would take the unusual step of stating publicly they were not interested in buying him.

'The club wishes to state,' read the Madrid communique at the beginning of July, 'that it has not made any efforts, either directly or indirectly, aimed at signing the aforementioned player and, furthermore, has no intention of pursuing such an operation.'

But now, a couple of months into the job, Maresca is already risking the reputation City built in their Pep Guardiola years, for being a side that was widely admired for the quality, style and attitude with which it went about dominating the Premier League.

Chelsea have set a deadline of 5pm on Friday for City to make a bid for Fernandez and meet their asking price but it is possible the story will bleed further towards the transfer deadline of September 1.

City under Guardiola were the team of gifted stars like Kevin De Bruyne and Bernardo Silva. They were the team of Rodri and Ilkay Gundogan, Jack Grealish and Erling Haaland. They were a team that put a smile on the face of any neutral that watched them.

The purchase of Fernandez, if it happens, will change that. Fernandez is a fine player but his quality comes at a high cost in terms of the image of the team he plays for. The wisest managers buy character as well as quality.

The truth is that if City buy Fernandez, it will represent not just a downgrade on Rodri but a reversal of much that the club stood for under Guardiola. It will represent an embrace of the ugly side of the game. It will be a transfer that stands for cynicism. It will be a move that says City are swapping beauty for the game's dark arts.

The truth is also that Chelsea overpaid for Fernandez when they agreed to give Benfica £106.8million for him in the aftermath of the 2022 World Cup. He has not been as big a failure as some of the BlueCo signings but he has mixed some outstanding performances with periods of near anonymity.

The truth is that if City buy Fernandez (right), it will represent not just a downgrade on Rodri (left) but a reversal of much that the club stood for under Pep Guardiola

It will represent an embrace of the ugly side of the game. It will be a transfer that stands for cynicism. It will be a move that says City are swapping beauty for the game's dark arts

He is supposed to be one of the leaders of the team but there were spells last season when he looked nothing like a leader. Leaders don't flirt with other teams. Leaders don't get suspended by their own club. Leaders don't allow mediocrity to flourish all around them.

Chelsea finished tenth in the Premier League last season, 33 points adrift of champions Arsenal and Fernandez was part of that surrender. If Chelsea do sell him to City and somehow manage to recoup the money they paid for him, it should be cause for a huge celebration on the King's Road.

There are early signs, in fact, that Chelsea, under their own new manager Xabi Alonso, are starting to pursue a more coherent transfer policy and achieve a better balance in their playing staff. If Fernandez leaves, it will be another step in the right direction.

For City, it would be the opposite. Maresca already has the most difficult job in English football in attempting to replace Guardiola. If he signs Fernandez, that job will get a whole lot harder.

Sports.title: Paul Pogba's wife hits back at claims he should retire, with 33-year-old set to have Monaco contract ripped up after yet another cruel injury blow
Sports.content:
Paul Pogba's wife has hit back after claims that her husband should retire from football, with Monaco set to rip up his contract.

The former World Cup winner and ex-Man United midfielder has been dogged by injuries in pre-season and multiple reports in France state that his agents are in talks with the club over a mutual termination, at Monaco's request.

Pogba had been trying to revive his career following a doping ban but only featured in six games last season while earning £44,000-a-week at the Ligue 1 side.

He suffered a knee issue after 45 minutes of pre-season and another nasty setback with a thigh injury last week. But with some fans suggesting his body can no longer tolerate playing at the top level, his wife Zulay, 33, defended her husband online.

She wrote: 'For all the people saying Paul should retire or he came back to football for the money, let me make this clear, the only one who knows when he will retire is God.

'And for the ones who say he came back for the money, trust me we are very good with money, thank God.

Paul Pogba's wife, Zulay (right), defended her husband aft

'Social media accepts everything. People can sit behind a screen and say whatever they want, insult someone, question their intentions and forget that there is an actual human being on the other side.

'For those questioning what he has left to prove, let me remind you he achieved the dream every footballer in the world grows up chasing, dreaming to have. He won the World Cup for his country.'

Zulay is a Bolivian model and influencer and the couple met in 2017 before getting married two years later. They have two sons aged seven and six together.

Pogba only returned to training last week after injuring himself in the first game of pre-season but sustained a thigh issue in a small-sided game and was scheduled for an MRI this week.

Daily Mail Sport understands he was offered to MLS clubs in America on Tuesday.

Pogba was allowed back into football in March 2025 after his doping ban was reduced on appeal.

He had already left Juventus after having that contract terminated by mutual consent in December 2024.

Pogba was emotional when he signed for Monaco last summer, describing his comeback as a second chance after what he called 'a time of darkness'.

The midfielder told Daily Mail Sport in 2024 that he discovered news of his reduced ban while preparing for a film premiere, adding: 'We went through hell. A time of darkness. But this is my second chance, I have to use it.'

Sports.title: Ruben Amorim wields the axe at AC Milan: Former Man United boss tells EIGHT stars they have no future at the club - including Chelsea flop - as he implements his five-at-the-back system
Sports.content:
Ruben Amorim wields the axe at AC Milan: Former Man United boss tells EIGHT stars they have no future at the club - including Chelsea flop - as he implements his five-at-the-back system

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ruben Amorim has told seven AC Milan stars that they have no future with the Italian giants as he implements a brutal cull in his first summer at the club.

Former Chelsea stars Fikayo Tomori and Christopher Nkunku are among the octet being driven out of Milan by the ex-Manchester United boss.

Amorim took charge at the San Siro in early June, just over six months after he was sacked by the Red Devils, where he won 38.1 per cent of his games.

He has got off to a poor start in charge of the Rossoneri, drawing against Celtic and Inter Milan and losing 3-0 against Chelsea last Saturday.

But the Portuguese will have the chance to put things right against his old employers in two days' time as Milan face United in Wroclaw, Poland.

Alongside Tomori and Nkunku, he has put up for sale Youssouf Fofana, David Odogu, Pervis Estupinan, Santiago Gimenez and Philip Terracciano.

Ruben Amorim has told seven AC Milan players they no longer have a future at the club

Former Chelsea flop Christopher Nkunku will be shown the door, Daily Mail Sport understands

Tomori has had interest from Coventry City, managed by his old gaffer Frank Lampard, while Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest, and Villarreal are looking into Fofana.

Amorim held a crunch meeting with club bosses on Thursday to discuss his plans for the season, which inevitably involve instituting his five-at-the-back system which flopped so hard at Old Trafford.

He has accepted the task of transforming Milan's fortunes after they finished fifth last season in Serie A, which only qualified them for the Europa League.

Another of his tasks will be to sort out the future of winger Rafael Leao, who has been linked with the likes of Galatasaray and Leeds. He has been actively looking for a club.

Amorim is ready to embrace the challenge, and suggested that his task at the San Siro is even greater than his job at Old Trafford.

'I'm really very happy to be here, it's an honour to be the coach of Milan,' he said.

'Why did I choose Milan? If you read an old interview of mine you will understand it, for me a special club.

'It's a very big challenge that I accepted even if after the last one [at Manchester United] I told myself to accept a smaller one.

'Perhaps it is a greater challenge than the last. I'm proud to be here, we all are, me and my staff.

Fikayo Tomori is another of the eight stars who Amorim hopes will be saying arrivederci

'I'm at Milan to win, if you're Milan coach you have to have this mentality,' he added.

'I'm not naive, I know there's a lot of work to do, but if you're the Milan coach you have to play to win.'

Milan last won the Serie A title in 2021-22 under Stefano Pioli.

Last campaign they were managed by Massimiliano Allegri, who had been successful with them and Juventus previously but struggled to replicate those heights despite them having no European football.

Sports.title: 'If Henry Pollock wants to get involved, that offer is open': How new 'Ultimate Sevens' wants to shake up rugby - thanks to England's rising star, Sunderland's owners and the Hundred
Sports.content:
Henry Pollock wants to have a crack at playing sevens at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028. Transferring to the sport's shorter format will not be easy – especially in the wake of Matchroom Talent Agency head honcho Eddie Hearn’s demands for Pollock to be paid as much as a million pounds a year by his club employers Northampton Saints. But it is not impossible. There are options out there.

‘Should Henry want to get involved and do a bit of sevens preparation this year or next, that offer remains open,’ Barney Pascall, the managing director of a new sevens tournament aiming to shake up the rugby market, tells Daily Mail Sport.

‘It’s a great story that high-profile players in the sport want to play sevens. If Eddie wants to call, I’ll be ready.’

Pascall is the man heading up Ultimate Sevens, which will begin next month after investing ‘tens of millions’ in a competition which will take place in Madrid, Cardiff, Biarritz and London across four consecutive September weeks.

Rugby’s conservative ecosystem has been ripe for a new arrival for some time. R360, the proposed 15-a-side rebel league, failed to get off the ground amid rejection from the game’s existing authorities. But Ultimate Sevens wants to work alongside them, having spotted what Pascall sees as a gap in the market.

‘This is about elevating rugby sevens,’ he says. ‘We've been incredibly focused on being complementary to the ecosystem and there's a reason for that. It's because we can be.’

Henry Pollock’s representative Eddie Hearn has made it clear English rugby’s new sensation wants to have a crack at playing sevens at the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028

‘This is about elevating rugby sevens,’ says Ultimate Sevens founder Barney Pascall. ‘We've been incredibly focused on being complementary to the ecosystem. There's a reason for that'

2026 ULTIMATE SEVENS FIXTURES Sep 5 – Ontime Butarque Stadium, Madrid Sep 12 – Cardiff Arms Park, Cardiff Sep 18 – Parc des Sports Aguilera, Biarritz Sep 24 – Gtech Community Stadium, London

The funding needed to create Ultimate Sevens has not been insignificant. Its backers are BIA Sports Group (BSG), whose portfolio also includes Premier League side Sunderland.

It is aiming to capitalise on the growing popularity of rugby sevens, which has gone to a new level since France 15-a-side superstar Antoine Dupont won gold at the 2024 Paris Games, and also attract a new audience who may not be familiar with the sport at all.

Interestingly, in doing so, Ultimate Sevens has adopted a marketing slogan of ‘don’t call it rugby’ in a move similar to the one the England & Wales Cricket Board made when it created The Hundred. Like The Hundred, Ultimate Sevens has created new teams. Like The Hundred – which remains unpopular with cricket traditionalists – it wants to broaden rugby's appeal. It also plans to one day follow in the cricket competition’s footsteps by selling its sides to private investment.

‘It was an opportunity for us to be a bit punchy and challenge existing perceptions of rugby,’ Pascall says of his competition's commercial outlook. ‘It was a bit playful too. People who know sevens call it exactly that. If you're not in the rugby ecosystem, I think the slogan asks the question: “Well, if it's not rugby, what is it then?” That creates a hook and a level of interest.

‘I find it a compliment to even be in the same breath as The Hundred because they have tried and I think succeeded in bringing new audiences to cricket. We’re absolutely clear we want the integrity of the sport to remain at the heart of what we're doing. Sevens is a very credible sport. It’s existed since 1883. We want to add to that.’

Like The Hundred, Ultimate Sevens' six teams have both men’s and women’s outfits. The newly created sides are Albion Athletic, Atlantic Novas, Clan Taran, Foudre Bleue, Pacific Current and Sol Feroz. In time, Pascall wants to attract rugby’s biggest names such as Pollock. But season one will see the teams dominated by experienced sevens players.

Each of the four tournaments will see the men’s and women’s sides from the six teams play in a straight knockout format. All the action will be completed in one day, which is different to the traditional World Series Sevens circuit whose competing teams are nations. Matches will be ten minutes long with teams given the option of a 90-second tactical timeout.

One new innovation is around conversions. Tries scored under the posts will be worth an automatic seven points. If a try is scored wider out, teams can opt to take their additional kick from different, more challenging positions in a bid to earn more points. The range available is one, two or four points depending on the kick’s difficulty. Tickets for the London event at Brentford’s Gtech Community Stadium start at £30.

Rugby sevens' popularity has gone to a new level since France 15-a-side superstar Antoine Dupont won gold at the 2024 Paris Games

Like The Hundred, Ultimate Sevens has created new teams. Like The Hundred, it is open to selling its sides to private investment

‘The kicking rule adds another layer of entertainment and sporting jeopardy,’ says Pascall, who is assisted in the new competition’s creation by former England sevens captain Tom Mitchell as sport and innovation director. ‘This isn’t about a one-season wonder. This is a long-term play. This is about being around for many years to come. Younger and female audiences are increasingly introduced to rugby through sevens. That’s a powerful tool.’

For too long, rugby has badly needed investment as, outside the international 15-a-side game, it continues to experience financial difficulties. Fresh financing into PREM Rugby has been welcomed and so too should BIA’s arrival. Rugby as a whole will benefit if Ultimate Sevens can become a regular part of its landscape.

‘People ask me what success will look like,’ Pascall says. ‘I want people, in time, to know these players. That’s more of a qualitative than quantitative outcome, but if we get to that point, I think we'll have done something really special.

‘I absolutely believe this investment in the sport is going to be a positive energy for rugby, for Great Britain’s Olympic hopes, and for other countries around the world.’

Sports.title: 'We can achieve something really special': Man United boss Michael Carrick on aims for new season, the future of Marcus Rashford and why Andrey Santos is a 'dream'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick strides in to a plush conference room here at Carton House, the five-star spa hotel which has been home to Manchester United all week, with a big smile on his face. There's a lot for the United boss to be happy about, after all.

Back home his daughter, Louise, has collected her A-Level results and, here in Ireland, the late returns of Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Lisandro Martinez from the World Cup have added a fresh dynamism to a group who overcame Leeds on penalties at Croke Park only a few hours earlier.

Carrick, unlike predecessor Ruben Amorim, is level-headed. When the tough questions come his way, bosses are relaxed that Carrick won’t rock the boat like Amorim, who United face on Saturday in Poland when they play AC Milan, would do.

It’s why United were comfortable throwing open the doors to Amazon filmmakers for this season’s ‘All or Nothing’ behind-the-scenes documentary.

But don't mistake his calmness for ambivalence. Carrick is determined to win, too.

This has been a summer where top four rivals Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham have all spent north of £100million. Even newly-promoted Coventry and Ipswich have spent more than Manchester United. His message here, though, was crystal clear to those upstairs.

Man United boss Michael Carrick spoke to reporters on the club's pre-season trip to Ireland

United overcame Leeds on penalties at Croke Park in a friendly on Wednesday evening

'It can't be for the sake of it, but yeah, of course, we want to improve, we need to improve,’ Carrick says. ‘It's something that we're working towards, for sure.’

So far only Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow have arrived to strengthen the first-team squad. Tynan Thompson, an £8m pick-up from Tottenham, is seen as one for the future.

‘I have to say, Karl, Andrey, and Youri, are exactly what we hoped, exactly what we expected in every way,’ he adds.

‘Andrey, for such a young man to come in the way he's come in, his character, his personality is a dream. Literally, he’s a dream.’

But Carrick knows he needs more. United still need a left back - there have been two failed approaches for Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall this summer - and another central midfielder remains on the agenda.

By the time this conversation draws to a close, Carrick had referenced a need to ‘push’ in the transfer market four times.

'I think we've got a pretty good balance in all when you lay the squad out, but of course we would like more,’ he continued. ‘We would like more, we need to keep pushing for more.

‘There's one or two areas where we'd like to improve and we feel that there's the possibility to improve, but again, that needs to be something that we can do that makes us better and improves the group, whether that's quality or whether that's a little bit of depth. That's something we've got to manage. That's pretty obvious.’

Director of football Jason Wilcox is here in Ireland and remains in ‘constant communication’ with Carrick.

With a frugal approach to the summer so far, one which has so far seen them fail to land top target Elliot Anderson, Morgan Rogers, and others, can Manchester United seriously contend for a Premier League title this season?

‘I think you've got to have the belief, you've got to be going into the season thinking we can achieve something special,’ he says, reluctant to commit to any bold proclamation for the season ahead.

‘Don't be going into a season thinking this could be a struggle. We've got to set out to really achieve something.

‘We've definitely got the potential to achieve something really special. I'm not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that.

‘I'm not going to make any crazy predictions, but I think on the back of what we've done, I keep saying it, I think that gives us the confidence to move forward. How quickly we keep moving forward, that's the challenge.’

Carrick has been impressed with United's three summer signings so far, particularly Andrey Santos, but he wants more players to come through the door

Carrick was also full of praise for Marcus Rashford, who returned to the club on Sunday

There remains a question mark over Marcus Rashford and the prospect of his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt since 2024, when Amorim left him out in the cold, this weekend.

United have long been open to moving the £325,000-a-week attacker on as part of a plan to reduce the wage bill. They have also been in the market for a left winger all summer, with Crysencio Summerville among the targets, before he opted to move to Saudi Arabia.

Barcelona passed up on their buy option to sign Rashford, who is now back and training well.

‘He's a very good player, Marcus, and I think if you're going to have a career over 10 or 15 years, there's going to be times when things go in maybe a different direction,’ Carrick adds, before electing not to go as far as ruling out a potential move before the deadline.

‘I think there's ups and downs, and that doesn't judge you as a one-off kind of judgment. It's what happens over time, and now we're in a positive place as a group, and Marcus can offer us so much.

‘He has done (in the past), and he can do again, so in that respect, it's quite exciting.’

There’s a return for Kobbie Mainoo too. Carrick kept in touch with Mainoo all summer via text, checking in as he went through the entire World Cup without playing a minute.

There’s no concerns though. In fact, Carrick believes the Mainoo that has come back is ready to take the Premier League by storm.

'The biggest thing for me, Kobbie's in a really good place,’ he adds. ‘I think he feels that. He’s come back and he's come home and he's ready for a big season.’

But there are lingering concerns over squad depth with United competing back in Europe this season.

‘We're not naive, we know what we're going into,’ he concludes, pressed on the fact that United are facing the prospect of 15-20 more games than last season’s historically low total of 40.

‘But we feel we're a stronger group now than we were last season as well in many ways, so we've just got to capitalise on that.’

Sports.title: Ash Gardner breaks her silence on the collapse of her marriage after her wife demanded she be stripped of cricket leadership roles over alleged affair
Sports.content:
Ash Gardner breaks her silence on the collapse of her marriage after her wife demanded she be stripped of cricket leadership roles over alleged affair

Australian women's cricket vice-captain Ash Gardner has spoken out about swirling rumours of an affair with her younger teammate Georgia Voll following several weeks of silence.

Her ex-wife Monica Wright, 30, recently called out Cricket Australia's inaction over the potential conflict of interest arising from Gardner's involvement in selection and decision-making for the team.

Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg spoke about the situation on SEN radio on Thursday, saying he will bring in 'additional guardrails' for personal relationships among team members and staff.

This was followed by Gardner taking to Instagram to issue a statement on Thursday evening.

'While my separation from my wife is a personal matter, I understand my current relationship status needed to be addressed by Cricket Australia given my position as vice-captain,' Gardner wrote.

'I am grateful that the CA Board has chosen to support my continued leadership. I look forward to playing a strong role as a leader and providing the best possible support for my teammates in the season to come.

'I am grateful for the time Monica and I shared and sorry for the pain this has caused. I wish her nothing but happiness and success in the future.

'I won't be making any further public comment on this matter at this time and ask that the privacy of those involved is respected.'

Ash Gardner (left) who was appointed Australian co-vice captain on January 28 alongside Tahlia McGrath, married her long-term girlfriend Monica Wright (right) in April 2025

Greenberg said CA oversees any team decisions and relationships were a personal matter, but that he was aware there could be a 'perception' of a conflict of interest.

'In situations where there are some personal relationships (we will) make sure there are some additional guard rails so the perception of conflict (of interest) and I am talking about things like selection are handled appropriately.'

Gardner serves as vice-captain of Australia's women's team and captains the Sydney Sixers in the Women's Big Bash League.

Her ex-wife alleged Gardner had an affair with fellow Australian player Georgia Voll, 22, during the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup in India last year not long after the pair got married.

Wright questioned why Gardner had been permitted to retain senior leadership positions after Cricket Australia became aware of the situation.

'I think if you're privileged enough to represent your country and be seen as a role model, there's a responsibility to hold yourself to a high moral standard,' Wright told The Daily Telegraph.

'What I can't understand is why Cricket Australia hasn't said anything publicly.

'Does their silence mean they support the actions of Ashleigh and Georgia?

Gardner serves as vice-captain of Australia's women's team and captains the Sydney Sixers in the Women's Big Bash League

'Captains are expected to set the standard, and that kind of conduct falls well short of it.'

Wright also claimed the controversy would have been treated more seriously had it involved members of the Australian men's team.

She pointed to the treatment of late cricket legend Shane Warne, who was removed as Australia's men's vice-captain in 2000 following reports that he had sent explicit messages to a British nurse.

Gardner, who was appointed co-vice-captain on January 28 alongside Tahlia McGrath, married her long-term girlfriend Wright in April 2025.

However, just months later, things started to fall apart while the team was in India for the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup.

A team source with knowledge of the situation says there was some awkwardness during that tour when Wright flew over to India to see her wife.

'It was a little bit weird,' the insider said.

'It was like something was a little bit off with Ash, but we thought it was because of the pressure of the World Cup.'

Wright called for her to lose her leadership roles following allegations she had an affair with a younger teammate (pictured together in April 2025)

The insider said it was 'just horrible' when Wright arrived in India and Gardner didn't seem like herself.

Daily Mail understands that Gardner and Wright had a heart-to-heart after they returned to their Northern Beaches home in Sydney following the World Cup.

'When they got home, [Gardner] goes, 'Hey, look, can we talk?' and she sat her down,' the source claimed.

Gardner allegedly disclosed to Wright why things had been 'off' during her visit to India, leaving Wright 'shattered' and 'distraught'.

The conversation effectively marked the end of the couple's marriage.

Sports.title: Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr shows off the results of his cosmetic chin surgery on return to football
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr played his first game for Real Madrid this pre-season, in what was also his first outing since undergoing chin harmonisation surgery.

Real won 1-0 at LaLiga counterparts Deportivo La Coruna, thanks to a first-half stoppage-time goal from Brahim Diaz.

Vinicius Jr started the match before being replaced on 71 minutes for Jorge Cestero by new boss Jose Mourinho.

And while he sported a new look, the Brazilian still could enjoy the winning feeling as they won the Teresa Herrera Trophy.

The winger's facial operation came just weeks after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit by Norway.

According to Brazilian news outlet TMC, he headed straight to a dermatologist in Goiania when he landed back in his homeland following a short vacation in Europe with on-and-off girlfriend Virginia Fonseca.

Vinicius Jr played for Real Madrid for the first time since having chin harmonisation surgery

His return ended in success as Real beat Deportivo La Coruna to win the Teresa Herrera Trophy

A number of photos of the 26-year-old appearing unrecognisable after the op have gone viral on social media, with fans blown away by his remarkable transformation.

Vinicius Jr posed alongside Dr Alessandro Alarcao, who performed the surgery in Goiania, in another picture that emerged online.

He underwent the procedure, which 'uses fillers to sculpt the facial contour', to add more definition to his chin after being cruelly mocked over it during the World Cup.

It's been an eventful summer so far for Vinicius who was linked with a move away from the Spanish giants – with Arsenal a leading potential destination as he had 12 months left on his contract.

However, any notion about a move to the Premier League ended earlier this month when he signed a new six-year contract at Real until 2032.

Vinicius posted on Instagram: 'Eight years at the Bernabeu are too short.... Six more years, and then forever.'

The club said in a statement: 'Vinicius Jr has become one of the most important players in one of the most successful periods in our history.'

Vinicius Jr joined Real from Brazilian side Flamengo in 2018 and signed a contract extension three years ago.

The Brazil superstar looks completely different after undergoing chin harmonization surgery

🚨 Vini Jr at the clinic after his chin harmonization surgery. pic.twitter.com/WOq8OC0fgs — Madrid Zone (@theMadridZone) July 20, 2026

Vinicius jr is the first person in history to look like the AI version of himself 😭😭 pic.twitter.com/Sqhnd3M0bX — Anabella💙❤️ (@AnabellaMarvy) July 21, 2026

He and Brazil were dumped out of the World Cup at the last-16 stage after a 2-1 loss to Norway

He returned to the club last week for his first pre-season training session and medical assessment following his World Cup campaign with Brazil.

The prolific forward has scored 128 goals in 375 appearances for Real across all competitions, winning two Champions League titles, three La Ligas and a Copa del Rey.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

YouTube YouTube , which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
