World.title: Osun 2026: Adeleke’s campaign organisation asks INEC to send away Ebonyi REC from Osun
World.content:
The Imole Campaign Council, the campaign organisation of the Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke, has called on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately withdraw the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) for Ebonyi State, Pauline Ugoyenka, from Osun ahead of Saturday’s governorship election.

The council alleged that Ms Ugoyenka was in Osun despite not being listed among the RECs deployed to supervise the election, and demanded that INEC explain her presence and activities in the state.

The demand was contained in a statement issued on Thursday by the Chairman of the council’s Media and Publicity Committee, Bamidele Salam.

The council also raised concerns over alleged plans to use ballot papers and result sheets that were not specifically customised for the Osun governorship election.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to Mr Salam, the council received reports that Ms Ugoyenka was staying at Tees Continental Hotel on Laro Timileyin Street, Ayekale, Osogbo, Osun State.

He alleged that the Ebonyi REC, an information and communication technology expert, had previously stayed at Aenon Suites, where he claimed individuals allegedly brought in by the All Progressives Congress (APC) from Lagos and Abuja were also lodged.

The campaign council did not provide evidence to substantiate the allegations concerning the alleged hackers or their activities.

It, however, questioned the authority under which Ms Ugoyenka was allegedly operating in Osun.

The council said an INEC letter dated 3 August and addressed to RECs from 15 contributing states identified the states providing supervisory personnel for the Osun election, adding that Ebonyi was not included among them.

“So, who authorised Mrs Pauline Ugoyenka’s presence in Osun, and what exactly is she doing here?” the council asked.

“This is an election, not a covert operation. INEC must immediately explain her role, authority and activities in Osun and publish the full list of all officials deployed for the election.”

The council appealed to INEC’s national leadership to investigate what it described as the “unofficial” presence of the Ebonyi REC and ordered that she leave the state if she was not officially assigned duties there.

“We demand immediate exit of the Ebonyi REC as she was not posted here for any official duties and her presence constitutes grave danger to the electoral health of Osun people,” the statement said.

Mrs Ugoyenka could not be reached for comment at the time of filing this report.

Concern over electoral materials

Beyond the presence of the REC, the Adeleke campaign organisation also demanded clarification from INEC over alleged concerns about the customisation of ballot papers and result sheets for Saturday’s election.

The council said electoral materials intended for the Osun governorship election should be clearly customised, produced and verified for the poll.

“We also seek immediate clarification from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on why electoral materials meant specifically for the Osun governorship election would not be duly customised,” it said.

It warned that the campaign would oppose any process it believed could undermine the credibility of the election.

“Accord will not accept any arrangement capable of compromising the integrity, transparency or credibility of the August 15 election,” the council said.

The council urged INEC to provide immediate clarification and ensure that only properly customised ballot papers and result sheets produced and verified for the Osun governorship election are used.

“Anything short of this raises serious questions about the credibility of the process and will be firmly resisted,” it warned.

The Osun governorship election is scheduled for Saturday, 15 August, with Governor Adeleke seeking another term against other candidates, including the APC candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, and the African Democratic Congress candidate, Najeem Salam.

World.title: Osun 2026: Yiaga raises alarm over late movement of election materials, security risks
World.content:
Election observer organisation, Yiaga Africa, has raised concerns over the late movement of sensitive electoral materials ahead of Saturday’s Osun State governorship election, warning that the disruption to the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) logistics could create avoidable risks for the conduct of the poll.

The organisation said the situation requires additional security, closer oversight and contingency measures to ensure that the revised ballot papers and result sheets reach the 30 local government areas on time and are properly deployed to polling units before voting begins.

The Executive Director of Yiaga Africa, Samson Itodo, raised the concerns on Thursday at the organisation’s pre-election briefing in Osogbo, the state capital.

His warning came after INEC was forced to reprint ballot papers and result sheets following the late inclusion of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) candidate, Francis Ajala, in the election.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The commission said the revised materials would arrive in Osun on Thursday, 13 August, for onward distribution across the state.

“The Commission wishes to inform the public that the reproduced ballot papers will arrive in Osun State on Thursday, 13th August 2026, and will, same day, be moved to local government Aaea offices across the state, in line with its standard distribution procedure ahead of the election,” an earlier statement by the National Commissioner and Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee at INEC, Mohammed Haruna read.

The development has therefore compressed the time available for sorting and deployment of sensitive materials ahead of Saturday’s poll.

Mr Itodo said the late arrival had disrupted the commission’s original logistics plan and could result in electoral materials being transported at night in an already tense security environment.

“If as of this morning the revised materials have not arrived, and INEC has issued a statement to the effect that it will come in later, it has disrupted the logistics arrangement,” he said.

“We anticipate, and we are concerned that except extra measures are taken to ensure those materials get to the local government and their rights get activated early enough, then we might have a challenge.”

According to Mr Itodo, the timing of the materials’ arrival was particularly concerning because election logistics normally benefit from daylight movement and adequate preparation time.

He therefore called on security agencies to provide additional protection for election materials and personnel during the movement.

‘Readiness must be judged by performance’

Earlier, the Chairperson of the Osun Election Observation Mission of Yiaga Africa, Asmau Maikudi, said the election would be an important test of the commission’s operational readiness, the neutrality and professionalism of security agencies, the conduct of political parties and candidates, and the resilience of voters.

She described the election as the last major governorship election before the 2027 general election, adding that it would provide an opportunity to assess the implementation of key provisions introduced under the Electoral Act 2026.

These include the use of downloadable Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) for accreditation and the implementation of INEC’s regulations on electronic EC8A results and validation of polling-unit results within the results management process.

According to her, INEC’s preparations had advanced considerably, including PVC distribution, recruitment and training of election officials, mock accreditation, BVAS configuration and stakeholder engagement.

However, Mrs Maikudi, a former INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner, said preparations should ultimately be assessed by what happens when voters arrive at polling units.

She said INEC must avoid complacency and anticipate predictable points of failure, particularly around logistics, technology and results management.

“Security agencies bear a heightened responsibility to demonstrate neutrality, professionalism, and restraint. They must secure the election without becoming participants in it.”

This, according to Yiaga, is important given that the commission will deploy 4,427 BVAS devices across 3,763 polling units in the 30 local government areas.

A total of 2,339,233 registered voters are eligible to participate in the election.

BVAS problems raise another concern

Mrs Maikudi also raised concerns about the performance of BVAS during INEC’s mock accreditation exercise.

According to her, some devices temporarily failed to recognise voters’ fingerprints, facial features and older PVC records.

INEC, she said, attributed the facial verification failures to an excessively high compatibility threshold affecting older voter data, particularly records that had not been revalidated.

These technical problems, she stressed, must be resolved before Saturday because continued failures could lead to disenfranchisement, delays and tension at polling units.

“If unresolved, these failures could disenfranchise eligible voters, generate tension at polling units and undermine confidence in the credibility and legitimacy of the election,” she said.

Vote buying and violence remain threats

Beyond logistics, Yiaga Africa identified voter inducement as another significant risk to the election’s integrity.

Its observers documented the distribution of money and gift items by political actors. Although some of the activities were presented as social interventions or charitable assistance, the organisation said their timing raised concerns about possible attempts to influence voters.

Mrs Maikudi urged political parties, candidates and their supporters to refrain from vote buying and practices that compromise ballot secrecy.

She called for stronger coordination between security agencies, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) to arrest and prosecute those attempting to buy votes.

Yiaga to independently track results

To monitor the election, Yiaga Africa said it would deploy its Watching the Vote methodology using two complementary systems.

The first is its Process and Results Verification for Transparency (PRVT), formerly known as Parallel Vote Tabulation.

The organisation plans to deploy 300 stationary observers to a representative random sample of polling units, supported by 32 mobile observers covering all 30 local government areas.

The observers will collect information on accreditation, voting and counting and transmit the data for an independent assessment of the election.

The second mechanism is the Election Result Analysis Dashboard 2.0, known as ERAD 2.0.

The platform will track and independently audit polling-unit result sheets uploaded by INEC to its Election Results Viewing portal.

Yiaga Africa said ERAD would not collate results or declare a winner. Rather, it would monitor the availability, accessibility, timeliness and completeness of uploaded EC8A result sheets.

The organisation said the system would also provide an independent assessment of INEC’s electronic results management system.

The Osun election will therefore serve as a major test of whether the reforms and technologies introduced into Nigeria’s electoral system can withstand the pressure of a closely fought election.

World.title: Alia to Benue youths: Shun vices, seize opportunities
World.content:
Gov Hyacinth Alia of Benue State

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

Benue State Governor, Rev. Fr. Hyacinth Alia, has urged youths in the state to take advantage of opportunities provided by his administration, acquire relevant skills and shun social vices to enable them contribute meaningfully to the development of the state and the country.

Alia made the call on Thursday in Makurdi during the 2026 International Youth Day celebration.

The governor, who was represented by his deputy, Dr Samuel Ode, commended Benue youths for their support for his administration, describing them as critical partners in the development of the state.

He urged young people to take the lead in transforming society, stressing that their voices must be heard in matters concerning the future of the state and country.

“Young people are partners in building a virile society in every aspect. Since you possess the capacity to transform the nation, your voice must be heard loudly.

“Always ask questions, provoke challenges and seek solutions. The International Youth Day provides an opportunity to reflect and celebrate creativity and ingenuity in different areas, especially sports,” he said.

Alia said his administration had created an enabling environment for youths to thrive, noting that young people were already contributing to the state’s development in agriculture, artisanship, sports, technology and other sectors.

He urged them to embrace agriculture and technology, acquire relevant skills and participate actively in politics while rejecting social vices, irrespective of their backgrounds.

“You are strategically located at the heart of this administration. Government looks up to you towards building the society through innovation, farming and other ventures with the capacity to create jobs.

“We will continue to be youth-friendly and provide the enabling environment for our young people to strive and prosper,” the governor said.

Youths must unite against insecurity — Ojema

Earlier, the chairman of the occasion and member representing Apa/Agatu Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Ojotu Ojema, described youths as critical partners in development and custodians of Benue’s future.

Ojema challenged the youths to critically consider the kind of state they wanted to inherit and the leadership required to build it.

He identified unemployment as one of the major challenges confronting young people, while noting that insecurity remained a serious threat to peaceful coexistence.

The lawmaker urged Benue youths to rise above political, ethnic, religious and personal differences and unite against insecurity.

“Together, we can build a safer, more peaceful and more prosperous Benue where every young person can live, work and pursue their dreams without fear,” he said.

9,700 youths engaged through BIPC

In his welcome address, the Senior Special Assistant to the Governor on Youth Mobilisation and Illegal Levies, Terver Gbenda, disclosed that more than 90 per cent of political appointees and political officers in the state were youths.

Gbenda said more than 9,700 youths had been engaged directly and indirectly through the Benue Investment and Property Company Limited (BIPC), while 10,000 youths had received training in Information and Communication Technology (ICT).

He added that 2,000 people had been employed by the Benue State University Teaching Hospital (BSUTH), while 5,000 youths had benefited from the Alia Cares programme.

Gbenda appealed to the governor to appoint a youth as substantive Commissioner for Youth, Sports and Creativity.

He also urged young people not to allow themselves to be used and abandoned by politicians.

Also speaking, the Group Managing Director of BIPC, Dr Raymond Asemakaha, expressed concern over the growing number of graduates in the state, saying about 60,209 young people graduated from tertiary institutions in 2026 alone.

Asemakaha urged youths to acquire practical skills and become problem-solvers, stressing that skills development was essential to making them relevant in the emerging economy.

World.title: 3 African countries that qualify for UK Child Benefit
World.content:
Moving to the UK from African countries does not automatically mean you can claim Child Benefit. Applicants generally need to meet eligibility requirements, including living in the UK as their main home and having the right to reside.

However, UK rules provide specific exceptions for nationals of some countries.

Here are three African countries whose citizens may have a route to claiming Child Benefit under the rules.

1. Morocco

Moroccan nationals who are subject to UK immigration control may still be able to claim Child Benefit if they are working in the UK.

This is one of the specific exceptions to the general rule that people who are subject to immigration control cannot claim Child Benefit.

2. Tunisia

Tunisian nationals may also qualify for the same exception if they are working in the UK.

The UK government specifically lists Tunisia among the countries whose citizens can claim Child Benefit despite being subject to immigration control, provided they meet the relevant conditions.

3. Mauritius

Mauritius is included among the countries that have an agreement with the UK covering Child Benefit.

This means Mauritian nationals may have eligibility under the terms of the agreement, although they still need to meet the applicable conditions before making a claim.

Other key requirements

Being from one of these countries does not automatically guarantee payment. In general, people moving to the UK must show that they live in the UK as their main home and have the right to reside.

People with settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme can also qualify, while those with pre-settled status may need to meet additional requirements.

The rules can also differ where a child lives outside the UK, particularly where the child lives in an EU country, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein.

Anyone considering a claim should check the latest UK government eligibility rules before applying.

World.title: Nigeria not prone to earthquakes — NGSA
World.content:
Nigeria Flag

…urges adherence to building codes for heavy infrastructure

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA: The Nigerian Geological Survey Agency (NGSA) has allayed fears over the recent earth tremor in Abuja, saying Nigeria is not prone to earthquakes.

The Director-General of the agency, Prof. Olusegun Ige, stated this on Thursday at a press conference at the NGSA headquarters in Abuja, where he provided details of the tremor recorded in the Federal Capital Territory on August 4, 2026.

Ige explained that the incident was a low-magnitude earth tremor and not an earthquake, adding that it posed no threat to lives and property.

He said the agency considered it necessary to sensitise Nigerians and provide a detailed report on the incident to dispel concerns arising from the tremor.

The NGSA boss disclosed that the shock was felt at the logistics unit of the Defence Intelligence Agency, Mambila Barracks, Asokoro, parts of the NNPC Towers and some buildings in the Central Business District.

According to him, the event was recorded at the NGSA seismic monitoring station at 11:23:27 a.m., local time, at a distance of about four kilometres from the epicentre.

Ige said the agency continued monitoring seismic activity for more than five days after the incident, adding that the waveform signals recorded by the seismogram showed only baseline noise, indicating that the tremor had completely subsided.

He said the NGSA monitoring team subsequently conducted a follow-up assessment of areas where the tremor was felt to document the experiences and determine whether there were any effects.

The areas visited included the Defence Intelligence Agency at Mambila Barracks, Asokoro, NNPC Towers and some buildings within the CBD.

“In all the buildings inspected by the monitoring team, there was absolutely no evidence of any structural damage, nor was there any report of injury or serious discomfort from any person living in any of the affected areas,” he said.

According to Ige, analysis of the waveform and seismic signals showed that the tremor was a low-moment event, with low amplitude and a very brief shock period lasting about five seconds from an originating depth of less than one kilometre.

He said the possible cause was an intra-plate response to accumulated stresses that may have originated in the deeper crust and were aided by the reactivation of northeast-southwest and northwest-southeast conjugate sets of strike-slip faults running through Nigeria.

He explained that the movement of the faults could trigger minor tremors, which dissipate through secondary fractures to points of impact.

“NGSA maintains that the very low magnitude and isolated nature of the tremor make it a micro-event that lacks the required energy to damage building foundations, cause cracks on walls or trigger secondary hazards, and therefore poses no threat to lives and properties, except for the discomfort of the shake,” Ige said.

He stressed that seismic activity occurred in Nigeria regularly, although most events were too weak to be felt by residents.

“Every day we have seismicity going on. It’s not all of them that we feel,” he said.

NGSA seeks more monitoring stations

Ige, however, called for improved monitoring of seismic activities across the country, noting that the agency currently operates only five monitoring stations.

He urged the Federal Government to expand the number of NGSA monitoring stations and provide adequate logistics and funding to facilitate effective monitoring and accurate analysis of seismic events.

He also called on the Ministry of Solid Minerals Development to require major quarry and mining operators to install seismic monitoring equipment at their sites to complement government monitoring stations.

On infrastructure, the NGSA boss urged government to strengthen enforcement of standard seismic building codes for heavy infrastructure and industrial projects in Abuja and other cities.

Agency gives emergency contact

Ige also urged Nigerians to promptly report unusual earth movements to the agency.

He gave the NGSA customer service number as 0913 944 2811, which he said members of the public could call to report earth movements and seek information.

World.title: Leicester City’s owners put club up for sale – Reports
World.content:
Former Premier League champions Leicester have been put up for sale by the club’s Thai owners, according to reports on Thursday.

Just 10 years after their fairytale Premier League title triumph, Leicester will play in English football’s third tier for only the second time in their history this season.

The Foxes, who won their first FA Cup in 2021, have endured a dire period featuring successive relegations from the Premier League in 2025 and the Championship in 2026.

Last season, they were docked six points after breaching the Football League’s profit and sustainability rules, sparking their slump into League One.

A BBC report on Thursday said Leicester’s Thai owners King Power — run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family — have commissioned a leading US investment bank to help find a buyer, with the club’s assets said to be listed at more than £200 million ($269 million).

King Power bought Leicester in a £35 million deal in 2010.

Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman following the death of his father Vichai in a helicopter crash outside the club’s King Power Stadium in 2019.

Following last season’s relegation, Aiyawatt said he should shoulder the “blame” for the club’s predicament but also stressed the “structure will change”.

Russell Martin’s side kick off their promotion bid with a trip to Notts County on Saturday.

AFP

World.title: Police officer killed as suspected armed herders attack checkpoint in Benue
World.content:
Stock image

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

A Police personnel has reportedly been killed in a suspected armed herders’ attack on a joint police and military checkpoint in Uzer community, Logo Local Government Area (LGA), of Benue State.

It was gathered that the incident occurred when the attackers stormed the security checkpoint, prompting troops of Sector 1, Operation Whirl Stroke, stationed in Ayilamo, and a team of mobile policemen to respond.

According to a local source, the attackers took to their heels and disappeared into the nearby bushes on sighting the advancing troops.

He said the “security personnel subsequently launched a follow-up operation in the area to track the fleeing assailants and restore normalcy.

“During the operation, the troops reportedly recovered the body of a Police Inspector who was killed during the attack,” he said.

He stated that the remains of the slain officer were deposited at the Ayilamo Hospital mortuary for autopsy and other necessary procedures.

Confirming the incident, the Benue State Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO, DSP Peter Aondongu, said the command lost one of its personnel in the attack.

“I can confirm that we lost one of our officers in Ayilamo, as the report stated. Operations in that axis are still ongoing to bring the perpetrators to book,” Aondongu said.

Meanwhile, it was gathered that security forces have intensified patrols and surveillance around Uzer, Ayilamo and other border communities in Logo LGA following the attack.

World.title: ‘This was my World Cup’ says Somali ref after UEFA Super Cup
World.content:
Omar Artan

Somali referee Omar Artan described taking charge of Wednesday’s UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa in Salzburg as his “World Cup”.

The 34-year-old was denied the chance to referee at the World Cup itself after being refused entry to the United States.

He was turned away on arrival at Miami International Airport, despite being part of the panel of referees selected by FIFA for the tournament.

In a post on X on Thursday, UEFA shared a photo showing a match ball from Wednesday’s match on which Artan had written: “This was my World Cup”.

UEFA added the caption: “A special Super Cup souvenir from Omar Artan”.

UEFA extended the invitation for Artan to officiate the Super Cup, which PSG won 2-1, after he was blocked in Miami.

A US State Department official told AFP at the time that the referee was “associated with suspected members of terrorist organizations”, therefore “making the traveler ineligible for admission to the United States”.

These allegations were rejected by the referee and caused outrage in Somalia, where Artan was welcomed as a hero on his return.

On Thursday, Artan used his Instagram account to thank UEFA and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“Thanks to everyone who made this possible,” he posted.

“Especially to UEFA for giving me the trust and opportunity and who welcomed me (to) their continent with open arms.

“My own confederation, CAF, for the support and making this possible.”

UEFA justified its decision to appoint Artan by referring to the agreement it signed at the end of April with CAF to encourage cooperation between the two confederations.

But it is also a political gesture by UEFA, which is regularly critical of FIFA, and one that takes on even greater significance in light of the conflict that has pitted the European body against FIFA president Gianni Infantino for the past few weeks, centring on the abandoned plan to open up the World Cup to private investors.

The plan’s failure was largely due to the revolt led by UEFA, which continues to wield the threat of a boycott of FIFA tournaments -– including the World Cups -– in an attempt to force Infantino to step down.

AFP

World.title: FG demands citizen-security alliance
World.content:
Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris

By Joseph Erunke, Abuja

The Federal Government has called for stronger collaboration among security agencies, government institutions, communities, the media and citizens to address Nigeria’s security challenges.

Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, made the call in Abuja on Thursday, saying the country’s security challenges could no longer be tackled through military force alone.

Idris spoke when the Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, Maj.-Gen. Adeyinka Famadewa (retd.), paid a courtesy visit to the Ministry of Information and National Orientation.

He described the visit as an opportunity to strengthen cooperation between the ministry and the newly established Office of the Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, particularly in the area of communicating security policies and initiatives to Nigerians.

The minister said sustainable peace and national development depended on closer coordination among relevant stakeholders and active citizen participation in the country’s security architecture.

“Peace and security are essential elements; in fact, they are the building blocks of any development that can happen anywhere,” he said.

Idris said deploying more force alone would not resolve the nation’s security challenges, stressing the need for stronger collaboration between security agencies and citizens.

“You cannot shoot yourself out of this problem. Security requires collaboration between the security agencies, the armed forces and the general public,” he said.

He urged the armed forces and other security agencies to strengthen their engagement with communities, while government institutions and the media should ensure that Nigerians receive credible, timely and accurate information.

The minister said the grassroots presence of the National Orientation Agency and other agencies under his ministry could be leveraged to strengthen community resilience, promote responsible citizenship and improve public understanding of national security initiatives.

He also identified fake news, misinformation and disinformation as emerging threats to national security, warning that false information could undermine public confidence, heighten tensions and complicate efforts to maintain peace.

Idris therefore called for greater media and information literacy as well as responsible communication by all stakeholders.

Information key to homeland security — Famadewa

Speaking earlier, Famadewa said his visit was aimed at establishing a stronger working relationship with the ministry, stressing that information and public enlightenment had become indispensable to modern homeland security.

He said the new office would focus on strengthening intelligence and surveillance, improving border security, identifying security threats and developing effective protocols for reporting and responding to crises.

Famadewa said information management had become increasingly important in contemporary security operations, particularly with the rapid spread of narratives through digital platforms.

“Information is key in asymmetric warfare. The first person to speak wins, and we cannot sit back and allow others to shape perception for us,” he said.

He stressed the need for government to communicate swiftly and effectively during security incidents to prevent misinformation from filling information gaps and shaping public perception.

Responding, Idris assured the Special Adviser of the ministry’s full cooperation, saying stronger institutional coordination and effective public communication would be critical to the success of the homeland security strategy.

He said active citizen participation, improved information management and closer collaboration among security agencies and communities would complement the Federal Government’s efforts to realise President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s vision of a safer, more peaceful and prosperous Nigeria.

World.title: US court dismisses Trump admin lawsuit over alleged Harvard antisemitism
World.content:
Harvard

A US federal court on Thursday threw out a Trump administration lawsuit against Harvard University which accused the prestigious institution of permitting antisemitism during pro-Palestinian rallies on campus.

District Judge Richard Stearns in Boston ruled that the government had not sufficiently proven that Harvard breached a Civil Rights Act provision that bars discrimination along race, nationality and other lines.

President Donald Trump has launched a campaign against major American universities, accusing them of giving free rein on their campuses to pro-Palestinian movements in the face of the Israeli offensive in the Gaza Strip.

In its complaint filed in March, the Department of Justice said Harvard “faculty and leadership turned a blind eye to antisemitism and discrimination against Jews and Israelis.”

“Harvard let anti-Israeli demonstrators occupy its libraries. Harvard allowed an anti-Israeli encampment to persist for twenty days in violation of university policy,” it said.

But Judge Stearns, who granted a Harvard request to dismiss the lawsuit, said the incidents raised by the Trump administration were “too isolated and episodic” to prove noncompliance with the Civil Rights Act.

The decision marks a blow to Trump’s attacks against the oldest university in the United States.

His administration has separately moved to freeze billions of dollars of funding for Harvard for allegedly tolerating antisemitism and harboring liberal bias.

Last September, a federal judge ruled that move largely unlawful and ordered the funds be restored.

AFP

World.title: Osun 2026: Deputy Senate President Urges Support for Oyebamiji, Says APC’s Victory Will Return State to Political Mainstream
World.content:
Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, has urged the people of Osun State to vote for the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji (AMBO), to return the state to Nigeria’s political mainstream for the development of the state.

Speaking during the grand campaign mega rally of the APC ahead of Saturday’s election at the Freedom Park, Osogbo, Osun State, on Thursday, Senator Barau said two key things are hindering the development of the state.

Senator Barau, who is the Secretary of the national campaign council of the APC for the Osun Governorship Election, said the first challenge hindering the development of the state was a lack of good leadership to lead the path for its development.

Amid a mammoth crowd that thronged the venue of the campaign rally, he said the candidate of the APC possesses the capacity to turn around the fortunes of the state for the benefit of its people.

“Osun State is a state that has enormous potential and enormous resources, both natural and human.

“But the problem is that it doesn’t have a governor to harness these resources. What is needed at this moment is to elect APC’s AMBO, who has the requisite pedigree and the requisite background to harness these resources,” he said.

He added that, “Apart from that, there’s one thing that is also lacking. Osun State is not within the mainstream of Nigerian politics. What is needed at this stage is to bring Osun State into the mainstream of Nigerian politics.

“As we speak, we have 31 states being governed by the APC. But Osun is isolated. So, you (voters) need to go out on Saturday to bring Osun into the equation of our national politics by voting for APC.

“When you do that, Osun State will gain and develop. Please, on Saturday, go out there and vote for APC’s candidate. By doing so, you have voted for development and for infrastructure.”

As a firm believer in issue-based politics and the sanctity of human life, he urged the people of the state to shun any issue capable of causing crisis before, during and after the election.

World.title: National Policing Bill: FG Extends Deadline For Submission of Memoranda, Position Papers By Eight Days
World.content:
* Submission now to close Friday, August 21

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill set up by President Bola Tinubu has extended the deadline for the submission of memoranda and position papers on the proposed legislation by eight days.

The submission of the proposed bill’s memo and position papers initially billed to close by 5pm on Thursday, August 13, 2026 will now end by Friday, August 21, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. West Africa Time (WAT).

According to a statement issued on Thursday by the Chief of Staff to the President, who also doubles as Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon Femi Gbajabiamila, the extension is intended to provide stakeholders with additional time for thorough preparation and ensure that interested individuals, institutions and organisations have adequate opportunity to make well-considered contributions to the proposed legislation.

The release stated that the Presidential Working Group is committed to ensuring that the process of developing the National Policing Bill benefits from broad consultation and the informed perspectives of Nigerians and relevant stakeholders.

The proposed legislation, Gbajabiamila further explained, is intended to provide the operational, administrative, institutional and funding framework necessary for an effective policing architecture that responds to Nigeria’s evolving security needs, while providing appropriate safeguards for accountability, professionalism and the protection of citizens’ rights.

Gbajabiamila, in the release, stated inter alia: “Given the significance of the proposed reform to the future of policing and internal security in Nigeria, the Working Group considers it important that stakeholders are afforded more opportunity to make substantive and technically sound contributions to the process.

“Accordingly, legal practitioners, civil society organisations, security sector professionals, state governments, professional bodies, academics, experts and interested members of the public are encouraged to take advantage of the extended period to submit their memoranda and position papers. All submissions must be made on or before 5:00 p.m. WAT on Friday, August 21, 2026, exclusively through the official National Policing Bill portal, nationalpolicingbill.com.

“The Working Group recognises that developing an effective policing framework requires careful consideration of critical issues, including sustainable funding, command and control structures, recruitment and training standards, operational jurisdiction, inter-agency coordination, accountability mechanisms and safeguards against political interference or abuse.

“These considerations underscore the importance of robust stakeholder engagement in developing a framework that is effective, accountable, sustainable and responsive to the peculiar security needs of communities across the Federation.

“At the conclusion of its assignment, the Presidential Working Group will present a final, implementation-ready draft of the National Policing Bill for onward legislative processing.

“The Presidential Working Group appreciates stakeholders who have already made submissions and encourages others intending to participate in this important national process to take advantage of the extension.”

Gbajabiamila had on Monday, August 3, in a bid to encourage public participation, announced an open call for memoranda and position papers from Nigerians, civil society organisations, professional bodies, security institutions and other stakeholders.

The CoS to the president, who spoke with newsmen at the end of the Group’s meeting at the State House, Abuja, disclosed that a dedicated portal, nationalpolicingbill.com, had gone live to receive submissions, with plans for migration to a government domain.

“The whole idea behind state policing is for you and I and everybody out there to take ownership. No matter your station in life, you have an opportunity to contribute meaningfully,” he said.

World.title: Katsina Moves to Block Financial Leakages, Tightens TSA Operations
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The Katsina State Government has commenced moves to plug financial leakages and strengthen the implementation of the Treasury Single Account (TSA) system as part of efforts to improve accountability, transparency and efficiency in the management of the state’s public funds.

The state Commissioner for Finance, Alhaji Bello Hussaini Kagara, disclosed this Thursday at a one-day follow-up capacity-building workshop on TSA implementation organised by his ministry for accountants and initiators in the state.

He charged the accountants and other financial officers in the state to uphold high ethical standards and ensure efficient implementation of the treasury single account system.

He explained that the training was aimed at strengthening the capacity of financial officers, identifying operational gaps and improving the efficiency and transparency of the state’s financial management system.

He stressed the need for the state financial officers to identify issues surrounding payment processes, checks and balances, appropriations and the handling of payment vouchers (PVs), noting that gaps in these areas could undermine the effectiveness of the TSA system.

He explained that previous assessments had revealed instances where funds were transferred into accounts that were not intended to receive them, warning that such loopholes must be identified and addressed to safeguard government resources.

Kagara urged the participants, whom he described as critical operators of the system, to unravel challenges affecting the TSA operations and make practical recommendations that would help the state government to improve its financial management processes.

He said the state government was committed to periodic training of its financial officers to enable them update their knowledge, improve their skills and adapt to emerging developments in public financial management.

“We cannot have a perfect operation, but what we want is an efficient system. All we want to do is to ensure that we put in our best and do the best we can,” the commissioner said.

He assured the participants that recommendations arising from the workshop would be given serious consideration by the state government, adding that their contributions were important to improving the operational success of the TSA system.

The commissioner further urged the participants to demonstrate ethical competence, obedience to established procedures, self-reliance and the willingness to ask questions whenever necessary.

Kagara said the government expected the participants to translate the knowledge acquired from the training into improved performance and greater accountability in the discharge of their responsibilities.

World.title: Niger Pilgrims Board Set September 20 As Deadline For Payment of 2027 Hajj Deposits
World.content:
Laleye Dipo in Minna

The Niger State Pilgrims Welfare Board has set September 20, this year for the payment of deposits by potential 2027 Hajj pilgrims.

A statement by the Public Relations Officer of the Board, Hajia Lubabatu Mohammed Kusherki, in Minna said the deadline followed a similar action taken by the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON).

NAHCONs action, she said, is in line with a decision by the Saudi Arabia Ministry of Hajj and Umrah.

Hajia Kusherki said the Saudi authority has mandated all participating countries to upload the biodata of their intending pilgrims onto the “NUSUK MASAR platform on or before September 20, 2026, based on slots allocated to each country.

According to her, NAHCON has said that Nigeria is expected to upload details of approximately 50,000 intending pilgrim within the stipulated period.

Kusherki said the board warned that failure of intending pilgrims to register and make payment before the deadline could result in the forfeiture of allocated slots for the 2027 pilgrimage.

“The board remains committed to providing all necessary guidance and support to intending pilgrims throughout the registration process,” she stated.

Kusherki urged Intending pilgrims to visit the Niger State Pilgrims’ Welfare Board Office in Minna or designated local government centres for registration and further inquiries.

World.title: Katsina, Security Chiefs, Intensify War Against Banditry, Terrorism
World.content:
• Seek stronger collaboration to tackle scourge

Francis Sardauna in Katsina

Security chiefs, Katsina State Government and other stakeholders have called for stronger synergy, intelligence sharing and coordinated operations among security agencies to defeat terrorism, banditry and other criminal activities threatening the North-west region of the country.

The call was made at the North-west Conference of State Directors of Security, held in Katsina on Thursday, with the theme ‘Unite Against Terror.’

Speaking at the conference, the Katsina State Director of the Department of State Services (DSS), Alhassan Iliyasu, said collaboration among security agencies, communities and other stakeholders to effectively tackle terrorism, banditry and other criminal activities in the region is vital.

He said the fight against terrorism and banditry could not be won by security agencies alone, stressing that every member of the society had a role to play in providing useful information and supporting security operations to tackle the region’s evolving security challenges.

He added that the conference provided an opportunity for heads of intelligence-led organisations and security agencies across the region to review emerging threats, share experiences and develop renewed strategies for curbing banditry and related criminal activities.

Iliyasu said: “The purpose of this conference is for us to come together, review the nitty-gritty of the security challenges, come up with renewed strategies and scale up our countermeasures.”

He noted that the collaboration among security agencies, community-based security structures, vigilante groups and other stakeholders would significantly improve responses to security threats across the North-west region of the country.

He commended the Director-General of the DSS, Mr Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi, for providing renewed direction for the Service and creating opportunities to strengthen its intelligence and tactical capabilities.

On his part, the Commander, 17 Brigade, Nigerian Army, Katsina, Brigadier-general Ishaya Ibrahim, explained that the synergy among security agencies was no longer an advantage but an imperative in confronting the evolving and borderless nature of terrorism.

He disclosed that military firepower and territorial operations alone could not defeat terrorists, adding that actionable intelligence remained critical to the success of military operations.

He said terrorists exploit gaps in information, coordination and trust, hence the need for the nation’s security agencies to bridge such gaps through real-time intelligence sharing, joint operational planning and mutual support.

In his opening remarks, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda said Katsina State had recorded significant improvements in its security challenges through a combination of both kinetic and non-kinetic measures.

Represented by his Deputy, Faruk Lawal, the governor attributed the security improvement in the state to the cooperation between conventional security agencies and the state’s home-grown security initiative, the Community Watch Corps.

He added that the state government had also “invested heavily” in non-kinetic interventions aimed at addressing some of the socio-economic factors that could fuel insecurity in the state.

He, therefore, appealed to security agencies and the media to be strategic in communicating security-related developments, warning against reports that could inadvertently amplify the activities of bandits and other criminal elements.

Radda urged the media to support security efforts by providing responsible coverage capable of boosting public confidence and the morale of security personnel operating in the North-west region of the country.

World.title: NHRC Cautions Against Hate Speech Ahead of 2027 Polls
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has issued a stark warning that escalating hate speech, intimidation, incitement and divisive political rhetoric could plunge Nigeria into violence and chaos ahead of the 2027 general election.

The commission said on Thursday that inflammatory statements by political and public figures were increasingly threatening human dignity, peaceful coexistence and citizens’ right to participate freely in the democratic process.

Speaking during a press conference at the NHRC headquarters in Abuja, the Executive Secretary of the commission, Chief Tony Ojukwu, said Nigeria must act decisively before dangerous rhetoric translates into violence.

Ojukwu specifically cited statements attributed to Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir and Senator Francis Fadahunsi, saying the commission considered some of the comments to have crossed “the red line for decency” and to have the potential to denigrate individuals or groups, deepen divisions and heighten tensions.

He stressed, however, that the intervention was not targeted at any political party, religious organisation, ethnic group or individual, but was a human-rights response designed to protect the dignity and equal worth of Nigerians.

“Freedom of expression is a fundamental human right. However, freedom of expression carries responsibilities,” Ojukwu said, warning that the right did not constitute a licence to incite violence, promote hatred, dehumanise others or deliberately provoke hostility against individuals or communities.

The NHRC boss warned that hate speech must not be dismissed as ordinary political rhetoric, arguing that language portraying people or communities as enemies, inferior, dangerous or undeserving of protection could fuel discrimination, exclusion, intimidation and violence.

According to him, the consequences could include attacks on political opponents and voters, restrictions on civic participation, displacement and insecurity, deepening ethnic and religious tensions, and a loss of public confidence in democratic institutions.

Ojukwu invoked the painful lessons of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda, noting that sustained propaganda, denigration, dehumanisation and incitement could create an environment in which discrimination and violence become increasingly acceptable.

While stressing that Nigeria was not Rwanda, he said the lesson from history was universal and should compel authorities and citizens to confront dangerous narratives before they escalated.

“The situation, if unchecked, could escalate circumstances into uncontrolled violence and chaos. God forbid,” he said.

He maintained that prevention was a fundamental human-rights obligation, adding that government had the primary responsibility under national and international law to prevent violence and protect citizens.

The commission therefore called for early identification of dangerous narratives, responsible public communication and lawful accountability for those who cross established legal boundaries.

With the 2027 elections approaching, the NHRC urged political actors to ensure that campaigns revolve around policies, programmes, competence and records of service rather than ethnic hostility, religious antagonism and personal attacks.

The commission warned that unchecked divisive rhetoric could intimidate voters, suppress political participation and trigger violence before, during and after the elections.

It also cautioned that communities that feel targeted or threatened could become vulnerable to insecurity and displacement, while prolonged political hostility could leave lasting social fractures long after the elections have ended.

Ojukwu said the protection of human rights and prevention of election-related violence must consequently be treated as complementary objectives.

The NHRC called on political parties to rein in their members and strengthen internal mechanisms for preventing and sanctioning inflammatory and intimidating rhetoric.

Religious, traditional and community leaders were similarly urged to use their influence to promote tolerance, peace and mutual respect rather than hatred, violence and division.

The commission also placed responsibility on the media, warning journalists and media organisations against becoming channels for amplifying inflammatory statements.

It urged the media to maintain professional and ethical standards and ensure that potentially harmful content was reported with context, verification and proper public-interest considerations.

Social media users and digital platforms, the commission added, must also exercise greater responsibility, particularly in verifying information before sharing material capable of provoking hostility or violence.

Law enforcement agencies were urged to respond appropriately to credible cases involving incitement, threats, intimidation and other unlawful conduct, while ensuring that investigations and prosecutions comply with the Constitution, due process and fundamental rights.

World.title: Osun Election: Fadaunsi Accuses Adeleke of Importing Violence into Osun East While Ede is Peaceful
World.content:
Alleges 30 APC members killed within a month

Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

Senator representing Osun East Senatorial District, Femi Fadahunsi, yesterday accused the Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, of allegedly importing political violence and terrorism into the senatorial district ahead of Saturday’s governorship election.

It would be recalled that Adeleke called for arrest of Fadahunsi over reported incitement against supporters of Accord Party.

Meanwhile, Fadahunsi, who spoke at a press conference in Osogbo yesterday, alleged that more than 40 people had been killed in the district in the last one year, accusing the state government of failing to prevent the violence.

He further alleged that 30 members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) had been killed within the last month, claiming that the violence was designed to intimidate opposition supporters and prevent them from coming out to vote.

According to him, “Adeleke created terrorism from Ede into Osun East, the stronghold of APC, for us to be destabilised, so that people will not go out en masse to cast their votes.”

Fadahunsi, who chronicled several incidents of violence in Ijesa land, alleged that four people were killed while 16 others sustained gunshot injuries during the crisis over the control of local government administration.

He also referred to the violence recorded in Esa-Oke in April 2025, alleging that four people were killed while 12 others sustained gunshot wounds.

He accused unnamed government officials and political allies of being behind some of the incidents, alleging that the violence was connected to political interests in the area.

The senator further alleged that members of the Amotekun Corps killed four of his constituents in Akinlalu, leaving six others critically injured.

He said, “In the last one year, over 40 people were killed in the district unchecked by either the police or the governor.”

Fadahunsi also alleged that some individuals with links to cult groups had been used to perpetrate violence in Ijesa land.

He alleged that four people were killed in Ilesa during the local government control crisis and that several others were wounded.

The senator also referred to the death of a suspected cultist, identified as Rogba, alleging that he had been linked to previous killings before he was killed by a rival cult group.

Fadahunsi said the situation had become particularly worrisome ahead of the August 15 election, alleging that opposition supporters had been targeted.

He claimed that 12 APC members were killed within 24 hours in recent attacks, while several others sustained injuries.

“Go to Wesley Guild, there are corpses everywhere. The former Speaker, Timothy Owoeye, and Remi Omowaiye are in hospital instead of planning for the election,” he said.

He alleged that the violence was aimed at creating fear among voters in Osun East, while claiming that Ede, the governor’s home town, remained peaceful.

“We observed that it is only Osun East that this governor from Ede is terrorising,” he said.

“Adeleke created terrorism from Ede into Osun East, the stronghold of APC for us to be destabilised, so that people will not go out en masse to cast their votes.”

Fadahunsi said he had led a protest to the palace of the Owa Obokun of Ijesaland to draw attention to what he described as politically motivated killings in the area.

He urged traditional rulers and security agencies to ensure that voters were not intimidated or prevented from exercising their franchise.

“I want to urge the security agencies to ensure arrest of anyone who may want to prevent our people from coming out en masse,” he said.

The senator also accused the Director-General of the Accord Party campaign council, Senator Oyewumi Iyiola, of intervening in a case involving a suspect allegedly linked to the killing of Remi Abass in Irewole.

He questioned the justification for what he described as selective demands for justice.

“If they want to return to power by force, it is not possible. Let us do our election free and fair, not by introducing terrorism in my district to chase away the people,” Fadahunsi said.

He also dismissed allegations by Governor Adeleke against security agencies and the APC, arguing that such accusations suggested that the governor was apprehensive about the outcome of the election.

“If Governor Adeleke is accusing police, army, APC and others, then he is afraid of losing,” he said.

Fadahunsi urged residents of Osun East to remain resolute and participate in the election, assuring APC supporters that their votes would determine the outcome.

He said the APC governorship candidate, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji (AMBO), would emerge victorious in the election.

“By August 15, when all these have ended, let them be going around to be talking grammar where they feel. The people of Osun State have understood the game that they are devilish and they are ready to reject them. AMBO will win the governorship race,” he said.

World.title: Igbere Traditional Rulers Back Dep. Speaker Kalu’s Bid for Another Term, Describe His Legislative Service as Outstanding
World.content:
Igbere traditional rulers in Bende Local Government of Abia State have thrown their weight behind the 2027 bid of the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu to return to the parliament.

Speaking on behalf of the traditional rulers during Kalu’s courtesy call in the course of his “Meet Your Constituents” tour to the traditional rulers on Wednesday in Igbere, His Royal Majesty (HRM) Eze Joseph Ukaoha Anyanta applauded Kalu for his outstanding legislative service, recalling that no one before him since the return of democracy in 1999 matched his service in terms of quality representation, legislative and infrastructure records.

The traditional rulers also gave their royal blessings to the Deputy Speaker, pledging their unflinching support for his legislative deliveries.

He said: “Yours is an outstanding legislative service, the best since 1999. Yours is different and we are seeing it all over the place. We are giving you our support so that you can do your work in peace.

“Anyone who wishes you evil will not succeed. We pray to God to give you the grace to achieve your lofty dreams for Bende. Whatever we can do to make this a reality, we will do it.”

Similarly, the women, youth of Igbere and non indigenes resident in Igbere also pledged their support for the Deputy Speaker, commending him for quality representation so far.

At Ibina Hall in Onu-Ibina Igbere, the women gathered in their numbers, singing and dancing in solidarity with the Deputy Speaker’s bid.

The same was the situation at Amankalu Igbere where the non indigenes resident in the town also gave their blessings to the Deputy Speaker.

The people lauded Kalu for attracting numerous projects to Bende, noting that all the 13 electoral wards of the constituency have witnessed unprecedented improvement in roads infrastructure, construction and renovation of school building amongst other people-oriented projects.

World.title: Long SASSA queues highlight growing demand for social grants
World.content:
Social Development Minister Dina Pule says she was overwhelmed by the large numbers of beneficiaries queuing at SASSA offices in Cape Town. Image: DA website

Social Development Minister Dina Pule says she was overwhelmed by the large numbers of beneficiaries queuing at SASSA offices in Cape Town, highlighting the growing demand for social assistance across South Africa.

Pule made the comments during an oversight visit to the SASSA offices in Khayelitsha and Bellville on Thursday, where she met with officials and beneficiaries to hear about the challenges they face.

Lengthy queues

The minister said the lengthy queues in Khayelitsha demonstrated the significant demand for both SASSA’s services and the social grants administered by the agency.



“In Khayelitsha, you have seen the number of people that are there. I was also overwhelmed myself with the numbers there and what it means for us,” Pule said.

She said the situation demonstrated that there was substantial demand for the work carried out by SASSA, as well as for the grants that provide financial support to millions of South Africans.

“It means there is so much demand for SASSA and the work that SASSA does. But also there is so much demand for the grants,” she added.



Thousands affected by Northern Cape grant stoppages

The minister’s comments come as thousands of beneficiaries in the Northern Cape were left without their social grant payments after failing to participate in SASSA’s annual review process.

SASSA withheld payments for more than 7 000 beneficiaries who did not make themselves available for the required review.

The annual review process is used by SASSA to verify beneficiaries’ information and determine whether they continue to meet the requirements for receiving social grants.



Affected beneficiaries have been urged to update their details and complete the necessary compliance requirements to avoid further interruptions to their payments.

Highlights the challenges

The developments highlight the challenges facing both beneficiaries and the social security system, as large numbers of people continue to rely on grants while SASSA works to ensure that payments are made only to those who remain eligible.

Pule’s visit to the Western Cape offices forms part of government oversight efforts aimed at understanding the challenges experienced by beneficiaries and SASSA officials on the ground.



The long queues in Khayelitsha and Bellville have once again placed the accessibility and efficiency of social grant services in the spotlight, particularly for beneficiaries who depend on their monthly payments for essential household expenses.

World.title: Mind games kick off as All Blacks turn up the heat on referees
World.content:
The psychological battle between the Springboks and All Blacks has already begun, with New Zealand coach Dave Rennie turning up the heat on referees. Image: Six Nations Rugby

The psychological battle between the Springboks and All Blacks has already begun, with New Zealand coach Dave Rennie making it clear that he wants referees to encourage a faster, more continuous game during the upcoming four-Test Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.

Rennie’s comments came after New Zealand’s emphatic 54-0 victory over the Sharks in Durban, where England referee Matthew Carley was praised by the All Blacks coach for taking action against what he viewed as unnecessary delays.

The All Blacks are building a clear identity under Rennie, with speed, continuity and attacking intent central to their approach.



Recent analysis has highlighted a significant increase in ball-in-play time, possession and ruck activity under the new regime.

David Rennie wants referees to keep the game moving

Rennie was particularly pleased with Carley’s approach to lineouts during the Sharks match.

The New Zealand coach believes teams should not be allowed to take excessive time before restarting play, arguing that delays give opponents an opportunity to disrupt the rhythm of the match.



“We know if we can be accurate and disciplined, the ball’s going to be in play a lot, and we’ll be able to apply pressure,” Rennie said.

“But every time you turn it over and give away a penalty, you give the opposition a chance to slow the game down.”

Rennie also praised Carley for allowing play to continue when players appeared to be suffering from relatively minor injuries, including New Zealand fullback Damian McKenzie.



The approach is consistent with the All Blacks’ desire to maintain a high-tempo contest and keep opponents under pressure.

A potential battle of styles

The comments are particularly significant with South Africa standing between New Zealand and their ultimate goal on this tour.

The two teams appear to have contrasting approaches to controlling matches.



New Zealand are looking to increase the tempo, keep the ball alive and attack with greater continuity, while the Springboks have traditionally been highly effective at controlling territory, using their kicking game and dominating set-piece situations.

That makes the battle for tempo potentially one of the defining features of the series.

If New Zealand can keep the ball moving and prevent South Africa from slowing the contest, their attacking game could become a major weapon.



Conversely, if the Springboks can impose their preferred rhythm, they could force the All Blacks into a more physical and structured battle.

The set-piece could be decisive

Interestingly, New Zealand’s desire for a faster game could also place greater importance on their own ability to secure clean possession.

Recent analysis of the two teams’ performances suggests the Springboks have an advantage at set-piece, while New Zealand’s lineout has been an area requiring improvement.



That could make the opening stages of each Test particularly important.

The Springboks will be looking to turn scrums and lineouts into attacking platforms, while the All Blacks will want quick, clean ball from set-piece situations to launch their multi-phase attack.

Mind games have begun

Rennie’s comments can be viewed purely as a statement about the way he wants rugby to be played, but they also add an interesting psychological dimension to the build-up.



With the first Test scheduled for 22 August at Ellis Park in Johannesburg, every aspect of the contest is already being scrutinised.

Matthew Carley has been appointed referee for the opening Test, making Rennie’s praise of his approach particularly noteworthy.

The All Blacks have made their preference clear: they want a fast, high-tempo contest with minimal unnecessary stoppages.



The Springboks, meanwhile, will be expected to remain focused on their own game plan rather than being drawn into the narrative coming from the New Zealand camp.

And with Rassie Erasmus at the helm, it would be a surprise if the Springboks were intimidated by a little pre-series pressure.

The real battle begins when the whistle blows.

Until then, the mind games are already well underway.

World.title: UPDATE | Survivors tell of horror of Zimbabwe ferry sinking as death toll hits 46
World.content:
Death toll grows: Zimbabwe police said 46 people are confirmed to have died in the disaster. Image: Jekesai NJIKIZANA / AFP

A man who survived a ferry disaster that claimed at least 46 lives on Zimbabwe’s Lake Kariba told AFP on Thursday how he watched helplessly as people tried to save themselves, with his best friend and seven of his relatives among the dead.

The overloaded government ferry – a vital link for villagers and fish traders around the vast lake – overturned in choppy waters on Tuesday in one of the country’s worst passenger boat disasters.

Memorial service

“Thank God that a wave pushed the sinking vessel and we managed to climb on top,” Chance Siyamavhu said at a memorial service in the lakeside town of Kariba close to the border with Zambia.



Perched on the upended boat, he watched as passengers struggled to survive, unable to save them.

“When the boat capsized, most of the people scrambled to get the life jackets but most of them did not even know how to use them,” the 45-year-old told AFP.

“Most people could not make it.”

“Our relatives were swept in another direction and they sank because we were not in a position to help them,” he said.

Dozens gathered for a memorial service in the lakeside town of Kariba © Jekesai NJIKIZANA / AFP

Dozens of mourners gathered in front of 44 coffins at the emotional service, as police announced that the death toll had risen to 46.

“The names of the victims who perished in the accident will be released in due course,” a police statement said.



Boat took on water

Officials say the boat was authorised to carry 90 people but was packed with 114 adults, five crew members and an unspecified number of children.

The civil protection unit said 77 people were rescued, and there were fears that other passengers may be unaccounted for.

Survivors said they had pleaded for the captain to turn back as the boat took on water.

Anymore Chambati, who had been a security official on the vessel, told AFP he had tried to hand out life jackets as the boat began to sink.

“I managed to only give not more than 10,” he said.

“The ferry engines were filled with water because of the heavy winds and eventually they failed, save for one.”

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: LIVE | Banyana Banyana vs Nigeria: ‘No margin for error’
World.content:
Banyana Banyana have vowed to bring their ‘A’ game when they face Nigeria in a crucial FIFA Women’s World Cup qualifier playoff at the Moulay Rachid Stadium in Casablanca on Thursday, 13 August.

The two nations were knocked out of the CAF Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON 2026) in the quarter-finals, thereby missing out on the four automatic World Cup qualification places.

Lifeline

They have, however, been given a lifeline by featuring in the playoffs that will take the winner into a long and difficult route to securing tickets to South America for the women’s football global showpiece next year.



“It’s not the place we want to be but we’ve been given another opportunity, a very big opportunity to go on a very long journey. We obviously have to bring our A game, there’s no margin for error, the disappointment of losing the previous game is going to probably drive us to get a positive result. It’s not going to be an easy game, two big guns of African football, not where we want to be and one of us not going further ahead to qualify for the World Cup.

“It’s a big game for us, we know how big it is, the players know how big it is, I’m sure Nigeria know how big it is, we just have to do what we have to do, we just have to execute our plans and make sure that we are victorious at the end of the day,” said coach Desiree Ellis.

‘Crucial match’

The two women’s football giants last met at the previous edition of the WAFCON, with the Super Falcons winning the clash en route to lifting their 10th continental title.

But things have changed and both sides are now fighting for a spot to the next phase of the playoff qualifiers.

Speaking to the media in Casablanca, Banyana Banyana captain Refiloe Jane said they will leave everything on the field to ensure that they are victorious.

“It will be a crucial match for the team, we came here with an objective to qualify for the World Cup, and we would have liked to qualify the first time given the first opportunity, but things didn’t go our way. We keep our heads up high, we have another opportunity to do so, so our focus is on the next match, to try and give it our all to continue on this journey.



“The rivalry against Nigeria goes back over the years, we just have to believe and put in the work, and we have shown in the past that we can do it. It’s a real do or die, and we want to leave the field knowing we have given it our all,” said Jane.

South Africa and Nigeria meet at 22:00 SA time, with the Ivory Coast and Ghana contesting the other playoff spot at the Larbi Zaouli Stadium at 19:00 (SA time).

Banyana Banyana 1-2 Nigeria

World.title: Miguel’s warning to Sundowns: We are Kaizer Chiefs, we fear no one!
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs defender Inacio Miguel has send a stern warning to Mamelodi Sundowns ahead of Saturday’s showdown at FNB Stadium.

The two giants of South African football will battle it out for three points on the day.

Kick-off is at 15:00.



And while Chiefs have won their opening two league games and sit atop the Betway Premiership standings, Sundowns have, over the years, dominated this fixture.

The Brazilians head into this encounter on the back of a hard-fought 3-2 win over TS Galaxy, and they will be aiming for a convincing win.

However, on the back of it all, Miguel said Amakhosi‘s objectives are clear, and they are to win their own matches to reach their targets.

Also read: Bafana Bafana starlet swaps English football for MLS

KAIZER CHIEFS FEAR NO ONE, SAYS MIGUEL TO SUNDOWNS

“My understanding is that we need to respect that Mamelodi Sundowns won the Champions League, Sundowns is Sundowns but at the same time we are Kaizer Chiefs, you know, we also fight for our goals,” Miguel told reporters.

“We fear no-one!



“I think the message is very clear, we fear no-one, no matter if they are the champions of the Champions League or the PSL, we will face them as we face Sekhukhune as I said before.

“We will start the game with the same ambition, with the same spirit of fighting. We go in for every duel and that’s the message very clear from the coach,” concluded Miguel.

World.title: ‘Pensioners go to loans’: SASSA grant recipients claim borrowing just to survive
World.content:
The South African’s recent report on disrupted SASSA payment dates drew a wave of reader reaction, including one comment pointing to a troubling coping mechanism among pensioners.

Commenter Zukido Gvolozela wrote: “Pensionèrs go to loans. after paying bills and all.necesaries” – a comment, despite its typos, that suggests pensioners are resorting to loans and after-pay arrangements just to keep up with bills and other necessities. If accurate, this points to a cycle where grant recipients take on debt simply to bridge the gap between a fixed R2 400 payment and rising living costs.

Fixed grant, rising costs for pensioners

This concern echoes the broader theme running through reader responses to the original article: a monthly grant that was never designed to stretch this far. Pensioners have already reported losing their insurance policies and electricity coupons due to payment-date disruptions and now face the added risk of debt traps if they turn to loans to cover shortfalls.



For pensioners on fixed incomes, taking on any form of credit carries long-term risk, particularly if repayment terms are unfavourable or poorly understood.

Other recipients report separate payment issues

Adding to the picture, commenter Alvenita Calvert said they had not yet received their child support grant, a separate issue from the pension payment delays, but one that suggests disruptions may be affecting more than one grant type at a time.

Together, these reader accounts suggest that SASSA’s payment schedule issues are pushing some recipients toward financial coping strategies that could deepen, rather than ease, their hardship. The comments underscore a growing call from grant recipients: predictable payments and higher grant amounts are needed to protect South Africa’s most vulnerable from falling further behind.

World.title: Weather: Morning frost, isolated showers and rain expected
World.content:
Here is what the weather has in store for KZN, Free State and North West on Friday 14 August 2026.

KWAZULU-NATAL

Morning fog will occur over the interior, while partly cloudy and cool to cold conditions will continue elsewhere.

Isolated showers and rain are expected in the extreme north-east.



Along the coast, light westerly to north-westerly winds will blow in the morning before shifting to moderate to fresh northerly to north-easterly winds later.

The UVB sunburn index is expected to be very high.

DURBAN

Durban is going to be fine.

Winds will start light from the north-west in the morning before shifting to moderate northerly to north-easterly winds later.

Temperatures will range from 12°C to 21°C.

The UVB sunburn index is going to be very high.

Free State is going to have morning frost in places, otherwise partly cloudy and cold to cool.
