World.title: Colombia declares economic emergency to rebuild after earthquake
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella said he would declare an economic emergency and create a reconstruction fund for homes and small businesses that were destroyed in Monday’s earthquake.

In a press statement, De la Espriella said that the government would initially support victims with temporary relief and will declare an economic emergency to find the funds for reconstruction.

Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said the government was not yet considering raising taxes to find the approximately COP20 trillion ($6.4 billion) that would at least be needed for reconstruction.

The president said his government would initially prioritize relief for the estimated 24,000 families from the west of the country who have lost their homes or businesses.

The temporary relief measures would include:

The payment of public services for affected families by the government.

Housing rent subsidies for those who lost their homes.

Tax and financial relief measures.

Economic support for the most vulnerable families.

Support mechanisms for merchants and small business owners who have been affected by the earthquake.

As part of the emergency, De la Espriella announced the creation of a “Miracle Fund, an entity that will channel national and international contributions destined for the reconstruction of hospitals, educational centers, properties, roads, and airports that suffered damage from the earthquake.”

“The state of emergency must encompass economic reactivation measures that stimulate investment, reduce obstacles to project development, and generate more jobs in the affected areas,” said the president.

An economic emergency gives the president three months to issue decrees related to the cause of the emergency without having to go through Congress.

The legal validity of the decree declaring an emergency and those that follow will only be tested by the Constitutional Court.

At the time of publication the President’s Office had yet to issue its first decree.

World.title: Colombia asked US to carry out joint military operations: Hegseth
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella asked the US Government for joint military operations “to destroy terrorists and terror networks,” said US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth Wednesday.

At an event of the so-called Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (ACCC) in Panama, Hegseth said that “Colombia will join the ACCC, becoming the 19th member.”

Through the newly inaugurated president, as our president likes to say “President El Tigre,” Colombia has already requested that our department of war join Colombia in its fight against narcoterrorism. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth

Hegseth’s announcement was rejected by leftist opposition party Historic Pact, whose Senate chief Ivan Cepeda said that “the US citizen Abelardo de la Espriella wants to surrender our government, our territory and our sovereignty to the strategic interests of the United States.

Cepeda stressed that Colombia’s constitution allows only the Senate to permit the entry of foreign troops to the country.

Colombia’s sovereignty is not up for negotiation, it is not to be surrendered, and it cannot be subordinated to the military interests of any foreign power. To defend it is to defend the dignity of the nation, the independence of the Republic, and the right of the Colombian people to freely decide on their territory and their destiny. Senator Ivan Cepeda

Ahead of taking office on Friday, De la Espriella said that he would join US-led alliances that allegedly seek to combat drug trafficking.

In his inaugural speech, the president said he intends to “defeat, without truce, narco-terrorism and all criminal organizations that threaten the freedom of Colombia.”

The State Department last week announced that it would seek to send a $1 billion military aid package to Colombia to “support the De la Espriella Administration’s efforts to defeat the vicious narcoterrorist and criminal organizations that threaten US, Colombian, and hemispheric security and economic prosperity.”

World.title: Controversy in Colombia over refusal to allow foreign search and rescue teams
World.content:
The government of President Abelardo de la Espriella has been criticized over its refusal to accept foreign search and rescue workers in the crucial hours after Monday’s earthquake.

One of the first to raise the alarm was China’s ambassador to Bogota, Zhu Jingyang, who called on the government on Tuesday to “release the name of the official and his or her designated contact person to coordinate international aid for the earthquake victims.”

El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele said that he was told that Colombia’s “rescue teams, medical personnel, and other emergency responders are on the scene and handling the situation” and “they do not require personnel support.”

Mexico’s President Caudia Sheinbaum said that her government was waiting for approval to send a team of 225 rescue workers to look for survivors, but was waiting for a “formal invitation” from Bogota.

In a response to growing pressure, newspaper El Tiempo said Colombia didn’t need foreign search and rescue teams because “the country has 23 teams with personnel that is part of the global elite.”

The Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday evening that it had “called on the international community to provide support in addressing the emergency, in order to tackle the most severely affected areas and mitigate the disaster.”

But social leader Leonard Renteria from Buenaventura said Wednesday that “as of yesterday, we still didn’t know anything about the arrival of rescue workers” in the partially destroyed port city.

“On the streets, we’ve seen people from the neighborhoods with the firefighters and civil defense personnel,” Renteria posted on social media platform X.

Fifty hours after Monday’s disaster, the US Department of State said it had “mobilized urban search-and-rescue (USAR) technical teams from Fairfax County, Virginia, and Los Angeles County, California to support Colombia’s search and rescue efforts.”

With chances of finding people alive rapidly decreasing, pressure on the government to respond increased online.

“I would really like to know the technical reason for rejecting assistance from teams that specialize in this type of disaster. There are many affected areas and plenty of evidence of technical inadequacies,” said civil engineer Gina Villalobos on X.

According to opposition congresswoman Maria Fernanda Carrascal, “it was an ideological decision, they only wanted rescue workers from Israel and the United States to enter while the Mexicans have been ready since Monday.”

On Wednesday afternoon, newly appointed disaster response chief David Tamayo said the government would also allow search and rescue workers from Ecuador and El Salvador “that can guarantee the provision of search and rescue teams and that are recognized by their own governments as meeting international search and rescue standards.”

These teams would come to search for hundreds of people who are feared to be under the rubble of buildings that collapsed in the worst earthquake in 10 years.

World.title: West Colombia earthquake killed more than 227 people, say local authorities
World.content:
Local and regional authorities have said that at least 227 people were confirmed killed in Monday’s earthquake while search and rescue teams continue to look for survivors.

So far, 120 people were confirmed dead in Valle del Cauca where locals said that entire towns in the north of the province were all but destroyed by the 7.4 magnitude earthquake that struck the Choco province on Monday.

In Cali, the capital of Valle del Cauca, rescue workers continued to look for survivors under the rubble of apartment buildings that collapsed. Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder imposed a curfew in the city after locals chased him away from a search and rescue operation.

Choco Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba said that mayors from the capital Quibdo and 22 affected towns reported 14 deaths and 140 injuries.

Multiple parts of the western province have yet to be contacted, however, as the local energy and telephone grid were destroyed by the earthquake, said Cordoba.

In Pereira, a city located at only 60 kilometers of the earthquake’s epicenter, and the surrounding Risaralda province, at least 88 people had died and dozens were still missing.

All major cities in the coffee region, Choco and Valle del Cauca declared an emergency to deal with the hundreds of injured that required medical attention at one of the cities’ hospitals.

President Abelardo de la Espriella said Tuesday morning that the earthquake destroyed more than 5,000 homes and that 188 people were missing.

The National Army and fire brigades from across Colombia sent teams to the cities in the disaster area to help with local search and rescue missions.

The US Department of State said it had committed $15.5 million “in funding for emergency shelter, food, protection, and earthquake assessments” for Colombia.

The Chinese embassy in Bogota said that Chinese companies that operate in Colombia were “sending heavy equipment to the most affected areas of the earthquake, participating in rescue efforts and the clearing of debris, in order to rescue the affected population using all available means.”

World.title: Colombia declares national disaster after devastating earthquake
World.content:
Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a national disaster and sent his ministers to the west of Colombia to coordinate rescue operations in response to a 7.4M earthquake.

Following an emergency meeting at disaster management agency UNGRD, De la Espriella said he would travel to Pereira, one of the worst hit cities, to further coordinate the government response.

Interior Minister Rodrigo Lara would coordinate rescue operations for the rest of the coffee region, the health and defense ministers would travel to the Choco and Transport Minister Elsa Noguera would coordinate efforts in Valle del Cauca from Cali.

De la Espriella canceled plans he had to visit La Guajira, a northern province that wasn’t affected by the earthquake.

Throughout the morning, local and regional media reported dozens of collapsed buildings in multiple cities in Valle del Cauca, the coffee region and Choco.

More than 110 people were killed and dozens were injured because of the earthquake, De la Espriella said at a press conference.

The earthquake damaged more than 1,500 homes and destroyed 37. Sixty-one buildings collapsed and 18 healthcare centers suffered damage as well as 52 schools and 17 community centers.

The roof of the Pereira airport also came down and five other airports in western Colombia reported damages, said the president.

According to the National Police, road travel has been complicated because of landslides and fallen trees.

The government has yet to report on missing persons.

“Right now, the most important thing is to protect lives, rescue those who remain trapped, treat the injured, and bring aid to the hardest-hit communities,” said Vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo.

“United we will overcome this emergency,” Restrepo added.

The vice-president, together with Foreign Minister Omar Bula, will coordinate foreign aid.

According to the Colombian Geological Service, the earthquake was the strongest in Colombia of the past decade and the strongest in the west of the country since 1979.

World.title: 7.4M earthquake hits western Colombia: at least 110 killed, dozens of buildings collapsed
World.content:
An M7.4 earthquake hit western Colombia on Monday, killing at least 110 people and injuring hundreds.

The earthquake struck around 7:30 and had its epicenter in San Jose del Palmar, a municipality in the Choco province.

In the hour that followed, locals began reporting collapsed buildings in the cities of Cali, Pereira and Manizales, where a tower of the cathedral and a dozen other buildings fully or partially collapsed, according to Mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas.

In a first report on fatalities, Risaralda Governor Juan Diego Patiño said that at least 40 people were killed in the capital Perira. Another three would have been killed in Manizales.

In Cali, an unknown number of people would be trapped under the rubble of multiple buildings. At least 27 people would be killed in the Valle del Cauca province.

Large parts of the roof of the Pereira airport came down, according to video shared on social media.

Flights to Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura were suspended while airport authorities check for damages to infrastructure

In Quibdo, the capital of Choco, at least four people were killed and another 69 were injured, Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba said in her second report.

The earthquake was also felt strongly in the capital Bogota and in Medellin where no injuries were reported.

In an initial response, President Abelardo de la Espriella said on social media platform X that he had “personally taken charge of the emergency response in San José del Palmar.”

“I will also be in Pereira in person to stand with those affected and monitor the government’s response,” said De la Espriella, who took office on Friday and has yet to appoint his director of disaster response agency UNGRD.

The president later reported that he was on his way to Bogota to lead rescue efforts from the UNGRD’s main office.

I have established a Unified Command Post at the UNGRD, from where I will personally lead the efforts to assist the communities in Chocó, the Coffee Region, and all affected areas. President Abelardo de la Espriella

According to the Colombian Geological Service, the earthquake was the strongest in Colombia of the past decade.

World.title: US seeks $1B aid package for Colombia’s new government
World.content:
Th US State Department said it will ask Congress for $1 billion for “deepening our shared and economic partnership” with the government of Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella.

The funding boost, which resembles that of the first year of Plan Colombia in 2000, seeks to “support the De la Espriella Administration’s efforts to defeat the vicious narcoterrorist and criminal organizations that threaten US, Colombian, and hemispheric security and economic prosperity.”

In preliminary talks, De la Espriella had already agreed to join the “Shield of the Americas,” a regional initiative of far-right governments to jointly fight crime.

According to a fact sheet, the funds that would require congressional approval would be used to:

Strengthen Colombia’s security forces

Disrupt illegal armed groups and organized crime’s ability to launder money

Significantly expand coca eradication and cocaine interdiction operations

Halt migration

Increase State presence in conflict regions

Combat child recruitment and exploitation by illegal armed groups

The administration of President Donald Trump also seeks to “increase trade and deepen economic ties between our countries.”

In order to do this, nominated US ambassador Nate Morris told the Senate that De la Espriella would withdraw from a memorandum of understanding with the government of China that sought to improve ties with the Asian giant.

Trump’s aid package would help Colombian communities “recover from potential El Niño-related flooding, drought,” which is expected to cause emergencies between December and March.

The US would also support a Bilateral Prosperity Dialogue to “stabilize” Colombia’s economy, “strengthening its energy generation and distribution sectors, exploring critical mineral investments, and creating new opportunities for US investors.”

The aid package would additionally “strengthen Colombian small and medium enterprises in agribusiness, manufacturing, and tech services by connecting them to US buyers and linking them to U.S.-aligned supply chains.”

The two governments would additionally seek to modernize Colombia’s digital, port and energy infrastructure while “positioning Colombia as a trusted nearshoring partner for supply chain diversification.”

World.title: De la Espriella sworn in as Colombia’s new president
World.content:
President Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in in Colombia’s third largest city, Cali, under extreme security precautions.

De la Espriella was sworn in by the president of Congress, Senator Honorio Henriquez of the far-right Democratic Center party in the theater of the private University of Santiago de Cali.

The first part of the ceremony was attended by the Spanish King Felipe VI, multiple heads of state from Latin America and more than 60 ambassadors.

After being sworn in, De la Espriella went to the nearby Pichincha Battalion to assume the supreme command of the armed forces and hold his first speech as president.

The president vowed the security forces that he would be “an essential part of the miracle country” and vowed that at the end of his four-year mandate “authority will be felt in every corner of the country.”

De la Espriella also promised that “nobody will be persecuted for his opinions” and warned members of the “regime” of former President Gustavo Petro he would cooperate with “other States,” suggesting they could be extradited.

Both ceremonies were boycotted by Petro’s leftist political party, the Historic Pact, which organized political rallies elsewhere in Cali, and in the cities of Bogota and Barranquilla.

In Barranquilla, Senator Ivan Cepeda stressed the left does not recognize the incoming government because of De la Espriella’s US citizenship and his alleged debts with the US Department of Justice.

“De la Espriella, who once acted as an intermediary for drug traffickers and paramilitaries—from whose ill-gotten gains he has profited—has now become a figure who will be pressured by the United States, by his own government, and by its federal agencies to allow all kinds of foreign intervention in Colombia,” said Cepeda.

The leftist senator lost the elections to De la Espriella with a razor-thin margin of less than one percent. His supporters continue to seek a court order to nullify the election.

World.title: Disapproval of Orsi's government climbs to 57% in the third quarter, Opción finds
World.content:
Disapproval of Orsi's government climbs to 57% in the third quarter, Opción finds

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 10:16 UTC Full article

The breakdown shows 30% rating the government's performance as very poor and 27% as poor, against 16% who consider it good and 3% very good

Fifty-seven percent of Uruguayans disapprove of the performance of the government led by Yamandú Orsi and 19% approve, according to the third-quarter 2026 Public Opinion Monitor released on Wednesday by the polling firm Opción. In the previous measurement the figures were 48% and 20% respectively.

The breakdown shows 30% rating the government's performance as very poor and 27% as poor, against 16% who consider it good and 3% very good. Twenty-four percent do not assess it either way and 1% did not answer. The net rating moved from -28 to -38 points.

The president's personal evaluation returns somewhat less negative figures. Twenty-two percent approve of his performance, 28% take neither view and 50% disapprove. His net rating went from -17 to -28 compared with the previous quarter. Orsi's approval is three points above the government's and his disapproval seven points lower.

The series for the term shows a sustained progression. Approval of the government's performance stood at 30% at the start of the mandate, 23% in the first quarter of 2026 and 20% in the second. Disapproval travelled the opposite path: 19%, 38% and 48%. According to the firm's analysis, the main shift lies not in the fall in support but in the contraction of the segment without a settled view, which was 51% at the beginning of the term and is now 24%.

The sharpest movement is within the governing party's own electorate. Among those who voted for the Frente Amplio in the first round of 2024, disapproval rose nine points from the previous quarter, the largest increase of the term so far, to 28%, while approval stands at 39%. Among Coalición Republicana voters, 81% disapprove and 4% approve. Those who backed other candidacies in 2024 show trends closer to opposition voters than to government supporters.

Opción argues this is the lowest level of support recorded by a Frente Amplio-led government at this point in a term. The measurement incorporates for the first time the controversy over the purchase of an official vehicle, which had not featured in the previous survey.

The poll was conducted by telephone in two stages, with 403 cases between July 16 and 20 and a further 403 between August 6 and 11, on a total sample of 806 people. The maximum margin of error is 3.5 percentage points at a 95% confidence level. On those parameters, the one-point change in approval is not significant, while the nine-point jump in disapproval is.

World.title: Lula's runoff lead over Flávio Bolsonaro narrows to 8.9 points, CNT/MDA poll finds
World.content:
Lula's runoff lead over Flávio Bolsonaro narrows to 8.9 points, CNT/MDA poll finds

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 09:03 UTC Full article

In the second-round scenario, Lula takes 48% of voting intentions against 39.1% for the Liberal Party senator

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva holds an 8.9-point lead over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in a potential runoff, according to the CNT/MDA poll released on Tuesday. The gap stood at 12.5 points in the June survey.

In the second-round scenario, Lula takes 48% of voting intentions against 39.1% for the Liberal Party senator. In June the figures were 49.3% and 36.8% respectively. The narrowing reflects both a 1.3-point decline for the president and a 2.3-point rise for the opposition candidate, variations that individually fall within the 2.2-point margin of error. The current gap between the two, by contrast, exceeds it comfortably. Blank and spoiled ballots account for 11% and undecided voters for 2%.

In the first round, Lula leads with 42.4%, virtually unchanged from June, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro on 28.7%, Ronaldo Caiado on 4%, Romeu Zema on 3.3% and Renan Santos on 2.8%. If no candidate exceeds 50% of valid votes, the two leading contenders go to a runoff, an outcome that has occurred in every Brazilian presidential election since 2002.

The poll tested other runoff scenarios, in which the president retains wider margins: 49% against Zema's 35%, 48% against Caiado's 36% and 49% against Renan Santos's 33%. Flávio Bolsonaro is therefore the rival who runs closest.

Measurements differ substantially depending on the polling firm. A Datafolha survey from mid-July put the runoff at 48% against 43%, four points above the figure CNT/MDA now attributes to the senator. In March, an AtlasIntel survey described the two as being in a technical tie.

The poll was commissioned by the National Transport Confederation and carried out by the MDA institute, with 2,002 face-to-face interviews conducted between August 5 and 9 in 140 municipalities across all regions of the country. The margin of error is 2.2 percentage points and the survey is registered with the Superior Electoral Court.

The figures come four days before the official start of campaigning for October's elections. Flávio Bolsonaro is the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for attempting a coup and endorsed his candidacy in December. Lula, 80, is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term.

World.title: Venezuela's government and opposition agree to renew the Supreme Court and claim the London gold
World.content:
Venezuela's government and opposition agree to renew the Supreme Court and claim the London gold

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 08:59 UTC Full article

National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez and Dinorah Figuera, who heads the delegated committee of the assembly elected in 2015

The government of acting president Delcy Rodríguez and a section of Venezuela's opposition closed the first round of negotiations in Caracas on Wednesday with two agreements: restarting from scratch the renewal of the Supreme Court of Justice, and acting jointly to recover Venezuelan gold reserves held at the Bank of England.

National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez and Dinorah Figuera, who heads the delegated committee of the assembly elected in 2015, signed the document and read out a joint communiqué in sections at a hotel in the capital, after more than six hours of deliberations. No questions from the press were taken.

The judicial agreement annuls the process the National Assembly had begun in May, following a reform that raised the court from 20 to 32 members. Instead, the parties agreed to amend the Supreme Court's organic law again, renew and expand the judicial nominations committee, activate a new nomination process and set up a council to review candidates' credentials. In 2024 the court upheld Nicolás Maduro's re-election despite fraud allegations and without disaggregated results being published.

On the economic front, both delegations committed to promoting the recovery of international reserve assets held at the Bank of England, some 31 tonnes of gold withheld since the United Kingdom stopped recognizing Maduro's government and the subject of litigation in London courts. Weeks ago, Delcy Rodríguez sent a letter to King Charles III requesting their release. The funds would go to assisting those affected by the June 24 double earthquake, which left more than 6,300 dead according to the official toll. The text provides for transparency, traceability and audit mechanisms over their use.

The communiqué makes no mention of the National Electoral Council, whose reform the opposition regards as a priority for any eventual election timetable, nor does it address the release of political prisoners. A group of trade unionists gathered outside the hotel calling for progress on both points. Eighty-four former political prisoners issued a statement backing the process and calling for a new court and an independent electoral authority.

Two technical working groups were set up, one on the earthquake emergency and another on strengthening democracy. Implementation begins this month and the delegations will meet again in mid-September.

This is the eighteenth attempt at negotiation in two decades, and the first held in Caracas after previous rounds in the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Doha, Oslo and Barbados. The process has the backing of the United States. María Corina Machado, in exile in Panama, remains outside the table and has said she will not obstruct it.

World.title: The main land crossing between Argentina and Chile passes its winter closure record
World.content:
The main land crossing between Argentina and Chile passes its winter closure record

13th Thursday, August 2026 - 06:55 UTC Full article

The corridor was closed as a precaution on July 14 in anticipation of the forecasts

The Cristo Redentor international crossing, which links the Argentine province of Mendoza with Chile's Valparaíso Region through the Andes, has now been closed for close to a month because of a snow and wind storm, surpassing the winter closure record set in 2023. Authorities on both sides estimate it could reopen next week, depending on weather conditions.

The corridor was closed as a precaution on July 14 in anticipation of the forecasts. Snowfall extended between the settlements of Punta de Vacas and Las Cuevas, reached accumulations of up to four meters in some sections and affected 80 kilometers of Route 7, the largest such record in the area since 2008, according to the national roads agency. Winds blew at between 110 and 160 kilometers per hour, with zero visibility.

Official counts put the number of international freight trucks held at various points in Mendoza at around 1,550, although transport sector estimates raise the figure above 2,000. Drivers from Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay and Chile are among those stranded. Each immobilized vehicle represents losses of close to 600 dollars a day, according to the sector's own calculations.

The delay has drawn criticism. The Mendoza truck owners' association toured the corridor and said the road was in good condition at least as far as Puente del Inca, and called for the tunnel to be opened. The national roads agency replied that clearing work reached the mouth of the international tunnel on August 9, but that winds prevent traffic being allowed through to Las Cuevas and that precautions are being intensified given the risk of avalanches.

In Chile, the head of the Border Crossings Unit, Sergio Salazar, rejected the idea that opportunities had been missed. “There really were no such windows,” he said, explaining that work on the Chilean side was completed the previous Friday and on the Argentine side this week. He said the only opening was brief and risky, and the decision was not to expose a small number of trucks.

Reopening will not restore normal traffic immediately. Authorities calculate between five and six days to clear the accumulated backlog, constrained by the winter timetable, which limits operations to around twelve hours a day. Under normal conditions the corridor handles between 500 and 600 trucks daily.

The storm has also kept the Pehuenche, Agua Negra, Pircas Negras, Pino Hachado and San Francisco crossings closed. Alternative routes to the Pacific involve travelling around 2,000 additional kilometers.

World.title: Falklands pause Loligo squid fishing for two weeks over low biomass
World.content:
Falklands pause Loligo squid fishing for two weeks over low biomass

12th Wednesday, August 2026 - 23:05 UTC Full article

The decision was taken after consultation with the industry and reflects, according to the official statement, a shared view that a temporary cessation is the most appropriate course of action

The Falkland Islands Fisheries Department announced on Wednesday that fishing within the Loligo Box will be paused for around two weeks as a precautionary measure, following low Loligo squid biomass in the area.

The decision was taken after consultation with the fishing industry and reflects, according to the official statement, a shared view that a temporary cessation is the most appropriate course of action. The Department coordinated a series of targeted trawls by the commercial fleet across the area on Wednesday, aimed at obtaining more precise information on the distribution of the stock. There were no public statements from the sector.

“This precautionary approach reflects the Department's commitment to the long-term stock sustainability and responsible management of the fishery,” the text says, adding that further updates will follow once more information is available.

Loligo squid, also known as Patagonian squid, is one of the main sources of income for the Falklands. Spain controls much of the world's catch of the species, mainly through the roughly sixteen licences the Islands grant to fish in their waters, with volumes close to 50,000 tonnes a year.

The pre-season survey carried out by the M/V Monteferro between February 3 and 18 had estimated biomass at around 41,725 tonnes, with a reliable range of between 34,726 and 60,190, a figure considered sufficient to sustain a commercial season. That survey already showed a markedly uneven distribution: 38,134 tonnes south of the Loligo Box against 3,591 tonnes in the northern zone, where around half the specimens sampled were at a very early stage of maturity.

The pause also comes after an unfavorable cycle in the archipelago's other squid fishery. The Illex season closed on June 22 with catches well below the ten-year average and against a backdrop of rising fuel costs, although the Fisheries Department and the Falkland Islands Fishing Companies Association agreed at the time that this was not an immediate cause for concern.

Squid in the southwest Atlantic is under growing pressure. Fishing effort by the Chinese fleet in the region rose 85% between 2019 and 2024, and between 300 and 500 foreign-flagged vessels operate along the outer edge of Argentina's exclusive economic zone. Argentina, which maintains a sovereignty claim over the archipelago, questions the licensing regime the Islands administer. In July, Buenos Aires enacted its accession to the FAO Port State Measures Agreement, the only binding international instrument specifically designed to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.

World.title: YPF divests its stake in gas distribution for 780 million dollars
World.content:
YPF divests its stake in gas distribution for 780 million dollars

12th Wednesday, August 2026 - 06:28 UTC Full article

YPF will transfer 70% of the capital of Metrogas, the country's largest gas distributor, and 5% of Metroenergía, its trading arm

Argentine oil company YPF, 51% state-controlled, has accepted Edenor's offer to buy its stake in Metrogas and Metroenergía for 780 million dollars, according to a filing submitted on Monday to the securities regulator. The deal takes the company out of the natural gas distribution business.

YPF will transfer 70% of the capital of Metrogas, the country's largest gas distributor, and 5% of Metroenergía, its trading arm. Metrogas supplies around 2.4 million customers in the city of Buenos Aires and eleven surrounding districts, more than a quarter of the national market. Edenor supplies electricity to 3.4 million customers in the northern part of the metropolitan area.

The buyer is controlled by the Edelcos consortium, made up of businessmen José Luis Manzano, Daniel Vila and Mauricio Filiberti. Manzano, a former interior minister under Carlos Menem, already held 9.23% of Metrogas through his investment vehicle. Once completed, the deal will place a single group in charge of the largest gas and electricity distributors in the metropolitan area, with close to 5.8 million customers combined.

The competitive process began in April with thirteen non-binding offers and narrowed to five finalists: besides Edenor, Central Puerto, MSU, Grupo Pierri and Litoral Gas took part. Citigroup advised the oil company. Edenor bid alongside British firm Andina PLC and will have to launch a tender offer for the remaining shares, held by the national social security administration, investors on the Buenos Aires stock exchange and Manzano's existing stake.

YPF said the sale forms part of a review of its asset portfolio and that proceeds will go to Vaca Muerta, the unconventional hydrocarbons field at the center of the strategy pursued by its chairman, Horacio Marín. Argentine law also bars vertical integration between gas production and distribution, an incompatibility the company had carried since taking control of Metrogas in 2012.

The timing coincides with improved results at the distributor. Between 2023 and 2025, Metrogas doubled its gross profit, quadrupled its operating result, cut its debt to a third and resumed dividend payments for the first time since 2001. The tariff adjustments introduced by Javier Milei's government and a five-year review setting an indexation formula shape the regulatory framework of the business.

Metrogas's licence, granted in 1992 for 35 years, expires in December 2027. The gas regulator has sent the executive a recommendation to extend it by two decades, to 2047, a decision not yet formalized. Completion of the transaction is conditional on authorizations from energy sector regulators.

World.title: Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro appear together for the first time since their June rift
World.content:
Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro appear together for the first time since their June rift

12th Wednesday, August 2026 - 06:21 UTC Full article

“We have set our disagreements aside. What family is perfect? Let anyone without family problems raise their hand,” the former first lady said at the end of the event

Brazil's former first lady, Michelle Bolsonaro, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the Liberal Party's presidential candidate, appeared together in public on Tuesday for the first time since the falling-out between them in late June. The meeting took place at the party's headquarters in Brasília, where they recorded campaign material and prayed together.

“We have set our disagreements aside. What family is perfect? Let anyone without family problems raise their hand,” the former first lady said at the end of the event. She added that both had put their differences behind them to unite “in favor of something much greater,” and confirmed she will take part in the campaign. “He can count on me on social media and he can count on the strength of women spread across Brazil,” she said.

The dispute erupted in late June, when Michelle Bolsonaro released a video accusing her stepson of mistreating and humiliating her over internal party matters, leaving her support for his candidacy in doubt. “They treat me as if I were an idiot. As if I had arrived yesterday,” she said at the time. Flávio Bolsonaro posted an apology video in July inviting her to join the campaign, and she responded positively, although they had not appeared together in public until Tuesday.

The former first lady heads PL Mulher, the Liberal Party's women's wing, and her backing is considered significant among evangelical and female voters. On August 2 she was nominated as a Senate candidate for the Federal District, at a convention she was unable to attend because of a hospitalization; her brother read the speech she had prepared.

The reunion comes four days before the official start of campaigning for October's elections. Flávio Bolsonaro has not secured alliances with the parties of the so-called Centrão and is competing for conservative voters with former governor Ronaldo Caiado, governor Romeu Zema and political figure Renan Santos.

Polls differ in scale but agree in placing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is seeking re-election, ahead. A Datafolha survey from mid-July gave him 48% against the senator's 43% in a potential runoff; later measurements cited by international agencies put the two at 44% and 39% respectively.

Jair Bolsonaro, Michelle's husband and Flávio's father, is under house arrest after being sentenced to 27 years for attempting a coup. He is barred from holding public office, has appealed the ruling and is seeking a legislative pardon.

Lula will open his campaign at the stadium in São Bernardo do Campo, in greater São Paulo, where he was a union leader. Flávio Bolsonaro will do so at Copacabana beach in Rio de Janeiro.

World.title: Argentina to mark every July 15 with the World Cup win that revived the Falklands dispute
World.content:
Argentina to mark every July 15 with the World Cup win that revived the Falklands dispute

12th Wednesday, August 2026 - 06:13 UTC Full article

The decision was approved unanimously on August 5 at an executive committee meeting held at the association's Ezeiza complex

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has established July 15 as National Football Teams Day, in tribute to the 2-1 win over England in the 2026 World Cup semi-final, the same match after which several players displayed a banner asserting a sovereignty claim over the Falklands that prompted a FIFA disciplinary case.

The decision was approved unanimously on August 5 at an executive committee meeting held at the association's Ezeiza complex. According to its statement, the date commemorates the “great and historic victory” of the side coached by Lionel Scaloni, which came from behind in Atlanta through goals by Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez, both set up by Lionel Messi. The AFA specified that the recognition also covers all national teams — youth, men's and women's, futsal, beach football and field football — that train at the Lionel Andrés Messi complex. Argentina went on to lose the final to Spain.

After the final whistle on July 15, a group of players unfurled a sheet reading “Las Malvinas son argentinas” — “The Falklands are Argentine” — in front of the stands. The British government condemned the gesture and asked FIFA to investigate, considering it a political demonstration at an official competition. A spokesperson for then-prime minister Keir Starmer said, as reported by the Daily Mail, that “the World Cup might not be ours, the Falkland Islands definitely are”, adding that self-determination rests with the islanders.

FIFA rules prohibit political messaging at its competitions. The governing body's disciplinary committee opened proceedings against the AFA and several players, among them Giovani Lo Celso, Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martínez. The case remains open and no sanction has been decided. There is a precedent: FIFA had already begun proceedings over a similar banner displayed at a friendly against Bosnia in La Plata before the tournament.

Argentine President Javier Milei backed the players. He called the celebration “perfectly valid” and said it reflects a sentiment shared by Argentines, though he anticipated a fine from the governing body.

The AFA also said the banner will be handed to veterans of the Falklands War. It was made by a group of fans from a bedsheet and paint at a cost of under ten dollars, taken into the stadium without authorization and retrieved from the pitch by a member of the delegation's staff.

The United Kingdom has administered the Falklands since 1833. In the 2013 referendum, islanders voted overwhelmingly to retain their status as a British overseas territory. Argentina maintains a sovereignty claim over the islands.

World.title: Attention cat lovers! A cat museum has opened in Mexico City
World.content:
From the pets of Palacio Nacional to the preferred companions of Mexican intellectuals like Elena Poniatowska and Carlos Monsiváis, cats have played a significant role in Mexican history. So it’s no surprise that a sanctuary devoted to them has just opened its doors at Reforma 87, Mexico City.

Here’s everything you need to know about the city’s new Museo del Gato.

Before the cat museum

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Time Out México (@timeoutmexico)

Like any good project, the Museo del Gato de Ciudad de México has been slow-cooked and shape-shifted throughout the years. Esther Garcilita and Marco Sotomayor founded “La Gatería” in 2015, a cat café inspired by Japanese coffee shops where you can have a drink among felines.

As the first cat café in Latin America, La Gatería was nothing short of groundbreaking and built a loyal following. Part of its objective was to debunk some of the most common misconceptions about cats.

Over the next decade, the concept evolved into a much more extensive experience: a museum dedicated to cats.

Museo del Gato de Ciudad de México

Now you will not only enjoy their company, but also learn everything you’ve always wanted to know about these cute yet fierce animals. The museum offers guided tours led by its mascot, a calico named Sissi.

Along the way, you’ll find art and history presented as an immersive experience that fills the senses with everything the feline universe has to offer. There are three thematic rooms dedicated to the history of cats, the feline language and their relationship with humans.

Needless to say, the Cat Museum is not a conventional one. Its founders prioritized an interactive experience, complete with gigantic animatronic cats, projection mapping and a virtual reality simulator that allows guests to see through the eyes of a cat.

More than a museum

Beyond revolutionizing the Mexico City museum scene, the Museo del Gato directly supports animal welfare. A portion of ticket proceeds will fund a mobile spay-and-neuter unit for stray cats and dogs, helping humanely manage the city’s street animal population.

Everything you need to know

Planning your visit? Here are all the essential details to make sure you don’t miss out on this unique experience:

When does it open? The museum officially opened its doors to the public on Aug. 8.

Where is it located? You can find the museum at Paseo de la Reforma 87, 4th floor, Colonia Tabacalera, Alcaldía Cuauhtémoc, Mexico City.

What are the opening hours? Monday to Friday: 11 a.m. to 9 p.m.; Saturday: 10 a.m. to 9 p.m.; Sunday: 10 a.m. to 8 p.m.

Ticket prices and where to buy them: General admission is 350 pesos Monday through Thursday and 385 pesos Friday through Sunday. Tickets can be purchased through the official museum website or via the Fever platform.

Access policy: To ensure a comfortable and personalized tour, entry is limited to small groups of up to 60 people per hour. It is highly recommended to book your time slot in advance.

Lydia Leija is a linguist, journalist and visual storyteller. She has directed three feature films, and her audiovisual work has been featured in national and international media. She’s been part of National Geographic, Muy Interesante and Cosmopolitan.

World.title: Ángel Aguirre, ex-Guerrero governor, ordered to stand trial for alleged part in the Ayotzinapa abductions
World.content:
Listen to this article

A judge has ordered former Guerrero Governor Ángel Aguirre to stand trial over his alleged involvement in the 2014 disappearance of 43 students from the Atoyzinapa Rural Teachers College.

Aguirre, governor of Guerrero from 2011 until his resignation around a month after the students disappeared in Iguala, Guerrero, on Sept. 26, 2014, was arrested in México state last week.

🚨Videos clave del caos Ayotzinapa no desaparecieron por un error técnico, según FGR. Esto fue lo que presuntamente destruyó Ángel Aguirre. pic.twitter.com/6YjhgPylFp — Aristegui Noticias (@AristeguiOnline) August 7, 2026

While governor, he is alleged to have ordered the concealment and destruction of security camera video footage that showed a bus on which the Ayotzinapa students were traveling at the time it was stopped by police in Iguala.

The students disappeared after police allegedly handed them over to members of a local crime gang. All 43 young men were presumably murdered, although the remains of just three of them have been found.

During a 15-hour hearing that began on Tuesday and extended into the early hours of Wednesday, lawyers for Aguirre argued that the 70-year-old ex-governor was not in Guerrero at 8:30 p.m. on Sept. 29, 2014, the time he is alleged to have received footage captured by security cameras located outside the State Palace of Justice in Iguala.

Rather, Aguirre was traveling back to Chilpancingo, the capital of Guerrero, at that time after attending a meeting in Mexico City with then Interior Minister Miguel Ángel Osorio Chong, according to the ex-governor’s lawyers, who presented 31 pieces of evidence in support of their argument that their client is innocent.

Despite the defense lawyer’s argument and evidence, Mario Elizondo Martínez, pre-trial judge (juez de control) at the Altiplano federal prison in México state, ruled that the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR) had presented sufficient proof to warrant an order for the ex-governor to stand trial on charges of enforced disappearance.

“In response to the defense’s case presented to discredit the defendant’s possible involvement in the events, the judicial authority determined that the arguments presented were not objective and failed to prove that Ángel ‘N’ was not in the state of Guerrero, as was claimed in an attempt to exonerate him from the events,” the FGR said in a statement.

“The pre-trial judge noted that the evidence presented by the prosecutor was sufficient to issue an order to proceed to trial, since, according to the National Code of Criminal Procedure, at this stage it must only be established that there is a likelihood that the crime was committed, and further evidence must be presented in subsequent stages,” the FGR said.

The Attorney General’s Office said that Aguirre was ordered to stand trial for what it described as “his probable involvement in the crime of enforced disappearance under the hypothesis that the public servant concealed highly relevant information related to the investigation into the disappearance of the 43 students.”

Elizondo allocated a period of four months for prosecutors to continue their investigation and for defense lawyers to prepare their case. Therefore, the earliest Aguirre could face trial is in December. If convicted, he could be sentenced to up to 60 years in prison.

The judge ruled that the ex-governor must remain in preventive detention as he awaits trial. Aguirre has been held at the Altiplano prison since his arrest last Thursday.

The FGR’s case against Aguirre

Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said last week that a reexamination of the Ayotzinapa case “confirmed with full evidence and adherence to due process the possible participation of Ángel ‘N,’ ex-governor of the state of Guerrero, in the destruction of evidence [needed] to determine the whereabouts of the students.”

She said that in January, a cooperating witness provided testimony that “confirmed the existence of the video recordings” captured by security cameras outside the Palace of Justice in Iguala. That witness, Godoy said, identified the person who “removed” the recordings in order to “deliver them directly” to Aguirre.

The attorney general said that in May, “a second protected witness strengthened said testimony” by declaring that Aguirre “ordered, in a meeting with top officials from his government,” the concealment of “any evidence related to the events that occurred in the vicinity of the Iguala Palace of Justice.”

One witness she was referring to is Lambertina Galeana Marín, former president of the Guerrero Superior Court of Justice. The other is Blanca María del Rocío Estrada Ortega, a former official of the same court. Estrada has told authorities that she stole a disk containing the Iguala video footage from Galeana’s office on Sept. 29, 2014, and handed it over to Aguirre at 8:30 p.m. that day.

Subsequently, Aguirre allegedly handed over the video footage to former Guerrero Attorney General Iñaki Blanco in order for it to be destroyed. According to the newspaper La Jornada, the footage showed “armed people forcing the students to transfer to another bus, which minutes later fled in an unknown direction.”

The Federal Attorney General’s Office believes that the footage “contained fundamental evidence for identifying who was on board the bus and the route they took to flee Iguala,” La Jornada reported.

The newspaper also reported that the FGR’s accusation against Aguirre is “based on testimonies from two witnesses who allege that the governor … ordered that all evidence of what happened on the night of September 26 [2014] be destroyed mainly because his nephew, Ernesto Aguirre, who served as his adviser, was aware of what happened to the Ayotzinapa students from the very beginning, since he had ties to the Guerreros Unidos criminal group.”

The arrest of Aguirre is one of the most prominent detentions in connection with the Ayotzinapa case, which sparked outrage in Mexico and around the world, and triggered large protests in Mexico City and across the country. The disappearance of the students was a major blight on the 2012-18 presidency of Enrique Peña Nieto, but he survived widespread calls for his removal from office.

Scores of people have been arrested in connection with the case, including soldiers, police and former Attorney General Jesús Murillo Karam, but no has been convicted of the crime and some suspects have been released from prison.

In a 2023 report, the previous federal government led by former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador outlined three “possible reasons” for the abduction of the students, one of which was “the possible presence of drugs, weapons or money” on buses Ayotzinapa students had commandeered to travel to a protest in Mexico City.

With reports from El Economista, Reforma, La Jornada, Infobae and MVS Noticias

World.title: Health investigators rule out any presence of the Cyclospora parasite in Riviera Maya hotels
World.content:
The Federal Commission for Protection against Sanitary Risk (Cofepris) has ruled out any presence of the parasite Cyclospora in samples taken from 16 Riviera Maya hotels during an investigation linked to reports of British visitors falling ill after traveling to the Quintana Roo coast.

Mexico’s top health safety agency reported Tuesday that the analyses included 32 samples of fruits and vegetables obtained from food bars, as well as 11 samples of water intended for human use. All products tested negative for the parasite, and no indicators of contamination were detected in the establishments inspected.

The samples were analyzed using the real-time PCR pathogen-detection technique by the Cofepris National Reference Laboratory, based on the Bacteriological Analytical Manual method. The review was conducted in coordination with the General Directorate of Epidemiology as part of the sanitary surveillance measures implemented in the Mexican Caribbean.

“The absence of the pathogen Cyclospora cayetanensis, as well as of contamination indicators in the microbiological and molecular analyses, demonstrates that, at least at the specific points verified, sanitary control and handling processes operated within safety limits,” Cofepris said in a statement.

The case made international headlines after the Health Security Agency in the United Kingdom reported a rise in cyclosporiasis infections among people returning from vacations in Mexico.

According to the UK agency, 67 cases were identified between April 30 and July 15. Of the 51 travelers with available travel history, 48 reported having visited Mexico.

Following the report, the Health Ministry, which had confirmed 33 cases of cyclosporiasis in 13 Mexican states between May 25 and July 31, opened investigations into possible links with U.S. and U.K. infection reports.

Health Minister David Kershenobich said in a video posted earlier this month that detected cases represent just 0.00002% of Mexico’s population, and stressed that Cyclospora cayetanensis infections “are recurrent worldwide” with no scientific evidence to date that Mexico is the origin of the outbreak.

Cyclosporiasis is an intestinal infection that causes severe diarrhea and has been linked to unwashed lettuce or salad greens. It is caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis, a parasite that affected individuals eliminate through feces, which can lead to contamination of food and water.

The parasite first gained global attention after the U.S. reported an outbreak of cyclosporiasis in mid-July, which affected over 1,600 people across 34 states.

World.title: Mexico’s expert search-and-rescue team arrives in Colombia to help with rescue efforts
World.content:
A 45-member team of Mexican search-and-rescue experts has arrived in Colombia to help save survivors buried in the rubble after a 7.4 earthquake hit the southwest region of the nation Monday morning.

The Azteca International Rescue Brigade, known as the Topos, or Moles, for their skill in tunneling through debris, confirmed their arrival in the South American country via social media, where they wrote in part, “We are ready to put our hands, our knowledge, and our hearts at the service of our Colombian brothers and sisters. Stay strong, Colombia!”

La brigada internacional “Topos Azteca” de #México llegó a Cali para sumarse a las labores de rescate tras el terremoto en #Colombia. El diputado del Valle del Cauca, @EstebanOli, informó el arribo de los rescatistas mexicanos liderados por el legendario rescatista Héctor… pic.twitter.com/3ss0Lc6fQd — David de la Paz 戴维 (@daviddelapaz) August 12, 2026

The Mexican brigade traveled to Colombia directly from La Guaira in Venezuela, where they were still participating in operations following the 7.2- and 7.5-magnitude earthquakes in that neighboring country on June 24. They reached the Colombian city of Cali more than 30 hours after the earthquake, but within the critical 48-hour window for locating people trapped under fallen buildings, according to information released by Noticias RCN.

Their help was not welcomed at first, according to press reports. The Colombian government, headed by far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella, initially rejected Mexican assistance, citing “sovereignty” and insisting that Colombians had “the emergency covered.”

The Topos reportedly responded that they would respect Colombia’s refusal, and would wait for a new Damage and Needs Assessment. By Wednesday morning, they were able to write on X: “We are here, Colombia!”

The contingent is equipped with technological tools for search operations, including infrared cameras designed to locate possible victims under the rubble, according to Yahoo News reports.

The epicenter of Monday’s earthquake was in San José del Palmar, in the department of Chocó in southwestern Colombia. Also suffering damage were the departments of Valle del Cauca, Risaralda, Quindío and Caldas.

The official death toll provided by departmental authorities on Wednesday was at least 240 victims, although the federal government placed it at 188.

With reports from El Financiero, Vanguardia, Infobae and Le Monde

World.title: MND Local: A new museum and rising real estate prices in the Guadalajara Metro Area
World.content:
This week we have emerging details on the new archaeology museum being developed in Zapopan’s historic center, good news about Lake Chapala’s recovering water levels, and a look at skyrocketing real estate values in the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area (GMA).

Zapopan’s former City Hall to become an archaeology museum

Since 1949, the Palacio Municipal building in the heart of Zapopan’s historic center has housed City Hall. But in recent years — as the city’s needs have grown and key functions moved elsewhere — the building sat idle.

Now, with the approval of the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), the Palacio Municipal building is being transformed into a new cultural venue: the Western Archaeology Museum (Museo de Arqueología de Occidente).

The institution’s stated mission is to collect, preserve and promote the archaeological heritage of Mexico’s western states — including Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacán — allowing visitors to learn more about the area’s pre-Hispanic roots.

Curated by Lorenza López, head of the collection at the INAH Jalisco Center, the new museum will house pieces from the Regional Museum of Guadalajara, along with other works donated by private collectors.

The ceramics to be exhibited have undergone extensive restoration by students and teachers at the Western School of Conservation and Restoration (ECRO), located in the Analco section of Guadalajara. The painstaking work was carried out under the tutelage of historians, scientists and other specialists.

The ceramic pieces, chosen for their aesthetic, stylistic, and historical significance, will narrate more than 3,000 years of pre-Hispanic history in western Mexico. Highlights include Maya art from the Late Classic period and a theater-type incense burner from Teotihuacan.

Renovations on the Palacio Municipal building have been underway for months. The work is expected to preserve the structure’s architectural roots while incorporating modern updates necessary to support a world-class cultural institution.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ing. Ismael Jáuregui Castañeda (@ing.ismael.jauregui)

The Western Archaeology Museum is slated to open in early 2027. Besides exhibition halls, the venue will feature spaces for artistic research, outreach and cultural activities, as well as an outdoor terrace and cafe.

Lake Chapala’s water level is recovering

Water levels in Lake Chapala, Mexico’s largest reservoir, have meaningfully improved this summer, thanks to significant rainfall in June and July (the region’s peak rainy season).

According to reports from Conagua and the State Water Commission, as of Aug. 4, 2026, the lake is at 69.48% of its total capacity. This represents a significant recovery from June 2025, when the lake’s capacity had plummeted to just 47.5%.

What does this mean for the city of Guadalajara?

For the residents of the GMA and the entire regional ecosystem, this recovery translates into peace of mind and improved water security. Lake Chapala provides approximately 60% of the drinking water consumed daily in Jalisco’s capital city.

If the current trend continues, the reservoir could reach 75% capacity before the winter dry season arrives and reduce the specter of rationing and supply cuts over the next nine months.

Although the outlook is favorable, Conagua is strongly urging people to maintain responsible water consumption. Climate change remains an unpredictable factor for water resource management and consumption.

Ongoing monitoring of the water levels in Lake Chapala remains essential to ensure the well-being of millions of residents in Jalisco who depend on its water.

Zapopan is now home to the four most expensive neighborhoods in Mexico

Unaffordable housing is not merely a problem confined to the United States. According to a recent study by ITESO, Zapopan is now home to the four most expensive neighborhoods in all of Mexico.

The Zapopan neighborhoods with the highest prices are Ayamonte, Villa Magna, Zotogrande and Residencial Los Frailes. In these areas, current asking prices on homes for sale average between 44 million and 53 million pesos (US $2.6 million to $3.1 million), while residential rents in these neighborhoods can reach 85,000 pesos (US $4,930) per month.

Meanwhile, most families in the metro area lack the income required to purchase property valued at only 1 million pesos (US $58,000), according to the most recent Economic Analysis Bulletin of the ITESO Business School (ENI).

It’s worth noting that ITESO’s methodology relies exclusively on purchase prices and rents advertised online, which results in an upward bias in the data. This is because many lesser-value properties geared to low- and middle-income residents are not marketed online and therefore not included in ITESO’s calculations.

That issue aside, the data ITESO aggregated from Jalisco was collected in the same manner as other regions, so the lofty prices observed in Zapopan are valid for comparison purposes.

Housing is increasingly unaffordable for locals

Additionally, there is ample anecdotal evidence to corroborate ITESO’s core finding — that the local housing supply has become unaffordable to a large share of locals. This reporter has seen both Mexican families and legal foreign residents on modest incomes evicted from their homes in the past year to make way for those able to pay higher prices.

Jalisco ranks sixth nationwide for the highest rental housing costs (29,432 pesos monthly average or US $1,707) and fourth for the most expensive home sales (8.2 million pesos on average, or about US $475,000). Further, housing prices have risen 12.5% across the metro area in the past year, outpacing gains in Mexico City (5.1%) and Monterrey (9.5%), two other high-priced markets.

The national average for monthly rents is currently 27,273 pesos (US $1,582), while the average cost of a home is about 6.8 million pesos (US $394,000).

For its part, ITESO has called for more regulation in the local housing market by city authorities to curb real estate speculation and an overemphasis on short-term rentals relative to long-term residential needs. It further notes that better financing options are needed for those currently locked out of conventional mortgages.

MND Writer Dawn Stoner is reporting from Guadalajara.

World.title: El Jalapeño: US enacts emergency guacamole rationing protocol following brief avocado import pause
World.content:
All stories in El Jalapeño are satire and not real news. Check out the original article here.

WASHINGTON, District of Columbia — Federal disaster management officials convened an emergency cabinet session last weekend to finalize strategic distribution guidelines for the nation’s rapidly depleting diplomatic reserves of mashed avocado.

The measure followed the temporary suspension of U.S. Department of Agriculture inspection services in Michoacán. This decision abruptly halted the daily northbound transit of thousands of metric tons of the single-seeded berries. Within hours of the announcement, commercial chip-and-dip supply chains across all 50 states reported critical supply compression, triggering what agriculture experts have termed an unprecedented “guacamole shortfall.”

According to documents released by the Department of Commerce, a newly drafted contingency framework has established a tiered alert system for food service establishments. Under new protocols, for example, restaurants will be legally required to dilute existing tableside preparations with up to 40% pico de gallo, sour cream or carefully seasoned air.

“We are asking the American public to maintain composure and exercise strict portion control during this period of geopolitical adjustment,” said Undersecretary of Agricultural Logistics Arthur Vance, speaking from a podium flanked by two armed guards safeguarding a glass-encased wooden bowl. “Effective midnight, the standard two-scoop serving accompanying commercial fajita platters will be temporarily capped at one measured teaspoon, available exclusively by documented proof of a birthday.”

In suburban markets across the Midwest, panic buying was reported at several upscale grocery chains, where distressed hosts queued for hours to secure individual, slightly bruised avocados. Emergency dispatchers in three states reported receiving non-emergency calls from frantic partygoers inquiring whether pulverized green Doritos, dyed mayonnaise or a paste made of minced lawn clippings and lime juice could be legally passed off as authentic guacamole without triggering guest walkouts.

At press time, backyard hosts across the nation were reportedly pivoting to high-risk contingency menus, with several trade groups advising organizers to distract guests from the empty dip bowl by dramatically increasing the tequila-to-sour-mix ratio for margaritas. However, the announced resumption of avocado exports may make such drastic measures unnecessary.
