World.title: Economy minister rejects proposed restrictions on nicotine products
World.content:
Economy Minister Erkki Keldo declined to approve a draft bill aimed at curbing the use of nicotine products among young people as the proposed changes could have a significant impact on sellers and importers.

The restrictions proposed by the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Ministry of Justice would allow nicotine pouches, nicotine strips and nicotine sprays containing no more than four milligrams of nicotine per gram to be sold in Estonia. The aim is to reduce the use of nicotine products among young people.

Erkki Keldo sent a letter to the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs on Wednesday informing it that he had declined to approve the draft bill. Keldo said the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications supports protecting the health of children and young people and curbing the illegal sale of nicotine products, but considers it important that measures restricting freedom of enterprise be sufficiently justified and proportionate.

Snus. Source: Flickr

"The changes proposed in the draft bill could significantly affect manufacturers, importers, wholesalers and retailers of nicotine products operating in Estonia. The explanatory memorandum does not adequately assess the extent of these impacts or provide a convincing justification for the proposed maximum nicotine content of 4 mg/g for nicotine-containing products related to tobacco products," Keldo said.

He noted that the draft bill's maximum nicotine content of four milligrams per gram is based on Latvia's approach, but said this was not sufficient justification for restricting freedom of enterprise.

"The explanatory memorandum does not indicate the nicotine content of nicotine pouches and other products covered by the bill currently on the Estonian market, what proportion of products currently marketed legally would comply with the proposed limit or how many businesses and products would be affected by the change," the economy minister said.

He is also dissatisfied that the draft bill does not include a comparative analysis of approaches taken by other EU member states or explain why Latvia's regulations are the best model for Estonia.

Keldo said the explanatory memorandum needs to be supplemented with a comparison of different options. The impact of the limit on the health of children and young people, the risk of accidental poisoning, businesses, the functioning of the legal market and consumer behavior should also be analyzed.

The data presented in the explanatory memorandum concern products containing e-cigarette liquid, but does not address the impact of the changes on nicotine pouches, strips, sprays and heated nicotine sticks.

"We ask that the impact assessment be expanded to separately cover all product categories regulated by the draft bill and the requirements proposed for them," the minister said.

Keldo also wants the impact of the changes on Estonian manufacturers, exports, employment and regional businesses to be examined, along with their impact on the legal market, illegal trade and tax revenue.

"Possible substitution behavior must also be analyzed, including whether some consumers could switch to products with unregulated contents or to other tobacco and nicotine products and what impact this could have on achieving the draft bill's public health objective," Keldo said.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications is also dissatisfied with a provision in the draft bill stipulating that products may not contain substances that produce a flavor or aroma other than tobacco or menthol and that only substances listed in a specific regulation may be used to provide those flavors. However, the explanatory memorandum does not explain why those particular substances are considered suitable or what costs businesses could incur in reformulating existing products.

Keldo said the bill's relationship with the planned update of the European Union's legal framework for tobacco and nicotine products should also be assessed.

The Ministry of Social Affairs has previously said that people are starting to use nicotine products at increasingly younger ages. While young people previously tried nicotine at ages 15 or 16, they are now doing so at around age 11. Nicotine pouches and e-cigarettes are the most common products used by those starting out.

Estonia's so-called Superministry building housing several government ministries. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Just over one-fifth of the nicotine products currently on the market comply with the requirements proposed in the draft bill. Around 60 percent of products would have to be reformulated, while nearly one-fifth would have to be removed from the market.

Several European countries have tightened restrictions on nicotine products in recent years. Latvia raised the minimum age for purchasing tobacco and nicotine products to 20 two years ago. No such proposal is currently under consideration in Estonia.

The new rules are planned to take effect in 2028, although the exact date will be determined as the draft bill moves through the legislative process.

World.title: Baltics' first AI factory to open in Estonia
World.content:
Dutch cloud company Nebius' Tallinn AI factory will begin operating at Greenergy Data Centers' data center this year. With a capacity of 22 megawatts, it will be the largest in the Baltics.

Nasdaq-listed Nebius announced Wednesday that it signed agreements in the second quarter to expand the company's AI infrastructure network in Europe. The first phase of its Tallinn AI factory, with a capacity of 22 megawatts, is expected to begin operating later this year.

Nebius Head of Communications Tom Blackwell said Estonia was a natural choice for the company thanks to its world-class engineers, vibrant digital economy and startup culture, as well as its ambitious plans for both artificial intelligence and the transition to clean energy.

"Nebius' Tallinn AI factory, which is being developed in partnership with Greenergy Data Centers, will provide state-of-the-art infrastructure to support Estonia's growing innovation ecosystem and help accelerate the development and adoption of artificial intelligence," he said.

Nebius' global capacity network has expanded rapidly. In Europe, the company is developing large-scale AI factories in Lappeenranta, Finland, and Béthune, France. It also has an operating center in Mäntsälä, Finland, as well as AI infrastructure projects in the United Kingdom, Spain and Iceland. Nebius' major customers include Microsoft and Meta.

Greenergy Data Centers CEO Kert Evert said Nebius' decision to choose Greenergy shows that Estonia is emerging as a competitive destination for large-scale AI infrastructure projects.

Blackwell said Nebius wants to work closely with the Estonian government, businesses and universities to develop AI skills, broaden access to artificial intelligence capabilities and strengthen Estonia's position as a leading hub for AI innovation.

Martin Salo, co-founder of Tensor Estate, a group of Estonian entrepreneurs that became a shareholder in Greenergy Data Centers last month, said the newly announced project is the first phase of a larger development that will make Estonia one of the international hubs for AI infrastructure in the coming years.

"Until now, Northern Europe's major AI factories have been concentrated primarily in Finland, Sweden and Norway, thanks to favorable electricity prices, renewable energy and a suitable climate. Having the Baltics' first AI factory come here means Estonia is joining the club of countries where the world's leading AI companies are building their infrastructure," Salo said.

In late July, Greenergy Data Centers' Head of Hyperscale Martin Rungi told ERR that attracting one major international customer to Estonia would make it significantly easier for data centers to secure additional customers, as the market develops after the first breakthrough.

In Nebius' case, however, the question of its ties to Russian technology company Yandex cannot be overlooked, as Nebius emerged after Yandex came under sanctions following Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In 2024, the company sold its Russian business units and changed its name to Nebius Group, which is headquartered in the Netherlands. Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh is also a co-founder of Yandex, but has since renounced his Russian citizenship.

A Greenergy representative said last month that such labeling was inappropriate, arguing that Nebius is probably one of the most thoroughly vetted organizations, given that despite its former ties to Russia, it has earned the trust of Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, the U.S. government and the New York Stock Exchange.

Economy minister: We have consulted security agencies

As government agencies have had concerns about Nebius and the workforce at the AI factory set to operate in Hüüru, Estonian security agencies have been consulted, Minister of Economic Affairs and Industry Erkki Keldo said.

"On the one hand, cutting-edge investments like these /.../ are certainly very welcome in Estonia, but on the other hand, the government has an obligation to look at the broader security picture. So yes, we are aware of the background, we are also in contact with Estonian authorities and will certainly minimize the risks," he said, adding that it is very important to understand that the factory is purely a private investment.

If questions arise about a company's background or workforce, there are rules and security agencies in place, and those agencies have also informed the public about potential risks and threats, the minister noted.

"We certainly have to ensure that any sensitive data, sensitive sectors and sensitive technologies do not, for example, fall into the hands of high-risk countries. And when using different types of data, we have to pay attention to whose technology we are using and where we use and store data, to ensure that it is protected. That is certainly what we are doing," Keldo said.

According to Keldo, Nebius was also discussed at a Cabinet meeting on Thursday and discussions on the matter will continue in the coming weeks.

"Estonian businesses need to understand these potential risks, including the company itself and that people with Russian backgrounds and Russian contacts are not welcomed here with overly open arms. We are certainly somewhat more vigilant about this than perhaps other European countries are, and that will remain the case in the future," Keldo said.

The article was updated to add comments from Minister Erkki Keldo.

World.title: Rare blind fish found in underground river in Iraq’s Anbar desert
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security and environmental teams have discovered a fascinating underground water system deep under the dry Anbar desert, where rare eyeless fish thrive in total darkness.

The location is in the Al-Khasfa region near Haditha, and crews traveled through a remote desert cave and sinkhole system to access running groundwater hundreds of meters under the surface.

The expedition’s footage shows little, pale fish moving in the subterranean water in the lack of sunshine.

The fish have evolved to live in darkness by losing their eyes and pigmentation, giving them a characteristic white-to-pink look.

The crew traveled more than 500 meters into the cave system despite challenging terrain and low oxygen levels.

The difference between above- and underground has piqued interest: underneath what seems to be an isolated and very arid stretch of western Iraqi desert, there is flowing freshwater and a specialized ecology.

Initial investigations have also suggested a link between the subterranean water system and the Euphrates basin, with the watercourse possibly running for a long distance under the desert.

However, environmental experts have highlighted that the blind fish themselves are not a novel finding.

Qais Najeh, the chairman of the Anbar Environment Directorate, stated that experts first confirmed the occurrence of eyeless fish in Al-Khasfa in 2010.

Similar fish have also been discovered in subterranean water near the Sheik Hadid mausoleum in Haditha district.

According to experts, the fish may grow to be roughly 49 millimeters long and survive in rather steady groundwater temperatures ranging from 20 to 22 degrees Celsius.

Their lack of vision and pigmentation are adaptations to generations of living in perpetually dark subterranean habitats.

The recent mission is nonetheless noteworthy because it has refocused attention on one of Iraq’s least-known natural ecosystems, perhaps allowing scientists to better research the subterranean water network, its geology, and the creatures that rely on it.

The fish’s severely limited environment renders it vulnerable.

Changes in groundwater levels, pollution, or human intervention might endanger a population that has acclimated to highly particular subsurface circumstances.

The Al-Khasfa location offers a unique dimension to Anbar, a region best known for its wide western desert and the Euphrates.

Hidden under that terrain lies an environment few Iraqis have ever seen: flowing subterranean water that feeds fish who have evolved to survive their entire lives without sunshine.

World.title: Israel reopens once-closed West Bank settlement
World.content:
GANIM – Israel officially reopened the West Bank settlement of Ganim on Thursday, more than 20 years after it withdrew from the community, in a move emblematic of the current government’s policy of rapid settlement expansion.

The smell of freshly-poured asphalt hung in the air above Ganim’s new and only street, where future residents and their families — who had come to help with the move — smiled at the sight of their pre-fabricated homes.

“A month ago there was nothing here. A rocky mountain, barely any trees, barely any shade. We’re arriving now,” new resident Reut Baran, 35, told AFP in front of her new home.

In a nearby truck, dozens of brand new air conditioning units still in their boxes were waiting to be installed.

Matan Berkovitch, a 25-year-old who moved into the new settlement with his wife and child, said he was satisfied with the government’s policy towards settlements as he looked around a brand new home just connected to the electric grid.

“I’m happy to be part of a time like this where there are ministers in the government who support and guide us in the right direction and know how to get things done properly,” he said.

Berkovitch’s mother Carmit, who came from Jerusalem to move him in, said another one of her sons would soon study at the religious school in the settlement, and expressed pride at their active part in the settler movement.

“Here, this is the Land of Israel. Here, we are staying forever,” Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said at the ceremony, after arriving by helicopter.

Ganim is one of four Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank that Israel evacuated under former prime minister Ariel Sharon’s disengagement plan in 2005.

The move came partly because of their isolated location in the north of the territory among many Palestinian cities and villages.

Under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, settlement construction and expansion have soared, including with the official re-establishment of three of the four evacuated communities — Ganim, Sa-Nur and Homesh.

In Ganim, about two dozen pre-fabricated homes have already been installed, while steamrollers and other construction machinery busily created new space for future houses on the hillside on Thursday.

About a hundred people from Israel and other West Bank settlements attended the ceremony, including Katz and Yossi Dagan, head of the Israeli authority in charge of settlements in the northern West Bank.

“The era of evacuation is over — from here, we only build,” Dagan said.

In the valley below, Palestinians who spoke to AFP feared Ganim’s construction would make their lives harder, or even mean eventual displacement.

On both sides of the road leading to the settlement from Israel, the army has demolished stores in recent days and blocked several dirt roads to Palestinian communities with piles of rubble.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israelis live in settlements in the territory, which are illegal under international law, among some three million Palestinians.

Violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers has increased dramatically since the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel by Hamas from the Gaza Strip.

World.title: Carrick urges Man Utd to push for more signings to boost title bid
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick has urged Manchester United to splash the cash to keep pace with their Premier League title rivals.

United have spent around £85 million ($114 million) on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow since the end of last season.

But that outlay pales in comparison to some of United’s fellow title contenders, with Manchester City, Arsenal and Chelsea all paying huge fees for high-profile signings.

Carrick knows United need more quality and depth if they are to challenge for a first English title since 2013, while also competing in the Champions League.

Remarkably, United have never spent more than £89.5 million on a single player — the fee paid for Paul Pogba in 2016.

And ahead of his first season as permanent United boss after a successful interim spell last term, Carrick called on the club’s hierarchy to push for more new recruits.

“I think we’ve done really good business and we’ve got really some top, top, top players,” Carrick told reporters on Thursday.

“We’re delighted with that. We always want to improve. We want more, we need more, we keep looking for how we can do that. That never stops.”

Carrick led United to a third-place finish in the Premier League after he replaced the sacked Ruben Amorim.

But with United so far spending less than promoted sides Coventry and Ipswich, some fans are becoming restless as their Premier League opener at Hull on August 22 looms into view.

“Money’s money, I get that. It’s still about the football, and that’s where the competition lies,” Carrick said.

“Certainly the situation is what it is as well, whether that’s finances or whatever. For now, we’ve got to make the most of it, but we’ve got to keep pushing and push everything and every boundary that we can to be able to win again.”

Asked why United were not spending on the level of other clubs, Carrick added: “To be honest, I haven’t got the answers for that. We’re working with pushing everything that we can to make the best of it.”

Having spent last season on loan with Barcelona, Marcus Rashford is back at United this week after returning from the World Cup.

Barcelona declined their option to buy the 28-year-old England forward and questions remain over his United future.

“He’s our player, and he’s a good player and he gives us something a little bit different in the group,” he said.

“Marcus can offer us so much. He has done, and he can do again, so in that respect it’s quite exciting.”

Several United players have backed the team to dethrone Arsenal as champions and the understated Carrick wouldn’t rule out a title push.

“We’ve definitely got the potential to achieve something really special,” he said.

“I’m not hiding from the fact, and we should aim to do that, but I can’t give you a definite answer on that.

“It’s certainly what we’re pushing to do because we have to, because that’s the club we are.”

World.title: Leicester’s Thai owners put troubled club up for sale: reports
World.content:
London – Former Premier League champions Leicester have been put up for sale by the club’s Thai owners, according to reports on Thursday.

Just 10 years after their fairytale Premier League title triumph, Leicester will play in English football’s third tier for only the second time in their history this season.

The Foxes, who won their first FA Cup in 2021, have endured a dire period featuring successive relegations from the Premier League in 2025 and the Championship in 2026.

Last season, they were docked six points after breaching the Football League’s profit and sustainability rules, sparking their slump into League One.

A BBC report on Thursday said Leicester’s Thai owners King Power — run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family — have commissioned a leading US investment bank to help find a buyer, with the club’s assets said to be listed at more than £200 million ($269 million).

King Power bought Leicester in a £35 million deal in 2010.

Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman following the death of his father Vichai in a helicopter crash outside the club’s King Power stadium in 2019.

Following last season’s relegation, Aiyawatt said he should shoulder the “blame” for the club’s predicament but also stressed the “structure will change”.

Russell Martin’s side kick off their promotion bid with a trip to Notts County on Saturday.

World.title: Iraq sets September 30 for US-led coalition exit as Al-Zaidi turns focus to Iran-linked militia weapons
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has reaffirmed Sept. 30 as the end date for the US-led coalition’s military mission in Iraq, putting more pressure on Baghdad to confront what could be the most difficult aspect of its sovereignty agenda: bringing weapons held by powerful Iran-aligned factions under state control.

During a meeting with U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) Commander Admiral Brad Cooper, Al-Zaidi said that October 1 will signal the beginning of a “new phase” for Iraq in the absence of a foreign coalition military presence.

The Prime Minister again emphasized the importance of the Iraqi state having exclusive control over weaponry, citing sovereignty, security, and economic growth.

Iraqi authorities said plans are already beginning to hand over remaining coalition locations, notably those in northern Iraq, to Iraqi security forces before the deadline.

The timeline is based on a 2024 agreement between Baghdad and Washington to end the coalition mission and transition the US-Iraq security partnership to direct bilateral cooperation.

However, the departure eliminates one of the primary justifications used by Iran-backed militias to preserve their weapons and strike US objectives.

Several prominent Iran-aligned factions work inside or alongside the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), who are officially part of Iraq’s governmental security system.

The PMF is made up of various groups with varying political and ideological perspectives, and it should not be viewed as a unified bloc.

However, organizations like Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and other Iran-aligned militias have maintained strong ties with Tehran and have rejected calls to relinquish their weapons.

Their actions have become an increasingly severe issue for Al-Zaidi’s administration.

Recent strikes ascribed by neighboring governments to Iran-backed forces operating from Iraqi soil have jeopardized Baghdad’s improved ties with Saudi Arabia and other Arab countries, as well as led to foreign military intervention in Iraq.

The escalation has put Baghdad in a difficult position: denouncing breaches of Iraqi sovereignty while also facing demands from its neighbors to prohibit armed groups from exploiting Iraqi territory to threaten them.

For Al-Zaidi, the September 30 withdrawal may fundamentally alter that equation.

Once the coalition mission is over, Iran-aligned elements will find it more difficult to justify maintaining autonomous military capabilities by citing the presence of foreign soldiers.

Baghdad will then have to decide whether it can impose its notion of a single armed authority in Iraq.

That problem is especially critical since Al-Zaidi is aiming to shift Iraq’s focus from decades of war and proxy conflict to rebuilding, investment, and closer economic ties with the US, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, and other foreign allies.

Repeated militia assaults risk undercutting that plan by raising investor anxiety and subjecting Iraq to reprisal for military choices that its government claims were not authorized.

The coalition’s exit therefore means more than just the removal of foreign troops.

It might serve as the catalyst for a far wider debate over who eventually controls Iraq’s armaments and war-making choices.

Baghdad will find it easy to declare complete sovereignty on October 1.

Demonstrating it will be far more difficult.

If Al-Zaidi is serious about guaranteeing that no foreign military presence stays in Iraq, the same sovereignty concept will increasingly be expected to apply to armed forces whose allegiance, weapons, or choices are not under the control of the Iraqi state.

Bringing such weapons under state control might prove to be one of the most important—and difficult—tests of Al-Zaidi’s leadership.

World.title: UAE’s ADNOC helps keep Iraqi oil flowing through Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is collaborating with the UAE’s ADNOC and other international energy merchants to maintain crude exports flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, as Baghdad seeks methods to secure key oil income amidst ongoing disruptions to Gulf shipping.

Iraq’s State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) reported that Abu Dhabi National Oil Company is one of the firms purchasing Iraqi petroleum and successfully transporting shipments over the strait.

According to Bloomberg, ADNOC’s trading arm is supplying Iraqi oil to Asian refiners via a shuttle system meant to mitigate the dangers involved with shipping bigger tankers into the Gulf.

Under the deal, smaller boats carry Iraqi Basrah oil via Hormuz before transferring the cargo to bigger tankers for delivery to Asian markets.

Tracking devices may also be turned off throughout sections of the route as ships negotiate the increasingly tough maritime environment.

The agreement is especially significant for Iraq, which relies heavily on oil exports to fund government expenditures.

The disruption at Hormuz has placed pressure on Baghdad to find methods to preserve exports while also ensuring the funds required to satisfy wages and other governmental commitments.

ADNOC’s cooperation gives Iraq another path to keep petroleum to overseas buyers while regular tanker operations are limited.

The move also follows the UAE’s exit from OPEC and OPEC+, which has given Abu Dhabi more control over its oil production and commercial strategy as it aims to boost output, trading activity, and energy income.

For Iraq, the immediate imperative is different but as important: keep crude flowing.

Baghdad is seeking longer-term options via Turkey and even the Mediterranean to minimize its reliance on Hormuz. However, until such routes are completely built, Iraq remains very vulnerable to Gulf disturbances.

The utilization of shuttle tankers and ship-to-ship transfers provides a temporary but potentially essential solution, allowing Iraq to keep access to Asian clients while also preserving the oil earnings that underpin much of the country’s economy.

World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: CAG finds 98% shortfall in Green India Mission forest cover targets, red-flags multiple lapses
World.content:
The Comptroller and Auditor General raised concerns about the inadequacies within the Green India Mission program, noting that the goal of increasing forest cover was far from realized over a decade. The audit pointed to significant issues in planning and financial oversight, which severely undermined the mission's objectives. Key vulnerable areas were neglected during afforestation, diminishing efforts to combat climate change.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Red-flagging lapses in the countryâs ongoing programme to increase and improve green cover, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has pointed out non-achievement of forest cover targets, noting that the observed increase in forest cover fell short by nearly 98% during 10 years of implementation (2015-16 to 2024-25) of the Green India Mission (GIM).Releasing the performance audit report on the Mission, CAG highlighted the wrong choice of landscape for planting trees, absence of convergence of various schemes to increase green cover, financial mismanagement, improper planning, lack of coordination and deficient monitoring behind non-achievement of the GIMâs goals.The broad objectives under the Mission were to increase forest/tree cover, improve the quality of forest/non-forest lands, improve ecosystem services, including biodiversity, hydrological services and carbon sequestration because of forest land/non-forest land, and to increase forest-based livelihood income of households living in and around forests.Underlining its key audit findings, the CAG in its report tabled in Parliament on Wednesday said, âAs against the target of 1.4 million hectares (mha), improvement of forest cover quality was observed in only 0.11 mha (nearly 92% shortfall). Similarly, an increase in forest cover was observed in only 0.03 mha as against the target of 1.4 mha (nearly 98% shortfall).âIt also noted that despite vulnerability being a key criterion, landscapes with low to moderate priority were selected over those more vulnerable to climate change for afforestation under the Mission.The performance audit examined the planning, implementation and monitoring of the GIM interventions in 16 states and UTs for which physical and financial targets were approved by the environment ministry during the period 2015-16 to 2024-25.Pointing out deficient monitoring, the CAG noted that 14 states even failed to provide required public web links for transparency. It flagged that audit evaluations revealed inflated data and overstated achievements, and GIS analysis showed that 70% of sampled sites had no noticeable changes attributable to GIM.

World.title: 'No clear information': Nepal ‘loses’ papers of centuries-old treaty defining borders with India
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Nepal has apparently lost the decades-old original of the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, a document that largely defined the Himalayan nation's boundaries with British India, its foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Monday.

Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives recently that while some treaty-related documents are held in the National Archives, their status as the original official documents remains unclear.

âThe Government of Nepal does not have clear information on whether we possess the official treaty documents. There are records showing that some documents related to certain treaties are kept at the National Archives.

But we do not have clear information as to whether those are the actual official treaties,â Khanal said.

He said Nepal does have documents related to the 1816 Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship with India.

The disclosure comes amid renewed tensions over the Nepal-India border after India and China agreed to reopen the Lipulekh trade route. Nepal claims Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura and Kalapani as its territories, while India maintains that they are part of its territory.





This becomes significant, as the dispute resurfaced recently after Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Kathmandu had raised with India concerns over alleged encroachment, including in Lipulekh. Shah said both sides had agreed to examine the issue through historians, surveyors and territorial experts and resolve it through diplomatic talks. He also called for the UK to be involved, citing its role in shaping the region's borders during the colonial era.

Shah said Nepal had found that ânot only had India encroached on Nepal's land, but Nepal had also encroached on India's land in multiple places.â

India rejected any role for third parties, with MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal having said âthere is no role for any third parties in a bilateral matter between India and Nepal.â He said nearly 98% of the boundary had been demarcated, with remaining issues including stretches affected by the shifting Gandak River and cross-border occupation or encroachment on no-man's land.

India has also rejected Nepal's claims over Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura as âneither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence.

â

The issue of missing treaty documents has been around for years. In 2016, when the Eminent Personsâ Group on Nepal-India Relations began discussions on reviewing or replacing the 1950 treaty, Nepal tried to locate the original but failed to find it. The government subsequently provided the Bhekh Bahadur Thapa-led committee with another copy of the treaty.

The matter later prompted a parliamentary inquiry. On July 22, the Delegated Legislation and Governance Committee of Nepal's National Assembly concluded that the original copies of both the Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship could not be found in the country.

The committee said it searched various locations where historical records could have been preserved, including libraries, archives and government repositories, as well as the Department of Archaeology, Narayanhiti Palace Museum, Ministry of Law and Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The matter had also come up in Parliament in 2019. Then Foreign Minister Pradeep Gyawali said the government had copies of both treaties but was unsure whether they were originals. âWe have both treaties, but we have to forensically verify whether these copies are originals or not,â Gyawali had said. âWe are also trying to find historical documents and maps in India and the United Kingdom.â

Khanal's remarks came as he outlined a broader plan to review Nepal's existing international agreements.

He said the country has 655 treaties and agreements, including 412 bilateral and 243 multilateral agreements.

Of these, 55 have already been concluded or amended, while the government plans to review the remaining 600 based on their necessity and relevance. Khanal said older or inactive agreements would be reviewed, amended or renewed in coordination with the countries or international organisations concerned.

âUnder the general principles of international treaty law, the review, amendment, or renewal of any bilateral or multilateral treaty or agreement depends on the mutual consent and approval of the concerned state parties or relevant international organisations,â Khanal said.

He added that the government would undertake the exercise with the cooperation and approval of the relevant countries and international organisations.

What is the Sugauli Treaty?

The Sugauli Treaty was agreed between Nepal and the British East India Company after the Anglo-Nepalese War. It was signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816, with the agreement establishing the basis for Nepal's territorial boundary with British India.

The treaty required Nepal to cede significant territories to the East India Company and renounce claims to lands west of the Kali River, while also setting out provisions governing relations between Nepal and the Company.

World.title: 2027 UP assembly elections: How parties are vying for Dalit votes amid Mayawati’s shrinking base
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Dalit politics in

is at a crossroads. For a very long time, Mayawati and her Bahujan Samaj Party were synonymous with the idea of Dalit vote in UP. Not any more. Mayawatiâs BSP today is a much weaker force.

The last three elections in the state have pushed Mayawati, the four-time chief minister of UP, to the margins of state politics. This has opened up the Dalit space and triggered an interesting scramble among political parties for a slice of the Dalit pie in the 2027 assembly elections.

So, we have the BJP playing the name-change game in Bhadohi and organising a 7-month campaign to honour 15th-century saint-poet Sant Ravi Das. Then we have Samajwadi Party chief

announcing 14 extra seats for the Dalits to cement his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) politics.

Congress too is trying to win back voters it lost decades ago. Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, who is trying to consolidate his own space in the state.

As Uttar Pradesh heads towards 2027, the question is: if the BSP continues to lose ground, where does Mayawatiâs old support base go and which of her rivals stands to gain the most?

From 206 seats to one: How BSP lost ground

The BSPâs rise in UP politics was as dramatic as its fall. The party was founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984 with the idea of giving Dalits and other marginalized communities an independent voice.





Mayawati, who emerged as his political successor, took the BSP to great heights in Uttar Pradesh. Under her leadership, the BSP won a majority on its own in the 2007 assembly elections, winning 206 seats with a vote share of 30.43%.

Dalits, who constitute around 21% of UPâs population as per the 2021 census, have for years been the core base of Mayawatiâs Bahujan Samaj Party. But that dynamic has now changed.

BSP is a much weaker force today. Mayawati has failed to mobilise Dalit support for her BSP in the last two elections in the state, thereby opening up the space for other political contenders.

In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.

The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawatiâs dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her partyâs vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSPâs influence among Dalits.

As Mayawati gears up for the 2027 assembly challenge, she faces an uphill road. The BSP chief has not just lost support of voters, but also control over her party. So, when Mayawati issued a stern message that all the candidates for the upcoming poll will be finalised by her and not by her nephew Akash Anand, it was an indication of the internal tussle in her party.

Akash Anand, who has been in and out of Mayawatiâs favour in the past, launched the partyâs 2027 assembly poll campaign from Sadabad in Hathras this week.

Mayawati, who has often been accused of helping the BJP, has ruled out any pre-poll alliance. She has claimed that some candidates have already been finalised for the upcoming assembly elections. Mayawati has asked party cadres to start rebuilding the party and drum up OBC support ahead of the polls. The cadres have apparently been asked to remind people of the party's past governance and convince them that the real benefit and welfare of the OBC community lie with the BSP and its "iron lady government".

Mayawati, however, must consider that it will be difficult for the BSP to come back to power only by holding on to its core Dalit vote alone. It will have to recreate the Dalit-OBC combination that originally carried Mayawati to power in Lucknow with a majority of her own.

BJP's Dalit outreach gets sharper ahead of 2027

One interesting fallout of BSPâs decline has been the BJPâs aggressive outreach to woo the Dalits. When Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath announced the renaming of Bhadohi district as Sant Ravidas Nagar last month, he put the BJP right at the middle of the Dalit outreach battle ahead of 2027 polls.

The move also revived an old political contest over name-change politics. Mayawati was the one who had renamed Bhadohi as Sant Ravidas Nagar in December 1997. Akhilesh Yadav restored the old name in 2014. Now, by bringing Sant Ravidas Nagar back, Yogi sought to make a bigger political point, accusing the SP of erasing a Dalit symbol while positioning the BJP as a party willing to restore it.

Mayawati publicly welcomed the decision, a rare moment of agreement with the ruling party.

She was quick, however, to remind voters that it was her government that had changed the district's name in the first place and that the decision was later reversed under Akhilesh.

The party realises that Dalit votes are up for grabs and hence is going all out to woo them. The partyâs 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyanâ appears planned to coincide with assembly elections in two key states, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, early next year.

Both these states have a sizeable population of Dalits who play an important role in many constituencies. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP and its ally Apna Dal (Soneylal) together bagged 63 Scheduled Caste (SC) seats compared to 20 won by the then Samajwadi Party-led opposition alliance. But the 2024 Lok Sabha polls changed the dynamics, with the SP and the Congress winning 43 of the 80 seats in the state and pushing the BJP to make an aggressive outreach.

The loss of Faizabad seat to SP's Awadhesh Prasad, a Pasi leader, was particularly significant and gave Akhilesh Yadav fresh ammunition for his PDA pitch.

Earlier this year, the Yogi Adityanath government approved the âDr B R Ambedkar Murti Vikas Yojna" under which Rs 1 crore is to be allocated to each of the state's 403 assembly constituencies for the beautification and development of statues of social reformers.

The BJP's efforts to woo Dalits has also been visible in its recent Cabinet expansion. Of the six new ministers inducted into the Yogi government, two were Dalits, Krishna Paswan from the Pasi community and Surendra Singh Daler from the Valmiki community. Three others were from OBC groups. Two non-Yadav OBC ministers were also given independent charge.

The BJP's primary task ahead of 2027 would be to hold on to the non-Jatav Dalit support it built over the past decade and prevent a repeat of 2024.

SPâs Dalit outreach

The 2024 Lok Sabha elections also showed that the Dalits in UP were ready to back other political parties who wooed them. Dalit support played a key role in the spectacular success of Akhilesh Yadavâs Samajwadi Party, which won 37 seats in 2024.

Together with its alliance partner Congress, the INDIA bloc won 43 of the 80 seats in the state, pushing the BJP on the back foot. Akhilesh Yadav, who has centred his politics around PDA (Pichhde, Dalits and Aplasankhyaks), gained from his Dalit outreach in the 2024 elections.

His Samajwadi Party fielded two Dalit candidates from general seats. While one of them went on to win the all-important Faizabad seat, the other lost by just 10,585 votes to the BJP in Meerut.

How Samajwadi Party performed when they contested independently

Little wonder, in the run-up to the 2027 assembly elections, Akhilesh has already announced plans to field 14 Dalit candidates from general seats. Uttar Pradesh has 84 seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and two for Scheduled Tribes.

With 14 more candidates on general seats, the total tally of reserved candidates for SP will increase to 100. This will help reinforce his message to the Dalits in line with his PDA politics.

The move will also help the SP shed the narrative of being a Muslim-Yadav party.

Congress tries to reclaim lost ground

has made it clear that Dalits would now play a 'central role' in Congress. Before Mayawati and the BSP built their massive Dalit vote bank in the 1990s, Congress was the primary choice for Uttar Pradesh's Dalits.

For nearly three decades after that, Congress was almost pushed out of UP politics.

Rahul Gandhi has started his road to the UP election by acknowledging that the party had failed to take the right steps for the community in the 1980s and 1990s. He even praised Kanshi Ram for bringing Dalits together and giving the community a sense of confidence.

Rahul has also made the Constitution a regular part of his social justice pitch.

He is often seen carrying the red book of the Constitution while warning that constitutional rights and reservation are under threat. He has repeatedly invoked BR Ambedkar in the same pitch, asserting that Congress wants to position itself as a guardian of the Constitution.

The party has also put a Dalit leader in charge of Uttar Pradesh. Rajendra Pal Gautam, who heads the Congressâs Scheduled Castes Department, has been appointed UP in-charge ahead of the 2027 polls.

Interestingly, Gautam had also made an unsuccessful attempt to meet Mayawati at her Lucknow residence earlier this year.

Whether the party will be able to translate this outreach into votes remains to be seen.

Chandrashekhar Azad adds another claimant

Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, whose 2024 victory from Nagina made him a prominent figure in UPâs Dalit politics. Unlike BJP, SP or Congress, Azad is trying to build an independent space outside the BSP. His challenge now is to take that appeal beyond one constituency and build an organisation strong enough to matter across the state in 2027.

That is what makes the coming assembly election in Uttar Pradesh interesting. For decades, politics in Uttar Pradesh has revolved around caste. Political parties build their electoral strategies around social coalitions, loyalty of communities and traditional vote base.

Mayawati may no longer command the Dalit vote the way she once did, but that vote bank has not disappeared. It simply has more claimants. And in 2027, where those voters eventually move could make a significant difference.

World.title: 'No NALSAR 2026 graduate will be enrolled as advocate': BCI amid CJI convocation invite row
World.content:
The decision follows a campaign by the students againsts the participation of CJI Surya Kant in the convocation ceremony.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has directed all state bar councils to halt the enrolment of any 2026 law graduate from NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, as an advocate until further orders. This follows an alleged organised campaign against the participation of Chief Justice Surya Kant in the universityâs convocation ceremony.The directive was issued by bar council chairman Manan Kumar Mishra, who said the Council had taken note of reports and material in the public domain regarding an organised campaign at NALSAR's convocation ceremony.The bar council has also sought an authenticated factual report from the university within three days and said the matter will be considered on August 19, after the vice-chancellor submits the report.The council has asked NALSAR to identify, on the basis of verifiable material, the persons allegedly instrumental in initiating, drafting, circulating, coordinating or mobilising the campaign. It has sought details of those involved in organising meetings, communicating with the media, administering social media or organised groups used for coordination, or proposing or mobilising any call for boycott, obstruction, disruption or organised non-participation in the convocation or any programme connected with the CJI.The bar council has also sought information on whether any student body, student bar council, studentsâ union or other recognised student organisation was involved in initiating, approving, coordinating or circulating the campaign. The university has also been asked to specify whether any faculty member, research scholar, alumnus or outsider participated in initiating, drafting, coordinating, advising or facilitating the campaign.In addition, the council has requested copies of relevant resolutions, minutes, agendas or other official records of meetings connected with the matter, and details of whether permission was sought or granted for any protest or organised activity and whether university rules governing student conduct or official functions were invoked.At the same time, the bar council clarified that participation in the representation or campaign would not automatically result in disqualification from enrolment. It said a distinction must be maintained between those who merely signed or supported a representation and those who organised or coordinated the campaign or proposed or mobilised an actual boycott, obstruction or disruption.

World.title: From erotic fantasy to Indian identity, a famous Italian calendar finds a new story
World.content:
In 1966, a photograph of a woman in underwear arrived at the Vatican. The fashion imagery might seem rather tame by today's standards, but it was enough to provoke an official complaint from the Holy See to an Italian tire company called Pirelli.

The Milan-based tire manufacturer had just begun producing these exclusive, high-fashion calendars, simply called 'The Cal', as a trade gift for its top clients â the idea being to give VIPs something a cut above the cheap pin-up calendars that were standard fare in garages and tire shops at the time.

But the condemnation had the opposite effect. Rather than suppressing the calendar, it generated enormous publicity, transforming a niche corporate giveaway into one of the world's most coveted cultural status symbols.

Within a few years, the calendar became less a marketing gimmick and more an annual referendum on where European ideas of beauty, sex and provocation stood. Over the decades, figures from Naomi Campbell, Cindy Crawford and Kate Moss to PenÃ©lope Cruz, Serena Williams and Yoko Ono have been framed within its pages by some of the world's most influential photographers.

But sixty-two years and a great many controversies later, the most recent edition of that same calendar is shot not on a Mediterranean beach or a Manhattan studio, but in the forts and villages of Rajasthan and the mean streets of Old Delhi, even featuring everyday barbers and artisans.





The 2027 Pirelli Calendar is dedicated to India. For the first time, it features an all-India cast and is shot entirely in the country, built around the idea of Indian identity. So alongside glamorous portraits of celebrities like television host and author Padma Lakshmi, actress Aditi Rao Hydari, sitarist Anoushka Shankar and supermodel Bhavitha Mandava are some 200 ordinary Indians, from dancers and street artists to musicians and craftspeople.

One half of the 2027 Pirelli Calendar features Indian celebrities photographed by Norwegian photographer SÃ¸lve SundsbÃ¸ I Picture credit: Alessandro Scotti

The project began as a collaboration between Norwegian photographer SÃ¸lve SundsbÃ¸ and Raghu Rai, modern India's most celebrated photojournalist known for chronicling the country's many faces and contradictions over several decades. Rai died in April shortly after the project began. His daughter, photographer Avani Rai, stepped in to complete it and in doing so changed its direction. What had been conceived as a studio shoot moved outdoors into the neighbourhoods her father spent his career documenting, from Kinari Bazar and Yamuna Ghat to the streets of Old Delhi.

When asked how a project like the Pirelli Calendar sits alongside her reportage-driven practice, Avani, speaking to TOI, gently rejects the premise of the question. Genre, she argues, describes where a photograph ends up, not how it is made. What remains constant, whether in documentary work or a fashion commission, is the attempt to stay honest to what is in front of the camera. "Curiosity, presence and empathy are not specific to one genre of photography.

The Pirelli Calendar asked me to bring those values into a different context. I wasnât interested in making images that simply looked beautiful. I wanted them to feel alive. To hold the same emotional honesty that I search for in every photograph I make," says Avani whose mother, conservation architect Gurmeet Rai, also appears in the calendar.

Even to this day, The Cal's physical copies are not sold publicly; Pirelli limits production to roughly 20,000 copies annually and they are sent as corporate gifts to monarchs, CEOs, prime ministers, top celebrities, fashion icons and the like.

But why India? SundsbÃ¸ says it was a long-held ambition within Pirelli. His contribution came from a very different vantage pointâthat of an outsider conscious of his own limitations. "The fact that Avani and Raghu Raiâs images would be one half of the Calendar enabled me to concentrate on portraits. That's a smaller and more realistic task for a visitor than capturing the whole soul of a nation.I didnât try to decide what âIndiannessâ should mean.

Especially not as the guest that I am. I tried to cast people I admire, women who have inspirational talent," says SundsbÃ¸.

The edition also marks the first time Pirelli has commissioned two photographers to share a calendar. What makes the India edition notable is not simply that it swaps eroticism for cultural identity; the calendar has been moving in that direction for years. Rather, it is the first edition shaped by two intertwined perspectives: an outsider looking in and a daughter completing her father's final project in the streets he loved.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"I used to think inheritance was about continuing someoneâs work. Now I think itâs about continuing their way of being in the world. The patience they lived with. The integrity they carried. The generosity with which they met people. Those are the things that survive," says Avani.

"Completing the calendar gave me a sense of continuity. It wasnât about recreating him or holding onto the past. I understood that what he had really left me wasnât an archive or even a body of work. It was a practice of being alive to the world," she adds.

World.title: Real 'Sena' battle: 'Sin' of defection should not be rewarded, Uddhav camp tells SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Uddhav Thackeray-led

(UBT) on Thursday told the

that constitutional provisions cannot be interpreted in a way that encourages the very conduct the anti-defection law was enacted to prevent. Appearing before a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant during the fifth day of hearings on the party symbol dispute, senior advocate

argued that the Constitution should not be read in a manner that rewards defections and weakens democratic safeguards.

A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing petitions filed by the Thackeray faction challenging the Election Commission's decision to recognise the Eknath Shinde-led faction as the real Shiv Sena and allot it the party's name and the 'bow and arrow' symbol.

"You can't interpret the provisions of the Constitution to give encouragement to the very sin which the anti-defection law sought to prevent," Sibal told the bench.

Sibal argued that the legal test for disqualification is fundamentally different from the test for determining whether a political party has split. "Split is completely different, and disqualification is completely different," he said, adding that subsequent events may be relevant in disqualification proceedings but not when deciding whether a split had occurred.

He told the court that the case presented an opportunity to lay down the law for the future of Indian democracy.





Calling the situation a "very sad state of affairs", Sibal said governments often ensure that disqualification proceedings remain undecided.

When he argued that the burden of preserving democracy rested on the judiciary, the bench responded that it was a "collective responsibility". "We are conscious of our role. The Constitution is lived by the people," the bench observed.

The Chief Justice added, "Let us not underestimate our other institutions.

They are also quite committed."

Sibal replied that while Parliament could continue enacting laws, it was ultimately the Supreme Court that had the authority to interpret and test those laws against the Constitution.

The hearing has been adjourned and will continue on 18 August.

During Wednesday's proceedings, the Supreme Court had observed that it would first have to determine whether a split had occurred within the Shiv Sena, noting that a division could originate in the legislature party and later spread through the party organisation and primary membership.

Responding to that observation, Sibal argued that a split in the legislature party could not by itself amount to a split in the political party. "As a proposition of law, a split in the political party can never arise merely from a split in the legislature party. That has been decided by the Constitution Bench (in a judgment)," he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He also questioned the Election Commission's approach in deciding whether there was a genuine dispute within the Shiv Sena and whether the faction approaching it had exhausted the internal remedies available under the party constitution.

Sibal challenged the Commission's assessment of the Shiv Sena's organisational structure, including the powers of the party chief and the process for appointing organisational office-bearers.

The bench is hearing two petitions filed by the Thackeray faction in 2024 challenging the Election Commission's order allotting the 'bow and arrow' symbol to the Eknath Shinde-led faction and the Commission's 17 February 2023 decision recognising it as the original Shiv Sena.

World.title: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy promises better life for urban poor
World.content:
Laying the foundation stone for Indiramma Towers in Kukatpally on Friday evening in Hyderabad, Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy took a swipe at the opposition parties even as he listed out the achievements of his government to benefit the urban poor.

“Telangana has seen a rapid burst of growth that is not limited to urban areas over the past two years that outpaces that of the previous 10 years. Nearly 55 lakh families are benefiting from the free 200 units of electricity which translates into savings for their families,” said Mr. Reddy addressing a public meeting after laying the foundation stone.

The Indiramma Towers scheme envisages affordable housing for poor with four 10-storey towers coming up with each tower having 120 houses with 12 flats on each floor.

“The earlier government promised houses for the poor but built them 40-50 km away from the city. People live in the city; they have businesses, shops and offices here. How will they survive if they have to commute for long hours? This 11-acre land parcel is very expensive but we want to build houses here for one lakh families so that they have a better life in the city. I don’t care about expenses,” said Mr. Reddy as a large number of women seated in the audience cheered.

“As your brother, I will stand by you to make your dream of owning a home a reality,” the Chief Minister told the women.

Highlighting the schemes launched for the empowerment of women, the CM said that distribution of ‘Indiramma Saris’, free bus travel for women on RTC buses, bank linked loans worth ₹65,000 crore for self-help groups, ownership of buses through Self-Help Groups, establishment of petrol bunks and solar plants by women groups and stalls at Shilparamam for self-help groups to sell their products brought a big transformation in the lives of the women in the State. “We are also providing fine-quality rice to 3.28 crore people, supplying 200 units of free electricity to every poor family and cooking gas for just ₹500,” said Mr. Reddy.

Referring to the disputes about lands under Section 22, Mr. Revanth Reddy assured that no one would lose their ownership of lands and there is no need to worry. The Chief Minister appealed to people not to believe in the false propaganda spread by some on social media on the prohibited lands.

World.title: Coimbatore CBI court convicts four in two elephant electrocution cases
World.content:
The Chief Judicial Magistrate Court in Coimbatore, which is the Special Court for CBI cases, on Thursday convicted four persons in two cases of electrocution of wild elephants in Erode and Coimbatore districts.

Chief Judicial Magistrate K. Sivakumar awarded the punishments in the cases, which were taken over and investigated by the CBI from the Forest Department, based on Madras High Court direction.

In the first case, the court sentenced Mathappa (38) and his father Kalayya (78) to three-and-a-half years of imprisonment for electrocuting a male wild elephant in Thalavadi in Jeerahalli forest range in Erode district in 2020.

The father-son duo cultivated crops such as ragi and paddy in six acres. They powered the iron cable fence around the farm by illegally connecting it to an overhead low tension powerline, resulting in the electrocution of a 10-year-old tusker on December 19, 2020.

The court found the two persons guilty for the crime and awarded a fine of ₹25,000 each along with the punishment.

In another case, the court sentenced Aruchamy (64) and his wife Thilagavathy of Thennamanallur near Thondamuthur in Coimbatore district to five years of imprisonment for the electrocution of a male elephant within the jurisdiction of the Boluvampatti forest range in 2021.

The couple cultivated paddy and other crops in a little over seven acres at Semmedu. They used the electricity connection given for agricultural purposes to power a fence in the farm illegally, leading to the electrocution of a 25-year-old tusker on January 5, 2021. The court also slapped a fine of ₹25,000 each on them.

Pronouncing the judgements, the judge observed that the crime committed by the convicts for their personal selfishness resulted in the death of a voiceless creature - elephant. When farming is done in forest areas where elephants naturally roam, it is normal for them to feed on nearby crops to satisfy their hunger. Hence, the act committed by the convicts was not one that warrants a reduction in punishment, he observed.

Public Prosecutor V. Surendra Mohan appeared for the CBI in the two cases.

World.title: Indian Coast Guard ramps up coastal security, fishermen safety via awareness programmes
World.content:
As part of the celebrations marking its 50th year, the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) has bolstered its coastal security and fisherman safety in Andhra Pradesh, by conducting nearly 1,000 Community Interaction Programmes (CIPs) across the State throughout 2025–26.

The initiative engaged more than 25,000 fishermen, strengthening the synergy between maritime security agencies and the coastal community, according to a statement on Thursday.

Conducted in close coordination with the Andhra Pradesh State Fisheries Department, Marine Police, and district administration, the programme aims to heighten awareness regarding maritime safety, search and rescue procedures, and sustainable fishing practices.

“Spanning the entire 1,050-km coastline, the campaign educates fishermen on critical safety measures, including the mandatory use of life jackets, communication equipment, and emergency distress devices”, the release said.

The focal point of these interactions is the promotion of the ICG’s toll-free emergency number 1554, ensuring rapid response during distress at sea. Furthermore, fishermen have been sensitised to the ecological and economic importance of the annual fishing ban, highlighting its role in protecting breeding grounds and securing future livelihoods.

“The enthusiastic participation of the fishing community has been instrumental in enhancing information sharing and bolstering our coastal surveillance efforts,” a senior ICG official noted.

These programmes also included demonstrations on first aid, cyclone preparedness, and safe navigation, fostering a more resilient and security-aware coastal ecosystem.

Looking ahead, the ICG plans to further expand its engagement across all coastal districts. Future initiatives will place greater emphasis on digital weather awareness and youth engagement in fishing villages.

The Coast Guard aims to transform every fisherman into an informed partner in safeguarding lives and securing the nation’s maritime frontiers, steadfastly upholding its motto, Vayam Rakshamah (We Protect), the release added.

World.title: As e-KYC deadline nears, consumers line up at cooking gas agencies
World.content:
With the State-run oil marketing companies (OMC) pushing August 16 as the deadline for finishing the e-KYC process for domestic liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) consumers are rushing to the agencies to get it done. Some agencies witnessed around 60-70 persons just on Thursday.

Distributors said that many of those, who came in had landed up despite having already completed the process. "I panicked because I got a message asking me to do the e-KYC. It is not a question of subsidy but the threat of having to buy cooking gas at commercial rates," said a consumer.

Around 88% of e-KYC has been completed so far in the State. Surendra Babu, a consumer, said that he had been busy with day to day affairs and hence couldn't finish the e-KYC. "I tried doing it at home. But found that my Aadhar card had not been linked with my LPG ID. Some ten years ago there was a similar drive. I wonder what happened to the data that we had submitted at that time," he said.

For some consumers the death of the person in whose name the connection was given, has caused them to change the name of the connection. "My mother died sometime ago. There were a lot of official business to take care including closing her bank account. By the time the time I got to the gas connection, the war started and we could not do any name transfer. Only recently, we changed it and have now done e-KYC," said a consumer.

Official sources said that e-KYC was being mandated to ensure delivery of cylinders to the correct consumers. "Delivery of cylinders will not be affected in any manner even if e-KYC is not completed," said a senior OMC official.

An industry source said that the Union government is heavily subsidising the product for domestic consumers. It cannot allow that amount to be squandered away by people who do not need subsidy. Consumer activist T. Sadagopan hoped that the last date would be extended. "The public is being unnecessarily put to hardship due to this. OMCs should hold special camps for this purpose in public places," he added.

World.title: Rahul scoffs at PM’s foreign policy; Kharge says being ‘Modi bhakt’ will not help country
World.content:
Congress president and Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday (August 13, 2026) attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah for allegedly avoiding the Opposition in Parliament for 20 days, while Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi described the BJP-RSS as a “bunch of jokers”.

Mr. Gandhi mocked Mr. Modi’s handling of foreign policy as being reduced to hugging world leaders. Speaking at the national convention of Rachnatmak Congress, a wing of the party which engages with civil society activists and organisations, the Opposition leader said it was “ignorance” to believe that foreign policy was about embracing leaders.

He then hugged Rachnatmak Congress chief Sandeep Dikshit to illustrate his point. “Imagine the ignorance… where did he get the idea that foreign policy was about hugging leaders,” Mr. Gandhi said, questioning the Prime Minister’s approach to international relations.

“Ek cheez pooch sakta hoon? Meloni samajh ke toh nahi pakda tha?” Mr. Dikshit said, dragging in a reference to Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. Several social media posts later slammed the Congress for “misogynistic and sexist” comments.

Mr. Gandhi said India could not be understood through a fixed political “order” imposed by the BJP-RSS, but only by allowing the country to express itself. Referring to the student protests at Jantar Mantar, he said the students wanted to express themselves, while the government wanted to impose “order” and prevent them from doing so.

“Their political philosophy is to impose an order on India which benefits them and certain other people. Our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” Mr. Gandhi said, adding, “We will drive them crazy.”

He said the Opposition’s fight against the government would continue without hatred or violence. “Till the day Mr. Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah don’t give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep. We will keep them awake,” Mr. Gandhi said, describing the struggle as one rooted in “love, brotherhood and ahimsa”.

Mr. Gandhi also attacked the RSS, claiming that it had ceased to represent its original social base and had become an “instrument of large capital”, naming industrialists Gautam Adani and Mukesh Ambani. He alleged that the “corporatisation” of the RSS had culminated during the Modi government.

He questioned why Mr. Modi did not hold press conferences, saying that after meeting him, he had concluded that the Prime Minister “cannot go before the media”.

Calling the BJP-RSS a “bunch of jokers” and “clowns”, Mr. Gandhi said its leaders had no understanding of India’s philosophy or history. “A lot of people in India are behaving as cowards before a cowardly force,” he said, arguing that understanding contemporary India required listening to its “expression”.

‘Not platform for publicity’

Earlier, Mr. Kharge said Parliament was not a platform for the Prime Minister’s publicity but a forum where different viewpoints should be heard, debated and answered within democratic norms. “Being a Modi bhakt alone will not benefit the country. We have to care about the country,” he said.

The Congress chief accused Mr. Modi and Mr. Shah of avoiding Parliament for 20 days and said Mr. Shah’s offer of a discussion shortly before the end of the session was a “deception”.

“Mr. Shah did not become Home Minister to sit in his chamber,” Mr. Kharge said, demanding that he face Opposition questions over the police action against students in Delhi.

He said the government was increasingly relying on “lathis and suppressing voices”, while accusing the BJP and RSS of pursuing a politics of division.

World.title: Bengaluru, parking car outside your house? Pay up to ₹25,000 based on car you own
World.content:
Bengaluru residents who use public roads for parking outside their homes may have to pay an annual fee of up to ₹25,000 or more, depending on the type of car, under the draft Greater Bengaluru Authority (Parking) Rules, 2026, published by the Karnataka Government on Tuesday.

However, it states that residential parking on streets other than arterial and sub-arterial roads may be allowed only for vehicles that have been issued a residential parking permit by the respective city corporation. The permits, however, will be given to only residents of residential buildings that are not in violation of minimum parking requirements specified in the building bylaws.

So, if a resident living in a house with inadequate parking inside the premises, as per building bylaws, parks their car on the roads in front of their houses, it will be deemed illegal and may attract fines under the illegal parking violation by the Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP).

To avoid that, citizens will have to resort to parking at a facility (off-street parking), for which the charges are exorbitant too.

SUV? Pay ₹25,000

The draft rules propose a minimum annual residential parking permit fee of ₹15,000 for hatchbacks, ₹20,000 for sedans, and ₹25,000 for sports utility vehicles (SUVs). The city corporations may also levy an additional administrative fee for issuing the permits, with the amount to be fixed by the GBA Chief Commissioner.

The permit will be issued against a vehicle and the name associated with its registration number. It will be valid for a year and can be renewed annually after verifying that the applicant still lives in the area. The permit will also be valid only on roads designated for residential parking within a walkable distance of the resident’s home. Parking outside the permitted area will also be treated as a violation.

On collector (non-arterial) roads, residential parking will be permitted only if at least six metres of road space remain available for traffic and 1.8 metres of clear walking space are maintained on both sides. On local roads, at least four metres must remain available for traffic, and a 1.8-metre clear footpath must be maintained on at least one side after a vehicle is parked.

Marshals in corporations or other designated employees may verify the validity of permits and report violations to the police. Traffic police will enforce no-parking provisions, including ensuring that only vehicles with valid residential parking permits are allowed in designated residential parking areas. The government has invited objections and suggestions.

The decision has drawn a mixed response. Prajwal Rao, a resident of South Bengaluru, said the rule would place a greater financial burden on people living in rented houses, particularly middle-class families. N.S. Mukunda, founder member of Bengaluru Praja Vedike, said that many citizens would readily pay the amount and obtain permits because it would guarantee them a parking space. However, he said the rule would be difficult to implement in practice and could lead to disputes. “The corporations will have to create off-street parking spaces at a time when there is a severe shortage of vacant land in the city,” he said.

EoM

World.title: Govt. stopped Rythu Bima implementation: BRS
World.content:
HYDERABAD

The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) has accused the Congress government of stopping the implementation of Rythu Bima, group life insurance scheme to landholding farmers, by not paying its premium with vengeance on former Chief Minister K. Chandrasekhar Rao.

In a statement, former minister for agriculture and BRS leader S. Niranjan Reddy said on Thursday that the last date for payment of premium for Rythu Bima scheme was August 15 for its continuation, but there is no move to pay the premium. He stated that a total of 21,099 farmers’ families benefited with the scheme as a total of ₹5,909.85 crore claims were paid at the rate of ₹5 lakh per insured farmer who died, irrespective of the cause.

He alleged that the government has made up its mind to discontinue Rythu Bima in the name of Intintiki Indiram Bima, though no guidelines have been issued so far for its implementation after announcing to implement it from June 2 this year and issuing newspaper and television s by spending crores of rupees.

Mr. Niranjan Reddy mentioned that there were instances of several landless families purchasing farm land to benefit from Rythu Bima scheme.

World.title: ‘Dial Your CMD’ resolves 1,046 grievances in 6 months, says APEPDCL Chief
World.content:
VISAKHAPATNAM

The ‘Dial Your APEPDCL CMD’ initiative has received a overwhelmingly positive response, with 1,046 of the 1,087 grievances received over the past six months being resolved, said A.P. Eastern Power Distribution Company Limited (APEPDCL) chairman and managing director Prudhvitej Immadi on Thursday.

In a statement, Mr. Prudhvitej said that the discom operates on a “Listen, Respond, and Resolve” framework to address consumer issues across 11 districts.

Since its launch on February 9, 2026, the direct line (8688400499)—operating alongside the 24x7 helpline 1912—has enabled high-level intervention for long-pending field issues. Most voltage and supply issues are resolved within 15 days, while metering and billing queries take two to three days.

Rather than merely closing complaints, the utility executed ₹7.47 crore worth of infrastructure projects based on feedback. Key works included installing 211 distribution transformers (DTRs), erecting 508 electric poles, strengthening 55.27 km of power lines, and laying 2,590 metres of cables.

Mr. Prudhvitej added that that the ground-level infrastructure upgrades based on public feedback have boosted public trust and improved overall perception of the discom’s services.

World.title: Yadgar-i-Fatah monument inaugurated in Islamabad on eve of Independence Day
World.content:
The Yadgar-i-Fatah monument, built to honour Pakistan’s martyrs and commemorate Marka-i-Haq, was inaugurated by President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad on Thursday night, on the eve of the country’s 80th Independence Day.
